sources.note: S0507's four-way multi-agent review (Principal Architect / Perplexity / ChatGPT / Kimi) of the 'bounded, dynamic knowledge' conceptual model: introduces Proposition-vs-Assertion, a Conceptual Separation Matrix method, ~18 non-collapsible distinctions, ten candidate invariants (incl. 'no epistemic upgrade by transformation'), dynamic Karaka roles, tacit knowledge, scale as a dimension, and the closing methodological principle 'a lens may generate a distinction/question/test, never impose its own ontology on KnowledgeOS.'

rows.anchor: H1 — Representation ... representation ≠ reality; representation ≠ knowledge.
rows.statement: H1: knowledge may be represented through language and other formal/structured representations (Reality->Observation/Interpretation->Representation->Proposition/Model), but representation is neither reality nor knowledge itself.

rows.anchor: H2 — Knowledge is not a document. A document is an artifact that can contain, express, reference, constrain, or evidence knowledge. It is not itself necessarily knowledge.
rows.statement: H2: a document is an artifact that can contain/express/reference/constrain/evidence knowledge without itself being knowledge; a Constitution may have authority to define a rule while an observation has authority to establish an observed fact -- different authority dimensions.

rows.anchor: H3 — Knowledge is dynamic ... K(P,t,c,E) ... I would not yet make this mathematical expression part of the kernel. It is a modelling lens.
rows.statement: H3: knowledge state may change as observations/evidence/interpretations/context/time change, tentatively K(P,t,c,E) (proposition, temporal state, context, evidence), explicitly held back as a modelling lens, not yet kernel-level.

rows.anchor: H4 — Knowledge space is potentially unbounded ... KnowledgeOS governs bounded portions of an effectively unbounded knowledge space.
rows.statement: H4: knowledge can expand through breadth, depth, connections, abstraction, and specialization with no obvious finite 'KnowledgeOS universe'; KnowledgeOS governs bounded portions of an effectively unbounded knowledge space.

rows.anchor: H5 — Knowledge domains require boundaries ... A topic is potentially informal. A domain has a governed boundary. ... H6 — Boundaries are not walls ... boundary crossing as a first-class relationship.
rows.statement: H5: a knowledge domain requires a declared scope within which concepts/claims/relationships/responsibilities are meaningful (distinguishing informal 'topic' from governed 'domain'); H6 corrects 'boundary' from meaning 'outside = inaccessible' to determining what belongs/does-not-belong/is-externally-referenced/is-dependent, making boundary crossing a first-class relationship.

rows.anchor: H7 — The Kernel validates admissibility, not truth ... Boundary validation / Epistemic validation / Authority validation / Temporal validation ... These must remain separate.
rows.statement: H7: the Kernel should answer 'is this representation admissible within this knowledge boundary?', not 'is this statement true?', separating boundary validation, epistemic validation, authority validation, and temporal validation as four distinct, non-collapsible questions.
invariants: boundary validation, epistemic validation, authority validation, and temporal validation must remain separate

rows.anchor: H8 — Knowledge has expressive capacity ... A domain is partly defined by what it can meaningfully express. ... H9 — Vocabulary is not the boundary ... Lexical boundary ≠ Conceptual boundary ≠ Relational boundary ≠ Propositional boundary.
rows.statement: H8: a domain's expressive capacity is vocabulary+concepts+types+relations+constraints+permissible propositions+abstractions+context, generalizing a prior 'subset of words and sentences' idea. H9 corrects the assumption that knowing every word in a sentence makes it valid in a domain: a valid relationship (e.g. voter--submits-->ballot) is also required, distinguishing lexical, conceptual, relational, and propositional boundaries as four non-identical things -- called probably the most important thing missing from the original model.
invariants: lexical boundary ≠ conceptual boundary ≠ relational boundary ≠ propositional boundary

rows.anchor: H10 — Knowledge has structure ... CLAIM: subject, predicate, object, context, temporal validity, provenance, epistemic state, relationships ... a modelling candidate, not yet a prescribed aggregate.
rows.statement: H10: knowledge is not merely words+sentences but Concept+Relation+State+Context+Time+Evidence, sketching a candidate CLAIM unit (subject, predicate, object, context, temporal validity, provenance, epistemic state, relationships), explicitly not yet a prescribed aggregate.
missing: decision on whether CLAIM is the fundamental aggregate (explicitly deferred, see 'biggest thing not decided yet')

rows.anchor: Missing Dimension 1 — Identity ... What gives a knowledge object stable identity? ... Missing Dimension 2 — Context ... What dimensions constitute context? ... Missing Dimension 3 — Time ... observed_at, asserted_at, valid_from, valid_until, verified_at ... should not automatically collapse into one timestamp.
rows.statement: Missing Dimensions 1-3: (1) Identity -- without stable identity ('Payment Service' vs PaymentService:v1/v2/Production/Development) a proposition may be syntactically valid but unanchorable; (2) Context -- the same sentence (e.g. 'the system allows voting') can mean a constitutional rule, software capability, current runtime state, historical behavior, or future requirement depending on domain/environment/role/jurisdiction/purpose/scenario/time; (3) Time -- observed_at, asserted_at, valid_from, valid_until, and verified_at must not automatically collapse into one timestamp.
invariants: observed_at, asserted_at, valid_from, valid_until, verified_at are distinct and must not collapse

rows.anchor: Missing Dimension 4 — Provenance ... Can every knowledge claim trace its lineage back to its originating observations or assertions? ... Missing Dimension 5 — Epistemic status ... "This statement exists" is not equivalent to "we know this statement to be true." ... Missing Dimension 6 — Authority ... semantic admissibility ≠ epistemic validity ≠ authority.
rows.statement: Missing Dimensions 4-6: (4) Provenance -- knowledge origin (human assertion, source code, runtime observation, document, experiment, inference, another claim) plus derivation kind (direct/derived/transformed/aggregated/generated), posing the question of whether every claim can trace lineage back to originating observations, especially important for AI-generated knowledge; (5) Epistemic status -- observed/asserted/hypothesized/inferred/supported/verified/contradicted/unknown/obsolete, since a statement's existence is not equivalent to its being known true; (6) Authority -- who may define a concept/boundary/rule/fact/classification/decision, keeping semantic admissibility, epistemic validity, and authority strictly separate.

rows.anchor: Missing Dimension 7 — Lifecycle ... verified + superseded is perfectly possible. A verified statement can become obsolete without ever becoming false. ... Missing Dimension 8 — Contradiction and plurality ... the Kernel should probably preserve epistemic plurality rather than prematurely collapse it. ... Missing Dimension 9 — Questions ... a knowledge system should know what it does not know. ... Missing Dimension 10 — Purpose ... Relevance is contextual and purposive.
rows.statement: Missing Dimensions 7-10: (7) Lifecycle (candidate->proposed->accepted->verified->active->superseded->retired) is a distinct dimension from epistemic state -- 'verified + superseded' is coherent, a verified statement can become obsolete without becoming false; (8) Contradiction/plurality -- conflicting claims (Service uses Kafka / Service does not use Kafka) must be preserved with who-claimed-what/when/context/evidence rather than prematurely resolved, connecting to the multi-valued-logic research; (9) Questions -- knowledge includes unresolved status (e.g. 'does the Voting Context enforce device continuity?' = unresolved), giving a Knowledge Space of known/unknown/disputed/uncertain/unexplored, important for the statistical/inverse approach; (10) Purpose -- the same fact has different relevance depending on task (architecture review, security audit, implementation, governance, legal dispute, AI agent task), so relevance is contextual and purposive, important for bounded knowledge delivery to AI agents.
invariants: lifecycle and epistemic state are different dimensions

rows.anchor: I would therefore redraw the model ... Not as a hierarchy, but as orthogonal dimensions around a claim: SEMANTICS / EPISTEMICS / CONTEXT / TIME / AUTHORITY / LIFECYCLE / BOUNDARY-SCOPE.
rows.statement: Redraws the conceptual model as seven orthogonal dimensions clustered around a CLAIM (Semantics: vocabulary/concepts/relations/meaning; Epistemics: evidence/confidence/provenance/uncertainty; Context: domain/purpose/scenario/audience; Time: validity/observation/supersession/verification; Authority: ownership/jurisdiction/decision-rights/governance; Lifecycle: proposed/active/superseded/retired), all nested inside a Boundary/Scope with Internal/External sub-division.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel preserves and validates the structural integrity of bounded knowledge representations while keeping semantic, epistemic, temporal, authority, and lifecycle dimensions distinct. ... I would not yet decide that a "claim" is the fundamental KnowledgeOS aggregate.
rows.statement: Redefines the Kernel's role away from 'the thing that verifies knowledge' toward preserving/validating structural integrity of bounded knowledge representations while keeping semantic/epistemic/temporal/authority/lifecycle dimensions distinct, delegating evidence/verification/governance/temporal/evaluation to specialized mechanisms; explicitly declines to decide yet whether the fundamental KnowledgeOS aggregate is a claim, proposition, knowledge assertion, state of affairs, or a combination.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Conceptual Model Discovery Questions ... A. Ontology ... B. Boundary ... C. Dynamics ... D. Epistemology ... E. Authority ... F. Representation ... G. Quantification ... H. AI
rows.statement: Poses 42 numbered discovery questions across eight categories (Ontology, Boundary, Dynamics, Epistemology, Authority, Representation, Quantification, AI), e.g. 'what is the smallest thing that can meaningfully be knowledge?', 'can two domains legitimately overlap?', 'can knowledge be superseded without becoming false?', 'can KnowledgeOS represent we don't know?', 'is an LLM-generated sentence knowledge?', 'what exactly are we trying to quantify?' (listing amount of information/uncertainty/coverage/depth/breadth/consistency/confidence/evidence strength/completeness/expressive capacity as distinct candidate quantities), and 'what does an AI agent actually receive from KnowledgeOS?'

rows.anchor: Is knowledge fundamentally a property of a statement, or a property of a relationship between a statement and reality under a context? ... My architectural intuition is strongly toward Model B, but I would not make it a decision yet.
rows.statement: Poses the file's most fundamental open question -- is knowledge a property of a statement (Model A: Knowledge->Statement) or a relationship between representation, reality, evidence, and context (Model B: Representation<->Evidence, both under Context, correspondence to Reality, yielding Knowledge State)? -- leaning toward Model B as an architectural intuition without yet deciding, proposing to freeze the whole review as a conceptual hypothesis and run it through thirteen accumulated lenses (Vani, Paninian, Karaka, Pramana, Wittgenstein, Shannon, Topological, Statistical, Shani, Ganesha, Leonardo, Krishna, Governance) asking 'what is the minimum ontology that survives all lenses without mixing dimensions?'

rows.anchor: Representation ≠ Proposition ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge state ... KS = <p, r, c, τ, e, a, λ, σ> ... a descriptive tuple, not yet a domain object or aggregate.
rows.statement: Perplexity's review agrees KnowledgeOS should not implement a 'knowledge' aggregate or universal truth-verification kernel yet, formalizing Representation != Proposition != Evidence != Knowledge state, and proposing a provisional descriptive (not aggregate) tuple KS=<p,r,c,tau,e,a,lambda,sigma> (proposition, representation, context, time, evidence, authority, lifecycle, epistemic status).

rows.anchor: verified + superseded ... authoritative + historically invalid ... structurally admissible + epistemically unsupported ... semantically valid + contextually inapplicable ... disputed + highly evidenced ... are all coherent combinations.
rows.statement: Tabulates twelve knowledge dimensions (semantics, ontology, representation, context, epistemics, evidence, provenance, authority, time, boundary, lifecycle, purpose), each with a core question and example, and gives five coherent cross-dimensional combinations that a single collapsed status field would wrongly forbid.

rows.anchor: Proposed minimum conceptual ontology: 1. Semantic object ... 2. Representation ... 3. Assertion ... A1(p,c1,t1,a1), A2(p,c2,t2,a2) ... 4. Evidence ... 5. Context ... 6. Boundary ... 7. Knowledge state ... a derived view.
rows.statement: Proposes seven minimum-ontology candidates: Semantic object (concept/relation/type/proposition/rule/question/model, interpretable independently of representation); Representation (document/source file/diagram/dataset/event/observation record/embedding/generated text, carrying provenance but not automatically inheriting epistemic status); Assertion (a contextual act of presenting a proposition, formalized as A1(p,c1,t1,a1) and A2(p,c2,t2,a2) where the same proposition p may have differing contexts/times/authorities); Evidence (typed and directional: supports/contradicts/qualifies/derives/contextualizes/supersedes); Context (domain/jurisdiction/environment/scenario/actor-role/audience/purpose/temporal frame/version, not one opaque value); Boundary (a set of constraints on vocabulary/concept membership/permitted relations/proposition forms/authority/external references/dependency direction/ownership/context applicability); Knowledge state (a derived view over the other six, avoiding treating 'knowledge' as a too-early primitive).

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Kernel preserves identity, provenance, structural integrity, boundary conformance, and cross-dimensional consistency for governed knowledge representations. It does not independently establish truth. ... Non-kernel responsibilities: evidential strength; reproducibility; truth or falsity; ... agent-specific retrieval.
rows.statement: Sharpens the Kernel boundary: the Kernel validates identity uniqueness/reference integrity, representation-to-semantic-object linkage, well-formed subject/predicate/object, permitted relation types, boundary membership/crossings, context completeness, temporal interval consistency, provenance graph integrity, authority compatibility, lifecycle transition legality, preservation of contradictory assertions, and immutable historical records; explicitly excludes evidential strength, reproducibility, truth/falsity, legal legitimacy, confidence, relevance, inference, statistical uncertainty, and agent-specific retrieval as non-kernel (specialized-service) responsibilities -- important for AI-generated content that may be structurally admissible yet unverified.

rows.anchor: 1. Representation independence ... 2. Assertion multiplicity ... 3. Status orthogonality ... 4. Contradiction preservation ... 5. Boundary explicitness ... 6. Temporal distinction ... 7. Provenance closure ... 8. Authority specificity ... 9. Unknown as first-class state ... 10. No epistemic upgrade by transformation.
rows.statement: Defines ten candidate core invariants: (1) multiple representations may express one semantic object and vice versa; (2) the same proposition may be asserted by multiple authorities in different contexts/times; (3) epistemic status, lifecycle status, authority, and temporal validity must not collapse into one state machine; (4) contradictory assertions must be representable without automatic destructive resolution; (5) cross-boundary references must be explicit/typed/traceable; (6) assertion/observation/validity/verification/supersession time must remain distinguishable; (7) derived/transformed representations must retain links to immediate inputs and transformation activities; (8) authority must be scoped to the kind of act performed (defining/asserting/verifying/classifying/governing); (9) an unresolved question/knowledge gap must be representable without becoming a false proposition; (10) extraction/summarization/embedding/generation must not automatically increase epistemic status.

rows.anchor: A proposition is semantic content ... An assertion adds situated metadata: who asserted it; under which domain and purpose; at what time; with what authority; based on what evidence; with what epistemic status; for which validity interval. ... Proposition and Assertion should remain separate candidates during discovery.
rows.statement: Names 'the most productive refinement' of the review: Proposition (semantic content, e.g. 'the Voting Context enforces device continuity') versus Assertion (that proposition situated by who asserted it, domain/purpose, time, authority, evidence, epistemic status, validity interval), enabling representation of the same proposition asserted by different parties, conflicting assertions, a stable proposition whose validity changes, a superseded historical assertion, and a question whose proposition is not yet established.

rows.anchor: Research protocol for the next round ... Vāṇī | Can representation be separated from meaning and speech act? ... The output of each lens should be one of: candidate concept; candidate relationship; candidate invariant; unresolved ambiguity; rejected conflation; question requiring empirical validation.
rows.statement: Proposes turning the twelve accumulated lenses into a traceable discovery protocol, each with a specific test (e.g. Wittgenstein: can propositions/states-of-affairs/logical boundaries be separated?; Shannon: can uncertainty/noise/redundancy/transmission be modeled without equating information with knowledge?), with each lens output classified as a candidate concept, candidate relationship, candidate invariant, unresolved ambiguity, rejected conflation, or a question requiring empirical validation.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Conceptual Separation Matrix with rows for candidate concepts and columns for the orthogonal dimensions ... The matrix makes category errors visible before they enter the kernel.
rows.statement: Proposes a Conceptual Separation Matrix (rows: Proposition, Document, Assertion, Observation, Question, Rule, Knowledge state; columns: semantic identity, representation, evidence, authority, time, epistemic status, lifecycle) with a worked example table, described as making category errors visible before they enter the kernel; final provisional formulation states KnowledgeOS governs bounded, contextualized, time-sensitive representations/assertions whose semantic/evidential/epistemic/authoritative/lifecycle dimensions remain distinguishable, restating the unresolved 'statement vs relation-under-context' question and leaning toward the relational (Model B) answer as architecturally safer.

rows.anchor: P = "Voting requires device continuity." ... A1: asserted by Architecture ... A2: asserted by Constitution ... A3: asserted by developer ... Same proposition. Different assertions.
rows.statement: ChatGPT's review endorses Perplexity's Proposition/Assertion split as particularly valuable, illustrating one proposition P with three differing assertions A1 (Architecture, 2026, source-code evidence), A2 (Constitution, 2025, Governance authority), A3 (developer, proposed implementation, no evidence).
dependencies: Proposition vs Assertion distinction (Perplexity, same file)

rows.anchor: We must not create something like: KnowledgeStatus = proposed | verified | approved | obsolete, because that would collapse fundamentally different dimensions.
rows.statement: Endorses the orthogonality principle (verified+superseded, authoritative+historically-invalid, etc. are all legitimate combinations), explicitly forbidding a single collapsed enum KnowledgeStatus={proposed,verified,approved,obsolete}, structuring an Assertion instead around semantic/epistemic/authority/context/time/lifecycle branches converging into one state.

rows.anchor: Don't call this Knowledge State yet. That name already assumes we have defined what knowledge is. ... I would call it something like: Epistemic Situation Model or simply: Knowledge Candidate Model.
rows.statement: Objects to naming Perplexity's KS tuple 'Knowledge State' since that name presupposes an unresolved definition of knowledge, proposing 'Epistemic Situation Model' or 'Knowledge Candidate Model' as neutral placeholder names until ontology discovery is complete.

rows.anchor: The biggest thing I would add: Observation. ... I would not let Observation = Evidence silently happen. ... An observation may become evidence depending on its relationship to a question/assertion.
rows.statement: Argues Perplexity's model omits Observation, which the project's existing architecture (Observation->Evidence->Evaluation->Legitimacy->Governance) already treats distinctly; warns against silently equating Observation with Evidence, proposing instead that Observation/Document/Source-code all feed into Evidence which feeds Assertion, with the exact ordering flagged as needing investigation.
missing: resolution of the ordering investigation

rows.anchor: Another missing concept: Question. ... your entire inverse-statistical idea becomes much more interesting if KnowledgeOS models not just what do we know? but what are we trying to determine?
rows.statement: Proposes elevating Question (already present as a semantic-object subtype in Perplexity's model) to first-class status, modeling Question->candidate propositions->available evidence->uncertainty->knowledge state, suggesting Question may be more fundamental to knowledge discovery than Knowledge State itself, connecting to the inverse-statistical research direction.
dependencies: inverse-statistical methods idea (S0498, S0504, S0505, S0506)

rows.anchor: Semantic boundary ... Responsibility boundary ... Authority boundary ... Knowledge boundary ... dependency does not imply ownership. That needs to become an invariant.
rows.statement: Distinguishes four boundary types -- semantic (what concepts/relationships belong), responsibility (what questions the domain must answer), authority (what it may legitimately decide), knowledge (what claims are currently part of its governed knowledge) -- illustrated by the Voting Context being responsible for voter verification/ballot submission/vote recording while depending on Identity/Cryptography/Infrastructure without owning them, proposing 'dependency does not imply ownership' as a candidate invariant.

rows.anchor: scope of responsibility ... responsible_for: ballot_submission ... depends_on: Identity, Cryptography ... does_not_own: identity_verification_policy, cryptographic_algorithm_design ... Now the boundary becomes operational rather than merely lexical.
rows.statement: Proposes 'scope of responsibility' as a possible missing bridge between DDD bounded contexts and the KnowledgeOS domain model: a domain declares what it is responsible_for, what it depends_on, and what it does_not_own (worked YAML example for the Voting domain), making the boundary operational rather than merely lexical.

rows.anchor: SEMANTIC PRIMITIVES: entity/concept, type, relation ... SEMANTIC STRUCTURES: proposition, rule, question, model ... worth testing through the Pāṇinian and Kāraka lenses.
rows.statement: Corrects Perplexity's flat 'Semantic Object' grouping (concept/relation/type/proposition/rule/question/model at one level) by splitting it into Semantic Primitives (entity/concept, type, relation) and Semantic Structures (proposition, rule, question, model) built from those primitives, proposed for testing via the Paninian and Karaka lenses.

lineage_claims.quote: Perplexity's 'Semantic Object' needs more scrutiny ... I would not yet put all of these at the same level.

rows.anchor: I would promote this immediately to a candidate KnowledgeOS constitutional invariant. ... Transformation preserves or potentially loses epistemic status; it cannot create authority merely by transformation.
rows.statement: Promotes 'no epistemic upgrade by transformation' to candidate constitutional-invariant status: a chain of Original observation -> LLM extraction -> summary -> embedding -> generated explanation must never increase confidence/authority/truth merely because transformations happened; any legitimate increase in evidentiary status must come from a new, independent epistemic act, not from the transformation itself.
dependencies: no epistemic upgrade by transformation invariant (Perplexity, same file)
invariants: transformation cannot create authority merely by occurring

rows.anchor: I think we need provenance lineage, not merely provenance metadata. ... Observation O1 -> Extraction E1 -> Proposition P1 -> Assertion A1 -> Evaluation V1 -> Knowledge State K1. ... essential if KnowledgeOS is going to support replay, audit and independent verification.
rows.statement: Strengthens Perplexity's provenance-closure invariant into a full traceable provenance lineage chain (Observation->Extraction->Proposition->Assertion->Evaluation->Knowledge State, each step reverse-traceable to its predecessor), argued to be essential for replay, audit, and independent verification.

rows.anchor: The Kernel should not become an epistemology engine by accumulation. ... otherwise KnowledgeOS Kernel slowly becomes EverythingOS.
rows.statement: Adds a constraint to the Kernel-boundary definition: the Kernel must not gradually absorb truth/confidence/relevance/inference/statistical-uncertainty/semantic-interpretation responsibilities simply because they need validation somewhere -- those belong to specialized mechanisms, or the Kernel becomes 'EverythingOS', the architectural failure to avoid.

rows.anchor: A semantic relationship crossing a domain boundary must not implicitly transfer ownership or membership across that boundary. ... important for preventing semantic scope pollution.
rows.statement: Adds the invariant 'no boundary inference by convenience': seeing Kafka referenced inside Payment must not automatically make the system decide Kafka belongs to the Payment domain; instead Payment must explicitly declare depends_on->Messaging->Kafka, preventing semantic scope pollution.
invariants: a boundary-crossing relationship must not implicitly transfer ownership or membership

rows.anchor: Representation multiplicity ... rather than Document = knowledge object. This is essential for AI.
rows.statement: Endorses and restates Perplexity's representation-independence invariant as 'representation multiplicity': a semantic object can be expressed as Text, Code, or Diagram simultaneously (with Document as one specific text-representation), rather than collapsing Document=knowledge object -- called essential for AI.

rows.anchor: Semantic Object -> {Concept, Relation, Proposition} -> Representation -> {Document, Code, Observation} -> Evidence -> Assertion -> {Context, Authority, Time} -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge State, surrounded by BOUNDARY (vocabulary, concepts, relations, propositions, responsibility, authority, dependencies).
rows.statement: Combines the Perplexity ontology with the project's existing observation/evidence architecture into one diagram: Semantic Object branches into Concept/Relation/Proposition, feeds Representation (Document/Code/Observation), then Evidence, then Assertion (qualified by Context/Authority/Time), then Epistemic State, then Knowledge State, the whole structure enclosed by a Boundary carrying vocabulary/concepts/relations/propositions/responsibility/authority/dependencies.

rows.anchor: Question 1: Is Proposition really the semantic unit we need? ... Question 8: What exactly changes when knowledge changes? This may be the deepest question.
rows.statement: Names eight unresolved foundational questions before calling the combined model an ontology: is Proposition or 'state-of-affairs' the right semantic unit; is Assertion an entity, event, or relationship; is Evidence an object, role, or relationship; is Knowledge State stored or derived (leaning derived); is Boundary itself knowledge (possibly governed semantic metadata); can knowledge exist without assertion; can two contradictory assertions both be valid (leaning yes, with separate contexts/evidence); what exactly changes when knowledge changes (called possibly the deepest question).

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS does not model knowledge as a document, sentence, claim, or static entity. ... The KnowledgeOS Kernel preserves structural integrity and boundary integrity; it does not determine truth. ... No transformation of a representation may implicitly increase its epistemic status, authority, or truth status. ... Knowledge domains are bounded responsibilities within an unbounded connected knowledge space; boundary crossing must be explicit and must not imply ownership transfer.
rows.statement: States four principles as 'the strongest outcome of the comparison': KnowledgeOS models structures/relationships (representation, assertion, evidence, context, boundary, authority, time) rather than treating knowledge as a document/sentence/claim/static entity, with knowledge state as a derived epistemic view; the Kernel preserves structural/boundary integrity without determining truth; no transformation may implicitly increase epistemic status/authority/truth; and knowledge domains are bounded responsibilities within an unbounded connected space where boundary crossing must be explicit and must not imply ownership transfer.

rows.anchor: "This is not ontology design. This is epistemic stress-testing." ... We are asking: Which distinctions survive adversarial examination from independent conceptual lenses? ... Vāṇī: expression vs meaning ... Leonardo: system integration.
rows.statement: Adopts Kimi's reframing of the whole exercise as 'epistemic stress-testing, not ontology design' -- asking which distinctions survive adversarial examination from independent lenses rather than deciding Concept=aggregate/Evidence=entity/Knowledge=object -- and endorses Kimi's twelve-lens test table (Vani: expression vs meaning; Paninian: generative/compositional integrity; Karaka: role/dependency; Pramana: epistemic justification; Wittgenstein: use/context; Shannon: information/transmission; Topological: structural/boundary integrity; Statistical: uncertainty/empirical regularity; Shani: invariant/consequence; Governance: authority/state transition; Krishna: emergence/change; Leonardo: system integration).

rows.anchor: Concept, Type and Knowledge State correspond to Parā ... This is too strong. ... Concept = dhātu; Relation = pratyaya; Document = sphoṭa ... the risky part is treating [these] as literal architectural equivalences.
rows.statement: Rejects Kimi's literal Vani mapping (Concept/Type/KnowledgeState=Para; Relation/Proposition/Observation=Pasyanti; Assertion/Question/Rule=Madhyama; Document/Evidence/Representation=Vaikhari) and literal Paninian mapping (Concept/Type=dhatu; Relation=pratyaya; Proposition/Assertion=vakya; Document=sphota) as turning philosophical lenses into ontological classification; reformulates them as safe tests instead: Vani asks 'at what stages can this candidate exist independently of a particular linguistic expression?'; Paninian asks 'can a representation be generated from structured semantic primitives through explicit transformations, and inverted sufficiently to recover the semantic structure?', explicitly connecting the latter to the project's Dhatu-extraction idea.

rows.anchor: Kāraka roles are semantic rather than syntactic, and the role can change depending on the epistemic frame. ... Evidence should probably be modeled primarily as a role/relationship, not simply as an intrinsic type.
rows.statement: Endorses Kimi's Karaka finding almost fully: an Observation O can be SOURCE in one operation, EVIDENCE in another, INPUT in another, or CONTRADICTING OBSERVATION in another -- the object hasn't changed, its role in a relationship has -- reinforcing the conclusion that Evidence should be modeled primarily as a role/relationship, not an intrinsic type.

rows.anchor: Pramāṇa is factive and a genuine pramāṇa never produces false belief ... We should not encode Pramana = Truth ... Every epistemic status must have an identifiable justification pathway.
rows.statement: Rejects Kimi's overstated pramana factivity claim (Pramana=Truth) as architecturally unsafe since source/method/evidence/inference/verification/truth must remain distinguishable, extracting instead the lesson 'every epistemic status must have an identifiable justification pathway', formalized as ASSERTION carrying justification method, source, evidence, transformation/inference, and verification status.
invariants: every epistemic status must have an identifiable justification pathway

rows.anchor: Kimi says the Wittgenstein lens should introduce a tacit/non-explicit dimension. ... A portion of knowledge can be represented linguistically; linguistic representation does not exhaust the knowledge state.
rows.statement: Adopts Kimi's tacit-knowledge finding as deserving serious investigation, expanding the Knowledge Space into explicit/implicit/tacit/inexpressible-or-currently-unrepresented, directly challenging and reformulating the project's original hypothesis 'knowledge can be expressed in words' into 'a portion of knowledge can be represented linguistically; linguistic representation does not exhaust the knowledge state.'

lineage_claims.target: original hypothesis 'knowledge can be expressed in words'
lineage_claims.quote: That directly challenges your original hypothesis: "Knowledge can be expressed in words." I would now reformulate it

rows.anchor: "Type has high entropy" and "Document has low entropy." I would not accept those statements. Entropy is not an intrinsic property of a semantic category ... Never turn Shannon terminology into architectural metaphors without defining the random variables.
rows.statement: Rejects Kimi's claim that 'Type has high entropy' / 'Document has low entropy' as a category error since entropy requires a defined random variable and probability distribution, not an intrinsic property of a semantic category; proposes the corrected question 'what uncertainty does this representation reduce, under a defined distribution?' (I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)) and states a new methodological rule: never turn Shannon terminology into architectural metaphors without defining the random variables.
invariants: never use Shannon terminology as metaphor without defining the underlying random variables

rows.anchor: Assertion → P(true | evidence) ... Knowledge = probability would be wrong. ... Knowledge State: uncertainty estimate, posterior distribution, confidence interval, evidence coverage, conflict probability.
rows.statement: Accepts Kimi's statistical direction (Assertion->P(true|evidence), Observation->measurement error, Knowledge State->posterior probability) only if the statistical model is defined, but rejects Knowledge=probability, instead treating statistical quantities (uncertainty estimate, posterior distribution, confidence interval, evidence coverage, conflict probability) as measurements of aspects of a Knowledge State rather than its definition.

rows.anchor: boundaries and contexts could be formalized as functors between categories. ... Topological/category-theoretic lens = yes. Functor as architecture = not yet.
rows.statement: Accepts the topological/category-theoretic lens as a research direction but declines to architecturalize Kimi's specific claim that boundaries/contexts are formalizable as functors between categories; the robust extraction is testing boundary crossing, semantic preservation, identity preservation, and relationship preservation directly, deferring the functor question to later research.

rows.anchor: every candidate should have a consequence function: what happens if it is violated, misused, or falsified? ... Candidate | Invariant | Violation | Detection | Consequence | Recovery
rows.statement: Adopts Kimi's 'consequence function' idea, adding a Candidate/Invariant/Violation/Detection/Consequence/Recovery column set to the Conceptual Separation Matrix, illustrated by a Boundary example (invariant: external dependency must be explicit; violation: implicit ownership transfer; detection: boundary consistency test; consequence: semantic contamination; recovery: explicit reclassification).

rows.anchor: Governance is not merely permission; it determines who can move a candidate from one state to another. ... It introduces transition authority.
rows.statement: Adopts Kimi's governance-as-state-transition-authority idea: rather than a static Evidence.owner=X field, governance should specify who is authorized to cause each lifecycle transition (Observation->Evidence->Assertion->Verified), introducing 'transition authority' as more precise than static ownership.

rows.anchor: Kimi interprets Krishna through Līlā, play and non-deterministic generation ... I would translate it into: Can the knowledge model accommodate emergence, exploration, alternative hypotheses, recombination and evolving interpretation without destroying its invariants?
rows.statement: Rejects Kimi's literal Krishna/Lila ('knowledge is divine play') interpretation, retranslating the Krishna lens's engineering test as: can the knowledge model accommodate emergence, alternative hypotheses, exploration, recombination, and evolving interpretation without destroying its invariants -- keeping the lens useful without turning it into ontology.

rows.anchor: Kimi's Leonardo test asks whether the whole matrix remains coherent and whether we have over-specified it. ... Does the model allow ambiguity, or has it become a rigid cage? ... Can the model remain useful without requiring every dimension to be populated?
rows.statement: Retains Kimi's Leonardo test almost unchanged as a coherence/over-specification check, warning against ending up with 15 candidates x 13 questions x 12 lenses x 10 states x 20 invariants producing 'a magnificent taxonomy nobody can use', adding the specific negative test 'can the model remain useful without requiring every dimension to be populated?'

rows.anchor: "Does it bind or liberate?" as an affective Bandha/Mokṣa dimension. I would not add this to the core ontology. ... Kāla, Samaya, Nitya ... I would not immediately adopt those categories literally either. But the underlying architectural question is excellent: what kind of temporal relationship does this knowledge have?
rows.statement: Rejects Kimi's proposed 'bind or liberate' (Bandha/Moksa) affective dimension as insufficiently architecturally justified for the core ontology (relegated to Krishna/philosophical interpretation only); similarly declines to adopt Kimi's Kala/Samaya/Nitya temporal-regime categories literally, but retains the underlying question 'what kind of temporal relationship does this knowledge have?', already partly answered by six named timestamp types (event/observation/assertion/validity/verification/supersession time), adding 'temporal semantics' to the research matrix.
dependencies: Time missing dimension (same file, earlier section)

rows.anchor: Kimi identifies scale as a gap. ... token, sentence, document, concept, domain, system, organization, ecosystem ... "Kafka" at token level is a word. At semantic level it is a technology. At architecture level it is a dependency. ... Knowledge properties may be scale-dependent.
rows.statement: Adopts Kimi's 'scale' as a new first-class research dimension: the same thing looks different at token/sentence/document/concept/domain/system/organization/ecosystem scale, illustrated by 'Kafka' being a word at token level, a technology at semantic level, a dependency at architecture level, an ownership boundary at organizational level, and part of a technology landscape at ecosystem level; concludes knowledge properties may be scale-dependent.

rows.anchor: SEMANTIC STRUCTURE + SCOPE&CONTEXT -> REPRESENTATION -> OBSERVATION -> ASSERTION -> {Evidence, Inference, Question} -> EPISTEMIC STATE -> KNOWLEDGE STATE (DERIVED), orthogonal to TIME/AUTHORITY/PROVENANCE/BOUNDARY/PURPOSE/SCALE/UNCERTAINTY/LIFECYCLE, with relationships represents/asserts/supports/contradicts/derives/verifies/authorizes/depends-on/contextualizes/supersedes/crosses-boundary.
rows.statement: Merges the original model, Perplexity's, and Kimi's contributions into one combined diagram (Semantic Structure/Concept/Relation/Proposition + Scope&Context -> Representation (Document/Code/Dataset) -> Observation -> Assertion -> {Evidence, Inference, Question} -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge State (derived)), with eight orthogonal dimensions (Time, Authority, Provenance, Boundary, Purpose, Scale, Uncertainty, Lifecycle) and eleven named relationship types (represents, asserts, supports, contradicts, derives, verifies, authorizes, depends-on, contextualizes, supersedes, crosses-boundary).
dependencies: all three prior sub-reviews (Architect, Perplexity, ChatGPT) in the same file

rows.anchor: Representation ≠ Meaning ... Document ≠ Knowledge ... Observation ≠ Fact ... Observation ≠ Evidence ... Proposition ≠ Assertion ... Assertion ≠ Truth ... Evidence ≠ Truth ... Evidence ≠ Verification ... Authority ≠ Credibility ... Authority ≠ Truth ... Validity ≠ Verification ... Lifecycle ≠ Epistemic Status ... Boundary ≠ Vocabulary ... Context ≠ Purpose ... Information ≠ Knowledge ... Inference ≠ Observation ... Knowledge State ≠ Knowledge Object ... These are becoming more important than our positive ontology.
rows.statement: Compiles the file's cumulative negative result: an eighteen-item list of distinctions that 'must not be collapsed' (Representation≠Meaning≠Referent, Document≠Knowledge, Observation≠Fact≠Evidence, Proposition≠Assertion≠Truth, Evidence≠Truth≠Verification, Authority≠Credibility≠Truth, Validity≠Verification, Lifecycle≠Epistemic Status, Boundary≠Vocabulary, Context≠Purpose, Information≠Knowledge, Inference≠Observation, Knowledge State≠Knowledge Object), explicitly stated to be becoming more important than the file's positive ontology proposals.
dependencies: every non-collapse claim made earlier in this file

rows.anchor: K = {C,U,E,P,S,B,T,X,Q,...} ... Knowledge may be better represented as a multidimensional state vector than as a scalar quantity.

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: Yet another cumulative multidimensional knowledge-state formalization, alongside the many tuples proposed across S0495-S0506; no file in the series reconciles them.

rows.statement: Stops asking for a single Knowledge Score, proposing instead a state-vector hypothesis K={C,U,E,P,S,B,T,X,Q,...} (coverage, uncertainty, evidence strength, provenance completeness, semantic connectivity, boundary stability, temporal stability, contradiction/conflict, unresolved questions), explicitly not a mathematical definition yet but a research hypothesis feeding the project's statistical/ML direction.
missing: formal definitions of each component

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Epistemic Stress-Test — Round 1 ... For every candidate, ask five fundamental questions ... Then add four questions I think we now need: at what scale does it exist? what is its temporal semantics? what happens if it is wrong or violated? can its epistemic state be independently reconstructed?
rows.statement: Defines 'KnowledgeOS Epistemic Stress-Test -- Round 1': fifteen candidate concepts run through twelve lens filters (Vani, Paninian, Karaka, Pramana, Wittgenstein, Shannon, Topology, Statistics, Shani, Governance, Krishna, Leonardo), each answering five original questions (what is it? what does it depend on? what can happen to it? what can relate to it? who can act on it?) plus four newly added questions (at what scale does it exist? what is its temporal semantics? what happens if it is wrong/violated? can its epistemic state be independently reconstructed?).

rows.anchor: Keep: the lens-as-filter concept; dynamic Kāraka roles; inverse semantic transformation; ... Do not freeze yet: Parā/Paśyantī/Madhyamā/Vaikharī as ontology categories; dhātu = Concept; ... A lens is allowed to generate a distinction, a question, or a falsification test. It is not allowed to impose its own ontology on KnowledgeOS.
rows.statement: Closes with a final Kimi assessment split into a keep-list (lens-as-filter, dynamic Karaka roles, inverse semantic transformation, epistemic justification pathways, tacit/explicit distinction, governance-as-transition-authority, consequence functions, scale, temporal semantics, counterexample-driven stress testing) and a do-not-freeze-yet list (Para/Pasyanti/Madhyama/Vaikhari as ontology; dhatu=Concept; pratyaya=Relation; document=sphota; categories-as-functors; intrinsic entropy on semantic candidates; bind/liberate as core dimension; Krishna/Lila as literal knowledge property), stating the resulting methodological principle: 'a lens is allowed to generate a distinction, a question, or a falsification test. It is not allowed to impose its own ontology on KnowledgeOS' -- protecting the research program from becoming Sanskrit/category-theoretic/statistical/LLM ontology.
invariants: a lens may generate a distinction/question/test; it may not impose its own ontology on KnowledgeOS

rows.anchor: Truth, falsity, coherence, relevance, and answer-completeness should not be properties of a word or sentence alone. They are evaluations of a statement/question within a context and against some evidence or knowledge state.
rows.statement: States the file's central architectural distinction and models it as a PlantUML class diagram: a Knowledge Space with Semantic Layer (Topic/Concept/Relation/Proposition/Fact), Representation Layer (Word/Phrase/Sentence/Document), Epistemic Layer (Assertion/Evidence/Observation/Inference), Question Layer (ten question subclasses: What/Who/Which/When/Where/Why/How/HowMany/HowMuch/YesNo), and Evaluation Layer (TruthAssessment/CoherenceAssessment/RelevanceAssessment/AnswerabilityAssessment/CompletenessAssessment/ContradictionAssessment, plus a TruthValue enum {TRUE,FALSE,UNKNOWN,BOTH,NEITHER}), with explicit notes that a word is a representation not meaning, a sentence's semantic interpretation corresponds to (not equals) a proposition, and truth is an assessment of a proposition against evidence/knowledge-state under a defined epistemic regime, not an intrinsic property of a sentence.
invariants: truth/coherence/relevance/completeness are evaluations, not intrinsic linguistic properties

rows.anchor: A question can be: ANSWERABLE, PARTIALLY ANSWERABLE, UNDERDETERMINED, UNANSWERABLE — independently of whether a candidate answer is true or false. ... An answer can be true but incomplete.
rows.statement: Notes on the initial model distinguish answerability (answerable/partially answerable/underdetermined/unanswerable) from truth of a candidate answer, and completeness from truth, illustrated by 'why did X happen?' answered truly but incompletely by 'because A' when B and C are also required.

rows.anchor: I would not model these merely as words. They are question operators. ... A question becomes a structured request against the Knowledge Space.
rows.statement: Elevates what/who/which/when/where/why/how/how-many/how-much/whether/whose/what-if/how-likely from mere words into thirteen 'question operators' each seeking a distinct kind of information, illustrated by 'why did the election result change?' (operator WHY, target ElectionResult, desired relation CAUSAL, temporal scope, context, required causal-explanation answer) versus 'when did the election result change?' (operator WHEN, desired relation TEMPORAL) as the same topic producing a structurally different epistemic query.

rows.anchor: True ... False ... Meaningless / ill-formed ... Incoherent ... Underdetermined ... Irrelevant ... Incomplete ... Ambiguous ... E = (S,T,C,R,A,K,U)
rows.statement: Distinguishes eight independent answer-quality failure modes (true, false, meaningless/ill-formed, incoherent, underdetermined, irrelevant, incomplete, ambiguous), formalizing an evaluation vector E=(S,T,C,R,A,K,U) (semantic well-formedness, truth status, coherence, relevance, answerability, completeness, uncertainty), proposed as much better than a binary answer=true/false and named an 'Epistemic Answer Vector'/'Knowledge Assessment Vector', framed as a way to quantify knowledge state without treating knowledge as one number.

rows.anchor: the PlantUML model currently crosses too many bounded contexts ... semantic modeling; linguistic representation; observation and evidence; inquiry and answering; epistemic evaluation; governance and contextual scope. In DDD terms, this is not one coherent domain model. It is a conceptual map across several bounded contexts.
rows.statement: Argues the PlantUML model combines six different domains (semantic modeling, linguistic representation, observation/evidence, inquiry/answering, epistemic evaluation, governance/contextual scope) into one apparent aggregate, when it is really a conceptual map across several bounded contexts; proposes KnowledgeOS be modeled as a federation of bounded contexts connected through explicit published language, translation rules, provenance links, and anti-corruption layers, citing PROV (entities/activities/agents/derivations/responsibility, not one 'source' attribute) and SHACL (structural graph validation, not truth determination) as established precedent.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeState should not own everything. ... KS = Project(A, E, C, τ, P) ... a derived domain concept rather than a universal container.
rows.statement: Corrects KnowledgeState from an aggregate owning Topic/Concept/Proposition (via composition) to a read model/projection selecting assertions, evidence, temporal scope, context/boundary, and epistemic policy, formalized as KS=Project(A,E,C,tau,P) (assertions, evidence/provenance, context, temporal scope, projection policy/purpose).
missing: definition of Project()

lineage_claims.target: KnowledgeState "1" o-- "*" Topic composition in the original PlantUML model (same file)
lineage_claims.quote: KnowledgeState should not own everything ... This is too strong.

rows.anchor: Fact should not be a primitive entity yet. A fact may mean at least four different things: a state of affairs in reality; a proposition accepted as true; an observed event; a database record labeled "fact." ... StateOfAffairs, ObservationRecord, AcceptedAssertion, FactClaim.
rows.statement: Warns the model's Proposition->Fact relationship risks reintroducing the exact conflation the architecture aims to avoid, since 'Fact' can mean a state of affairs, an accepted-true proposition, an observed event, or a database record; proposes temporarily replacing Fact with StateOfAffairs/ObservationRecord/AcceptedAssertion/FactClaim and investigating whether Fact is needed at all, with a safer relationship chain ObservationRecord--observes-->StateOfAffairs, Assertion--asserts-->Proposition, Evidence--supports-->Assertion, Assessment--evaluates-->Assertion.

rows.anchor: Evidence is not primarily an object type ... support an assertion; challenge; qualify; establish provenance; justify an inference; establish authority; indicate absence; demonstrate reproducibility. ... EvidenceRelation: source, target assertion, role, method, strength, evaluatedAt, provenance. strength should not be an intrinsic scalar on Evidence.
rows.statement: Corrects Evidence from a simple 'supports a proposition' object into an eight-role relational concept (support/challenge/qualify/establish provenance/justify inference/establish authority/indicate absence/demonstrate reproducibility) directed at an Assertion (not only a Proposition), formalized as EvidenceRelation{source, target assertion, role, method, strength, evaluatedAt, provenance}, with strength explicitly not an intrinsic scalar on Evidence since the same proposition may be supported by one source and challenged by another.
invariants: evidence strength is not intrinsic to Evidence; it depends on assertion, method, domain, and evaluation regime

rows.anchor: Observation should be an event or record, not a fact ... observer; instrument or method; observed subject; time; location or context; procedure; recorded result; uncertainty; provenance. ... ObservationEvent ... produces ObservationRecord. The record is not identical to the state of affairs observed.
rows.statement: Corrects Observation from a simple 'observes a Fact' relation into an ObservationEvent (observer, method/instrument, observed subject, time, location/context, procedure, recorded result, uncertainty, provenance) that produces an ObservationRecord distinct from the state of affairs observed, citing PROV's activity/entity/agent model as precedent.
invariants: an observation record is not identical to the state of affairs observed

rows.anchor: Semantic Modeling Context ... Representation Context ... Assertion and Evidence Context ... Inquiry Context ... Assessment Context ... each with a stated responsibility question and a candidate aggregate.
rows.statement: Proposes five bounded contexts each with an owning responsibility question and a candidate aggregate: Semantic Modeling ('is this structure well-formed and meaningful?', SemanticModel), Representation ('what representation exists, how produced, what interpretation does it propose?', with Representation--interpretedAs-->Interpretation--proposes-->Proposition replacing a direct Sentence->Proposition link), Assertion and Evidence ('who claims what, on what basis, under what context/time, how does it relate to other claims?', candidate Assertion aggregate held as a hypothesis not a decision), Inquiry ('what information is requested, under what interpretation, what counts as adequate?'), and Assessment ('given a regime/context/evidence/knowledge-state, what assessment results?', assessments as immutable records not mutable properties).
invariants: assessments are immutable records of evaluations, not mutable properties of the evaluated object

rows.anchor: these are not merely subclasses of Question; they are query intentions or information-seeking behaviors. ... QuestionOperator: type, required bindings, expected relation, expected cardinality, answer-shape policy. ... A question may contain presuppositions ... presuppositionally defective.
rows.statement: Corrects the ten Question subclasses (WhatQuestion, WhoQuestion, etc.) into a single Question entity carrying a QuestionOperator value object (avoiding inheritance proliferation), with the operator constraining rather than determining the answer space; adds question presuppositions as a major omission -- 'why did the election result change?' presupposes an election result existed, that it changed, that compared states are identifiable, and that 'change' is meaningful under the selected context -- so a question may be syntactically valid, semantically interpretable, yet presuppositionally defective or answerable only after clarification.

rows.anchor: TruthValue enum is potentially dangerous ... TruthStatus: TRUE, FALSE, UNDETERMINED, NOT_APPLICABLE. KnowledgeStatus: KNOWN, UNKNOWN, UNCERTAIN, DISPUTED, UNEXPLORED. ConflictStatus: CONSISTENT, CONFLICTING, INCONSISTENT.
rows.statement: Corrects the original model's single TruthValue enum {TRUE,FALSE,UNKNOWN,BOTH,NEITHER} as dangerously conflating unrelated scales (TRUE/FALSE concern semantic/model-theoretic evaluation, UNKNOWN concerns knowledge availability, BOTH/NEITHER reflect a paraconsistent/incomplete logic, and unsupported/disputed concern evidence/assertion state), splitting it into three independent enums: TruthStatus{TRUE,FALSE,UNDETERMINED,NOT_APPLICABLE}, KnowledgeStatus{KNOWN,UNKNOWN,UNCERTAIN,DISPUTED,UNEXPLORED}, ConflictStatus{CONSISTENT,CONFLICTING,INCONSISTENT}, with BOTH/NEITHER retained only as values within an explicitly chosen four-valued logic regime, not as universal kernel values.

lineage_claims.quote: The current `TruthValue` enum is potentially dangerous ... I would separate: TruthStatus / KnowledgeStatus / ConflictStatus

rows.anchor: Relevance is not a property of an answer alone. It is a relation: Answer --relevantTo--> Question ... Completeness = required answer obligations satisfied / required answer obligations. ... Answerability should be evaluated before truth assessment of a candidate answer.
rows.statement: Reformalizes three evaluation-vector components: Relevance as a relation Answer--relevantTo-->Question evaluated against purpose/audience/task/context/time/answer-policy (a technically true answer may be irrelevant); Completeness as a ratio of satisfied to required answer obligations (only meaningful once the question operator produces obligations); Answerability as evaluated prior to and independently of truth (a question can be answerable even when the true answer is 'false', and unanswerable even when a model produces a plausible sentence).

rows.anchor: SemanticModel ... RepresentationRecord ... AssertionRecord ... QuestionSpecification ... AssessmentRecord ... KnowledgeProjection — This should probably be a read model, not an aggregate.
rows.statement: Proposes six aggregate/read-model candidates with invariant examples: SemanticModel (relation endpoints must be valid semantic identities; concept identity stable across representation changes); RepresentationRecord (content hash/identity consistent; transformations reference source records; interpretation must not overwrite the original); AssertionRecord (exactly one proposition reference; explicit asserting agent/context/temporal semantics; epistemic status changes recorded as events); QuestionSpecification (operator present; presuppositions represented; ambiguity cannot be silently discarded); AssessmentRecord (evaluator/regime explicit; immutable; different assessment types cannot overwrite one another); KnowledgeProjection (a read model materializing selected assertions, temporal scope, boundaries, evidence summaries, conflicts, unanswered questions, and derived confidence/coverage measures).

rows.anchor: Avoid composition for cross-context ownership ... Replace direct sentence-to-proposition identity ... Connect evidence to assertions ... Make assessments contextual and immutable.
rows.statement: Corrects four specific PlantUML relationships: replace KnowledgeState/Topic/Concept/Proposition composition with reference/projection relations (a concept need not be owned by one topic); replace direct Sentence-->Proposition with Sentence--receives-->Interpretation--proposes-->Proposition (accommodating ambiguity); replace Evidence-->Proposition:supports with role-specific Evidence-->Assertion (supports/challenges/qualifies); replace a single Assertion-->'1' TruthAssessment cardinality with Assertion-->'0..*' AssessmentRecord (each tied to an EvaluationRegime and EvaluationContext), since an assertion may have multiple assessments under different regimes/times/authorities/purposes.

rows.anchor: Aggregates are consistency boundaries ... Assertion, Evidence, Question, and TruthAssessment may be related, but they probably should not be one aggregate. ... Domain events are preferable for cross-context propagation ... PropositionDefined, RepresentationRegistered, ... BoundaryVersioned.
rows.statement: States that aggregates should be chosen for transactional-consistency requirements, not diagram proximity -- Assertion/Evidence/Question/TruthAssessment differ in change rate, authority, and lifecycle and should not be one aggregate; proposes eleven domain events (PropositionDefined, RepresentationRegistered, InterpretationProposed, AssertionCreated, ObservationRecorded, EvidenceLinked, InferenceProduced, QuestionSubmitted, AssessmentCompleted, AssertionSuperseded, BoundaryVersioned) for cross-context propagation instead of direct cross-context mutation, plus a candidate value-object list (SemanticIdentity, TemporalInterval, LanguageCode, QuestionOperator, EpistemicStatus, EvidenceRole, EvaluationRegime, BoundaryReference, ConfidenceInterval, AnswerObligation, ProvenancePointer) and per-aggregate (not generic) repositories.
invariants: aggregates are chosen for consistency requirements, not conceptual proximity

rows.anchor: Facts versus hypotheses ... An observation record is not automatically identical to the state of affairs observed. ... The following should remain hypotheses: Proposition as the central semantic primitive ... A universal five-valued truth enum ... A one-to-one mapping from linguistic sentence to proposition.
rows.statement: Explicitly separates well-supported architectural facts (provenance models distinguish entities/activities/agents/derivations/responsibility; SHACL validates structure not truth; representation is distinct from what it represents, per Wittgenstein; an observation record != the observed state of affairs; evidence/completeness/relevance are all relative, not intrinsic) from items that must remain hypotheses (Proposition as the central semantic primitive; Assertion as the central epistemic aggregate; KnowledgeState as first-class rather than projection; a universal five-valued truth enum; a universal numeric knowledge-assessment vector; the listed question operators as a complete taxonomy; a one-to-one sentence-to-proposition mapping).
dependencies: tractatus-logico-philosophicus-lens (representation vs represented, referenced via Wittgenstein)

rows.anchor: I would rename Epistemic Answer Vector to Assessment Profile or Evaluation Profile. "Vector" suggests that the dimensions are commensurable ... Assess(x, q, K, C, R) -> <v, j, b, t> ... an act performed under a regime, not a permanent intrinsic property.
rows.statement: Renames the earlier 'Epistemic Answer Vector'/'Knowledge Assessment Vector' E=(S,T,C,R,A,K,U) to 'Assessment Profile'/'Evaluation Profile' since 'vector' wrongly implies the seven dimensions are commensurable and combinable; proposes an AssessmentProfile record (semanticAdmissibility, truthStatus, epistemicStatus, coherenceStatus, relevanceResult, answerabilityResult, completenessResult, uncertaintyRepresentation, evaluationRegime, context, evidenceBasis, assessedAt) where fields differ in kind (categorical/graded/probabilistic), and a general function Assess(x,q,K,C,R) -> <v,j,b,t> (result, justification, evidence basis, evaluation time), emphasizing an assessment is an act performed under a regime, not a permanent intrinsic property.

lineage_claims.target: Epistemic Answer Vector / Knowledge Assessment Vector (same file, earlier section)
lineage_claims.quote: I would rename Epistemic Answer Vector to Assessment Profile or Evaluation Profile.

rows.anchor: The model is not one Knowledge Space aggregate. It is a context map for semantic modeling, representation, assertion, evidence, inquiry, assessment, governance, and projection. ... DDD Conceptual Separation and Context Map.
rows.statement: Final recommendation: reframe the model as a context map (not one Knowledge Space aggregate) covering semantic modeling/representation/assertion/evidence/inquiry/assessment/governance/projection; proposes a ten-part 'DDD Conceptual Separation and Context Map' next artifact (bounded contexts, per-context term meanings, aggregate candidates, value objects, domain events, invariants, translation relationships, unresolved ambiguities, counterexamples, explicit non-responsibilities), replacing direct ownership/identity relationships with context-local models, explicit interpretation, assertion/evidence relations, immutable assessment records, projection-based knowledge states, and temporal/authority-aware references.

rows.anchor: A Published Language ... is a deliberately designed, publicly documented language used to translate between bounded contexts without forcing those contexts to share their internal models. ... For KnowledgeOS ... the Published Language should express inter-context meaning and commitments, not expose the internal ontology of the KnowledgeOS kernel.
rows.statement: Introduces the DDD Published Language pattern for KnowledgeOS: explicit, stable, documented as a semantic contract, and translated into local models rather than reused as domain objects -- neither a shared database schema nor a universal domain model, but an inter-context communication language expressing commitments without exposing the kernel's internal ontology, proposing a six-context map (Semantic Modeling -> Representation/Interpretation -> Assertion/Evidence -> Inquiry/Answering -> Assessment/Governance -> Knowledge Projection) not necessarily a mandatory pipeline.
dependencies: five bounded contexts (same file, DDD critique section)

rows.anchor: SemanticReference, RepresentationReference, AssertionReference, QuestionReference, EvidenceReference, ContextReference, BoundaryReference, AgentReference, TemporalScope, ProvenanceReference, AssessmentReference ... This message does not say that the proposition is true. It says that an assertion exists with specific provenance, context, authority references, and temporal semantics.
rows.statement: Proposes eleven stable semantic-primitive reference/contract types for the Published Language, illustrated by a worked 'AssertionPublished' JSON message (assertionId, propositionRef, assertedBy, contextRef, validity interval, epistemicStatus, provenanceRef) that explicitly does not assert the proposition is true -- it asserts that a situated, provenanced, time-bounded assertion exists.
invariants: a published assertion message never itself asserts truth of the proposition

rows.anchor: Semantic contract ... PropositionProposed ... The word "proposed" matters. ... Representation contract ... InterpretationProposed ... supports multiple interpretations rather than assuming that one sentence deterministically maps to one proposition. ... Assertion and evidence contract ... EvidenceLinked ... Avoid a generic field such as "evidenceStrength": 0.84 without specifying for which assertion... ... Inquiry and assessment contract ... QuestionSubmitted ... answerObligations.
rows.statement: Divides the Published Language into four message-family layers with worked JSON examples: Semantic contract (ConceptDefined/PropositionProposed/etc, where 'proposed' signals well-formedness without asserting truth); Representation contract (RepresentationRegistered/InterpretationProposed/InterpretationAmbiguous, supporting multiple candidate interpretations per sentence); Assertion and evidence contract (AssertionCreated/EvidenceLinked/AssertionDisputed, explicitly warning against an unscoped 'evidenceStrength: 0.84' field lacking target assertion/regime/evaluator/time/method); Inquiry and assessment contract (QuestionSubmitted carrying operator/target/requestedRelation/temporalScope/answerObligations, far stronger than a bare natural-language question string).

rows.anchor: I would avoid using a Shared Kernel for: KnowledgeState; Proposition; Evidence; TruthAssessment; Question; Document. ... A possible small Shared Kernel might contain only: StableIdentifier, Version, TemporalInterval, ProvenancePointer, ContextReference, CorrelationId.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Published Language from DDD's Shared Kernel pattern: KnowledgeState/Proposition/Evidence/TruthAssessment/Question/Document are too semantically loaded and context-divergent to be a Shared Kernel; only genuinely identical low-level primitives (StableIdentifier, Version, TemporalInterval, ProvenancePointer, ContextReference, CorrelationId) qualify, and even these only if their semantics are truly identical across contexts.

rows.anchor: Upstream and downstream relationships ... Semantic Modeling | Representation | Published Language ... Governance | All contexts | Open Host Service + Published Language ... The relationship type should be explicit in the context map, because the technical integration alone does not show power, ownership, or translation responsibility.
rows.statement: Tabulates six upstream/downstream context relationships with DDD relationship-type labels (Semantic Modeling->Representation: Published Language; Representation->Assertion/Evidence: Open Host Service+Published Language; Assertion/Evidence->Inquiry: Published Language; Inquiry->Assessment: Customer/Supplier+Published Language, inquiry defines answer obligations; Governance->All: Open Host Service+Published Language; Assertion/Evidence->Projection: Published Language), stating the relationship type must be explicit since technical integration alone hides power/ownership/translation responsibility.

rows.anchor: The Assertion Context may publish: epistemicStatus = ASSERTED. The Assessment Context may translate this into: reviewTarget.status = UNVERIFIED_ASSERTION. The two values are not contradictory. They belong to different bounded contexts.
rows.statement: Illustrates why Anti-Corruption Layers are essential: a downstream context translates published fields (propositionRef, epistemicStatus, validity, provenanceRef) into its own local concepts (ClaimUnderReview, ReviewBasis, ApplicablePeriod, SourceTrace) rather than importing them as domain classes directly, and a published 'ASSERTED' status may legitimately translate to a local 'UNVERIFIED_ASSERTION' without contradiction because the two values belong to different bounded contexts.

rows.anchor: Published Language must express uncertainty and plurality ... a conventional integration model often assumes one canonical value: {"status": "TRUE"}. That is unsuitable for KnowledgeOS. ... two AssertionPublished messages for the same proposition with status ASSERTED and DISPUTED ... A projection may later calculate conflictStatus = CONFLICTING, but this should be a derived view, not a destructive merge.
rows.statement: Requires the Published Language preserve plurality rather than collapsing to one canonical value: two published assertions for the same proposition (one status=ASSERTED, one status=DISPUTED by a different agent) must both be representable, with any conflictStatus=CONFLICTING computed only as a derived projection, never as a destructive merge of the source assertions.
invariants: conflict status is a derived view, never a destructive merge

rows.anchor: Domain events versus Published Language messages ... A domain event describes something meaningful that happened in the source bounded context ... A Published Language message is the stable, externalized contract ... internal events may change more frequently than inter-context contracts.
rows.statement: Distinguishes a domain event (internal, source-context language, e.g. AssertionCreated) from a Published Language message (stable externalized contract, e.g. AssertionPublished, possibly derived from multiple domain events and deliberately omitting internal details), since internal events may change more frequently than inter-context contracts.
dependencies: eleven domain events (same file, DDD critique section)

rows.anchor: Do not rely on schema compatibility alone. A message can remain structurally compatible while changing meaning. ... "verified by automated rule" to "verified by authorized human reviewer" without any JSON schema change. ... version: serialization schema; semantic vocabulary; evaluation regime; authority policy; temporal interpretation.
rows.statement: Warns that schema-compatible messages can silently change meaning (a 'verified' status changing from automated-rule-verified to human-reviewer-verified with no JSON schema change), requiring five independent versioning axes: serialization schema, semantic vocabulary, evaluation regime, authority policy, and temporal interpretation, each message additionally carrying messageType/schemaVersion/semanticModelVersion/producerContext/producedAt/correlationId/causationId/provenanceRef.
invariants: schema compatibility alone does not guarantee semantic compatibility

rows.anchor: Published Language governance ... otherwise, it becomes an uncontrolled shared kernel. ... Integration Language Governance ... PublishedTerm: termId, definition, semantic scope, allowed contexts, relation constraints, examples, counterexamples, version, owner, status.
rows.statement: Proposes a dedicated 'Integration Language Governance' capability (vocabulary definitions, message specifications, semantic versioning, compatibility policy, deprecation, migration guides, examples/counterexamples, conformance tests, translation rules, breaking-change approval authority) and a PublishedTerm schema making the Published Language itself a governed knowledge artifact, warning that without this it becomes an uncontrolled shared kernel.

rows.anchor: conformance should have at least three layers: Structural conformance ... Semantic conformance ... Governance conformance ... None of these automatically establishes truth.
rows.statement: Defines a three-layer conformance model for Published Language messages -- structural (required fields, valid references, cardinalities, well-formed temporal intervals; SHACL cited as a technical option for RDF graph validation), semantic (relation endpoint types permitted, proposition admissible in the declared semantic model, question operator compatible with target), and governance (producer authorized, authority scope valid, message version approved, evidence role permitted) -- explicitly stating none of the three establishes truth.
invariants: structural, semantic, and governance conformance never themselves establish truth

rows.anchor: AssertionCreated ... means: An assertion was created in the Assertion Context. It must not mean: The proposition is true. ... InterpretationProposed ... must not mean: The sentence has one final meaning. ... AssessmentCompleted ... must not mean: The result is universally valid in every context.
rows.statement: States 'the most important rule' of the Published Language design: message names must publish facts about domain activity and references to semantic objects, never universal interpretations -- AssertionCreated means an assertion was created, not that the proposition is true; InterpretationProposed means an interpretation was produced, not that the sentence has one final meaning; AssessmentCompleted means an evaluation was performed under a specified regime, not that the result is universally valid everywhere.
invariants: a published message about an act must never be read as a claim of universal truth

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Published Language is a governed, versioned integration language for exchanging semantic references, representations, assertions, evidence relations, questions, assessments, temporal scopes, authority references, and provenance across bounded contexts. It is not a shared domain model, not a shared database schema, and not a universal truth vocabulary. ... Shared communication language ≠ shared domain model.
rows.statement: Final DDD recommendation: formalizes KnowledgeOS Published Language as governed/versioned, exchanging semantic references/representations/assertions/evidence relations/questions/assessments/temporal scopes/authority references/provenance, explicitly not a shared domain model, shared database schema, or universal truth vocabulary; recommends combining Published Language, Open Host Service, Anti-Corruption Layers, a minimal Shared Kernel, Customer/Supplier relationships, and separate local models, condensed into the decisive principle 'shared communication language != shared domain model', which allows federation without recreating the semantic monolith bounded-context design is meant to prevent.
dependencies: all prior Published Language sections (same file)
invariants: shared communication language ≠ shared domain model

lexical.anchor: H1 — Representation ... representation ≠ reality; representation ≠ knowledge.

formal.anchor: H3 — Knowledge is dynamic ... K(P,t,c,E) ... I would not yet make this mathematical expression part of the kernel. It is a modelling lens.

governance.anchor: Don't call this Knowledge State yet. That name already assumes we have defined what knowledge is. ... I would call it something like: Epistemic Situation Model or simply: Knowledge Candidate Model.

aliases: Human-AI Organizations, Responsibility and Collective Intelligence (Step 97)

sources.note: Step 97: models organizations as first-class KnowledgeOS semantics. Distinct Person/Role/Team/Organization/Authority; temporal role assignment and scoped delegation; Responsibility!=Authority!=Accountability with AI-execution-does-not-transfer-accountability; dissent as first-class KnowledgeArtifact; two independent assurance dimensions ProceduralValidity vs EpistemicSupport; escalation as legitimate PendingHigherAuthority state; human override of AI as first-class provenance event; argumentation structure and UnresolvedConflict as legitimate status; escalation graphs preserving full history; Decision!=Fact (decisions as scoped institutional facts, not universal truth); organizational ontology; AI agent identity/non-repudiable attribution; OrganizationalStructure!=DomainStructure; executable organizational-orphan/authority-orphan/single-point-of-knowledge-failure detection; and OrgKnowledge(t) epistemic state. Builds directly on the pre-existing collective-choice-aggregation-model and decision-power-model-lens.

rows.anchor: Steps 91-96 established implementation->concurrency->failure->adversarial behavior->privacy->evolution. But organizations are not machines. Can responsibility, authority, disagreement, escalation and collective decision-making be represented as first-class semantics?
rows.statement: Frames Step 97's central question: whether responsibility, authority, disagreement, escalation, and collective decision-making can be first-class KnowledgeOS semantics rather than informal organizational assumptions.

lineage_claims.quote: Steps 91–96 established that KnowledgeOS can, in principle, preserve its semantics through: implementation→concurrency→failure→adversarial behavior→privacy→evolution.

rows.anchor: 97.1 — The organization becomes part of the system model ... Person, AIAgent, Role, Team, Organization, Authority. These are not interchangeable.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Person, AIAgent, Role, Team, Organization, and Authority as non-interchangeable entities, replacing the generic actor A.

rows.anchor: 97.2 — Experiment 1: person versus role ... Alice may occupy role ArchitectureApprover during [t1,t2]. Expected: the authority belongs to the role assignment, not permanently to the person. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 1: authority belongs to a temporal role assignment (Alice as ArchitectureApprover during [t1,t2]), not permanently to the person; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 97.3 — Role assignment is temporal ... Assignment(P,R,t). Authority(P,R,t) depends on whether the assignment is valid at time t.
rows.statement: Defines temporal role assignment Assignment(P,R,t), with Authority(P,R,t) depending on the assignment's validity at t.

rows.anchor: 97.4 — Experiment 2 ... Alice was ArchitectureApprover until t1. She issues an approval at t2>t1. Expected: the approval cannot automatically inherit the old authority. Result: PASS
