rationale_evidence.statement: Notes a sampled metric (1% of requests) is an estimate, not necessarily exact population behavior.

notations: ConformanceMatrix=Requirement x Architecture x Implementation x Verification x Runtime x Governance

sources.note: Step 108: the ConformanceMatrix artifact and fundamental rule Specified!=Implemented!=Verified!=RuntimeProven; seven conformance states C0-C6; per-capability tuple K=(S,D,I,V,R,G); six-level evidence-strength hierarchy E1-E6; nine conformance category codes (CONF/PART/SPEC/IMPL/DRIFT/VIOL/EXC/UNK/OBS); NoEvidence=>NoVerifiedClaim invariant; the AIJudgment vs DeterministicVerification distinction and assurance hierarchy (machine check wins over AI assertion); bidirectional Requirement<->Implementation<->Verification and ArchitectureDecision<->CodeComponent traceability; reframing the matrix as a knowledge graph G_C=(V,E) supporting conformance queries; evidence freshness/EvidenceValidity(t) and continuous conformance Conformance=f(t); the named Architecture Assurance Plane; the Finding object and closure-requires-verification-evidence lifecycle; risk-weighted ConformanceDebt (never ticket/class count); and the six-step implementation-archaeology methodology (with an explicit warning against filename-only evidence search). Extends architecture-conformance-engineering-model (S1000) with its concrete evidence/measurement apparatus, and previews Step 109 (evidence-based repository reconstruction).

rows.anchor: We now move from defining the architecture to measuring conformance. ConformanceMatrix=Requirement×Architecture×Implementation×Verification×Runtime×Governance.
rows.statement: Defines the central artifact ConformanceMatrix=Requirement×Architecture×Implementation×Verification×Runtime×Governance, transitioning from architecture definition to conformance measurement.

type_signature.domain: Requirement x Architecture x Implementation x Verification x Runtime x Governance

rows.anchor: The purpose is not to create another documentation exercise. The purpose is to establish an evidence-backed answer to: How much of the intended KnowledgeOS architecture actually exists in the software?
rows.statement: States the purpose of the conformance matrix: an evidence-backed answer to how much of the intended architecture actually exists in the software, not a documentation exercise.

rows.anchor: 108.1 — The fundamental rule ... Specified ≠ Implemented ≠ Verified ≠ Runtime Proven. A design document saying 'KnowledgeOS provides provenance' does not establish that provenance exists in the implementation.
rows.statement: States the fundamental rule Specified≠Implemented≠Verified≠RuntimeProven, illustrated by a design-doc provenance claim not establishing implementation, an existing table not establishing correct population, and passing tests not establishing runtime conformance.

rows.anchor: 108.2 — Conformance states ... C0 Not specified, C1 Specified, C2 Designed, C3 Implemented, C4 Verified, C5 Runtime proven, C6 Governed. These dimensions should not be collapsed into one number.
rows.statement: Defines seven conformance states C0 (not specified) through C6 (governed), stating they should not be collapsed into a single number.

rows.anchor: 108.3 — Why a single maturity score is dangerous ... Implementation=100% but RuntimeEvidence=0%. 'KnowledgeOS is 100% implemented' would be misleading. Instead we want a per-dimension status table.
rows.statement: Warns that a single maturity score is dangerous (100% implementation with 0% runtime evidence would make '100% implemented' misleading), preferring a per-dimension status table (Specification/Design/Implementation Complete, Verification Partial, Runtime Unknown, Governance Complete).

rows.anchor: 108.4 — The conformance tuple ... K=(S,D,I,V,R,G) where S=specification, D=design, I=implementation, V=verification, R=runtime evidence, G=governance.
rows.statement: Defines the per-capability conformance tuple K=(S,D,I,V,R,G): specification, design, implementation, verification, runtime evidence, governance.

type_signature.codomain: S x D x I x V x R x G

rows.anchor: 108.5 — Example: provenance ... Requirement R_prov, Architecture A_prov, Implementation I_prov, Tests V_prov, Runtime R_prov, Governance G_prov. Only then can we claim Conformance_prov=Strong.
rows.statement: Worked example: a provenance requirement is traced through architecture/implementation/tests/runtime/governance stages, with Conformance=Strong claimable only once every stage has evidence.

rows.anchor: 108.6 — Evidence hierarchy ... E1=Architecture statement, E2=Source implementation, E3=Automated test, E4=Deployment evidence, E5=Runtime observation, E6=Independent verification. The higher levels generally provide stronger empirical support.
rows.statement: Defines an evidence-strength hierarchy E1 (architecture statement) through E6 (independent verification), with higher levels providing stronger empirical support for implementation claims.

rows.anchor: 108.7 — Experiment 1 ... Architecture document states 'Agents use KnowledgeOS.' No code or configuration demonstrates this. Expected: Specified=True but Implemented=Unknown. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 1: an architecture-only claim ('Agents use KnowledgeOS') with no supporting code yields Specified=True, Implemented=Unknown; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.8 — Experiment 2 ... Repository contains KnowledgeClient but no tests. Expected: Implemented=True, Verified=Unknown. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 2: an implemented KnowledgeClient with no tests yields Implemented=True, Verified=Unknown; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.9 — Experiment 3 ... Tests exist but are never executed in CI. Expected: TestExists=True but VerificationStrength=Reduced. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 3: tests existing but never run in CI yield TestExists=True with VerificationStrength=Reduced; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.10 — Evidence must be traceable ... Claim→Evidence. C: 'KnowledgeOS records decisions.' Evidence: SourceFile+Test+RuntimeRecord.
rows.statement: States every conformance claim must trace to evidence (Claim→Evidence), illustrated by a decision-recording claim backed by SourceFile+Test+RuntimeRecord.

rows.anchor: 108.11 — No evidence, no conformance claim ... NoEvidence ⇒ NoVerifiedClaim. The result should be Unknown rather than Pass.
rows.statement: States the rule NoEvidence⇒NoVerifiedClaim: absent evidence, the result must default to Unknown rather than Pass.

invariants.name: I_NoEvidenceNoVerifiedClaim
invariants.statement: Absence of evidence yields Unknown, never Pass, for a conformance claim.

rows.anchor: 108.12 — Conformance categories ... CONF, PART, SPEC, IMPL, DRIFT, VIOL, EXC, UNK, OBS. These are more useful than simple pass/fail.
rows.statement: Defines nine practical conformance category codes (CONF/PART/SPEC/IMPL/DRIFT/VIOL/EXC/UNK/OBS), stated as more useful than binary pass/fail.

rows.anchor: 108.13 — First conformance domain: Knowledge model ... Evidence, Claims, Inference, Decisions, Authority, Actions, Observations, Provenance, Temporal validity, Conflict handling — all cells UNK, deliberately using '?'. We do not fill these cells from architectural assumptions.
rows.statement: Presents the Knowledge-model conformance domain table with ten capabilities, all cells deliberately marked '?'/UNK rather than filled from architectural assumption.

rows.anchor: 108.14 — Second domain: Governance ... Rule registry, Authority, Rule lifecycle, Change classification, Governance routing, Exceptions, Approval evidence, Governance drift, Rule versioning — all UNK.
rows.statement: Presents the Governance conformance domain table with nine capabilities, all cells UNK.

rows.anchor: 108.15 — Third domain: Agent architecture ... Pointer-layer model, Shared knowledge, Agent identity, Tool authorization, Recommendation boundary, Action provenance, Memory separation, Knowledge promotion, columns Claude/Codex/KnowledgeOS/Verification — all UNK.
rows.statement: Presents the Agent-architecture conformance domain table with eight capabilities across Claude/Codex/KnowledgeOS/Verification columns, all cells UNK.

rows.anchor: 108.16 — Fourth domain: Runtime ... Topology, Versions, Configuration, Dependencies, Security boundaries, Agent activity, Governance controls, Drift detection — all UNK.
rows.statement: Presents the Runtime conformance domain table with eight capabilities, all cells UNK.

rows.anchor: 108.17 — Fifth domain: assurance ... We need to distinguish AIJudgment from DeterministicVerification. 'The architecture looks compliant' is not equivalent to ArchitectureCheck=PASS.
rows.statement: Introduces the assurance domain, distinguishing AIJudgment from DeterministicVerification: an AI's compliance impression is not equivalent to a deterministic ArchitectureCheck=PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.18 — Experiment 4 ... LLM says 'The repository follows the architecture.' No deterministic check exists. Expected: AIAssessment not VerifiedConformance. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 4: an LLM's unchecked 'follows the architecture' claim is AIAssessment, not VerifiedConformance; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.19 — Deterministic assurance ... Rule→MachineCheck→Result. NoDirectDBAccess checked via dependency graph → PASS/FAIL.
rows.statement: Prefers deterministic assurance Rule→MachineCheck→Result where possible, illustrated by a NoDirectDBAccess rule checked via dependency-graph analysis.

rows.anchor: 108.20 — Experiment 5 ... Agent claims 'No service accesses the database directly.' Static dependency scanner finds one. Expected: DeterministicCheck=FAIL. Result: PASS. The machine check wins over the AI assertion.
rows.statement: Experiment 5: a static scanner contradicting an agent's no-direct-DB-access claim yields DeterministicCheck=FAIL, with the machine check winning over the AI assertion; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.21 — Assurance hierarchy ... DeterministicEvidence > ReproducibleVerification > RuntimeObservation > AIInterpretation > UnverifiedAssertion. This is not an absolute ranking for every purpose, but it is a strong default for conformance claims.
rows.statement: Defines the assurance hierarchy DeterministicEvidence > ReproducibleVerification > RuntimeObservation > AIInterpretation > UnverifiedAssertion, explicitly a strong default rather than an absolute ranking.

rows.anchor: 108.22 — Architecture rules as executable specifications ... A↛B should ideally be encoded as Check(A,B). ArchitectureRule→AutomatedTest.
rows.statement: States architecture rules should be encoded as executable checks (ArchitectureRule→AutomatedTest), e.g. Check(A,B) for a forbidden dependency A↛B.

rows.anchor: 108.23 — Experiment 6 ... Architecture rule exists. No automated check exists. Expected: Governance/ArchitectureAutomationGap. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 6: an architecture rule with no automated check yields a Governance/ArchitectureAutomationGap finding; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.24 — The conformance chain ... Rule→Check→Evidence→Finding and Finding→Decision→Remediation→Verification. This is the executable assurance loop.
rows.statement: Defines the executable assurance loop: Rule→Check→Evidence→Finding→Decision→Remediation→Verification.

rows.anchor: 108.25 — Requirement traceability ... Implementation→Requirement (backward) and Requirement→Verification (forward).
rows.statement: States every important implementation capability should trace backward to a requirement and forward to verification.

rows.anchor: 108.26 — Experiment 7 ... A major service exists. Nobody can identify which architectural requirement justified it. Expected: potential orphan implementation. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 7: a major service with no identifiable justifying requirement is flagged as a potential orphan implementation; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.27 — Orphan architecture ... Requirement R exists. No implementation satisfies it. Expected: ImplementationGap.
rows.statement: Defines the reverse orphan case: a requirement with no satisfying implementation is an ImplementationGap.

rows.anchor: 108.28 — Experiment 8 ... Requirement: 'All agent actions require auditability.' No implementation evidence exists. Expected: Gap. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 8: an auditability requirement with no implementation evidence yields a Gap finding; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.29 — Bidirectional traceability ... Requirement↔Implementation↔Verification is required for high-assurance capabilities.
rows.statement: States bidirectional traceability Requirement↔Implementation↔Verification is required for high-assurance capabilities.

rows.anchor: 108.30 — Architecture-to-code traceability ... ArchitectureDecision→CodeArea. Example: ADR-042→Knowledge Service.
rows.statement: Defines architecture-decision-to-code traceability (ArchitectureDecision→CodeArea), illustrated by ADR-042→Knowledge Service.

rows.anchor: 108.31 — Experiment 9 ... ADR says 'Use event-driven communication.' Repository has event infrastructure. But nobody can determine which parts implement ADR-042. Expected: Weak traceability. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 9: existing event infrastructure that cannot be tied to the specific ADR-042 that motivated it is Weak traceability; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.32 — Code-to-architecture traceability ... CodeComponent→ArchitectureDecision. This helps explain why a component exists.
rows.statement: Defines the reverse code-to-architecture traceability CodeComponent→ArchitectureDecision, explaining why a component exists.

rows.anchor: 108.33 — Experiment 10 ... Component exists. No architectural context is discoverable. Expected: potential architecture debt. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 10: a component with no discoverable architectural context is potential architecture debt; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.34 — Conformance is a graph ... G_C=(V,E) with nodes requirements/principles/rules/ADRs/components/code/tests/deployments/runtime observations/findings/decisions, and edges implements/verifies/supports/violates/supersedes/dependsOn.
rows.statement: Reframes the conformance matrix as a graph G_C=(V,E) with eleven node types and six edge types (implements/verifies/supports/violates/supersedes/dependsOn).

rows.anchor: 108.35 — Experiment 11 ... A component has no relationship to any architecture requirement. Expected: Graph identifies an orphan node. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 11: an unrelated component is identified by the graph as an orphan node; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.36 — Architecture knowledge graph ... This gives KnowledgeOS another important role: ConformanceGraph rather than merely DocumentRepository.
rows.statement: States KnowledgeOS's role as a ConformanceGraph rather than merely a DocumentRepository.

rows.anchor: 108.37 — Conformance queries ... Which architecture rules are not implemented? Rules-ImplementedBy. Which implemented components have no architectural justification? Components-JustifiedBy. Which governance rules have no enforcement? Rules-EnforcedBy. Which runtime violations have no remediation? Fi
rows.statement: Presents four illustrative conformance graph queries: unimplemented rules, unjustified components, unenforced governance rules, unremediated findings.

rows.anchor: 108.38 — Experiment 12 ... Query: Show architecture rules with no verification. Expected: KnowledgeOS can produce the set. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 12: KnowledgeOS can produce the set of architecture rules lacking verification via graph query; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.39 — This changes the role of documentation ... Documentation becomes KnowledgeGraphView rather than the sole source of truth. A document can explain a relationship. The graph preserves the relationship.
rows.statement: States documentation becomes a KnowledgeGraphView rather than the sole source of truth; the graph, not the document, preserves the relationship.

rows.anchor: 108.40 — Evidence freshness ... Conformance evidence itself becomes stale. A test passed yesterday. That does not necessarily establish today's runtime. EvidenceValidity(t).
rows.statement: Defines EvidenceValidity(t): conformance evidence becomes stale, and a previously-passing test does not establish current runtime conformance.

rows.anchor: 108.41 — Experiment 13 ... Architecture test passed six months ago. System changed significantly since then. Expected: Evidence freshness must be considered. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 13: a six-month-old passing test on a significantly changed system requires evidence-freshness consideration; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.42 — Continuous conformance ... Conformance=f(t). Not Conformance=Constant.
rows.statement: States conformance must be modeled as Conformance=f(t), not a constant.

rows.anchor: 108.43 — Experiment 14 ... Deployment changes a critical component. Expected: relevant conformance checks become stale or are rerun. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 14: deployment of a critical-component change should stale-mark or rerun relevant conformance checks; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.44 — Conformance triggers ... CodeChange, ArchitectureChange, PolicyChange, Deployment, RuntimeDrift, SecurityEvent.
rows.statement: Lists six conformance-recheck triggers: CodeChange, ArchitectureChange, PolicyChange, Deployment, RuntimeDrift, SecurityEvent.

rows.anchor: 108.45 — Experiment 15 ... Architecture rule changes. Expected: affected verification checks are identified. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 15: a changed architecture rule should have its affected verification checks identified; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.46 — KnowledgeOS as assurance infrastructure ... Architecture Assurance Plane. It connects Intent→Implementation→Verification→Runtime. This is stronger than a normal documentation platform.
rows.statement: Names the Architecture Assurance Plane capability connecting Intent→Implementation→Verification→Runtime, stronger than an ordinary documentation platform.

rows.anchor: 108.47 — Assurance finding ... A failed conformance check becomes a Finding, containing Rule, Expected, Observed, Evidence, Severity, Owner, Status.
rows.statement: Defines the Finding object (Rule,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Severity,Owner,Status) produced by a failed conformance check.

type_signature.codomain: Rule x Expected x Observed x Evidence x Severity x Owner x Status

rows.anchor: 108.48 — Experiment 16 ... Architecture check fails. No owner assigned. Expected: UnmanagedFinding. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 16: an owner-less failed check is classified UnmanagedFinding; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.49 — Finding governance ... A finding becomes a governance object when material. Finding→GovernanceWorkflow.
rows.statement: States a material finding becomes a governance object, routed via Finding→GovernanceWorkflow.

rows.anchor: 108.50 — Experiment 17 ... Critical security architecture violation occurs. Expected: automatic escalation according to policy. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 17: a critical security-architecture violation triggers automatic policy-driven escalation; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.51 — Closure evidence ... Finding closure requires evidence: Finding→Remediation→VerificationEvidence.
rows.statement: States finding closure requires Finding→Remediation→VerificationEvidence, not remediation claims alone.

rows.anchor: 108.52 — Experiment 18 ... Developer marks finding 'resolved.' No verification exists. Expected: Status≠Closed. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 18: a developer's unverified 'resolved' claim leaves Status≠Closed; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.53 — Conformance debt ... Unresolved findings accumulate as ConformanceDebt. This should not simply become 'Number of tickets.' It should account for Severity, Age, Impact, Risk.
rows.statement: Defines ConformanceDebt from accumulated unresolved findings, warning it must be weighted by Severity/Age/Impact/Risk, never reduced to a ticket count.

rows.anchor: 108.54 — Experiment 19 ... One critical violation is more important than 100 low-risk documentation deviations. Expected: risk-weighted assessment. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 19: one critical violation must outweigh 100 low-risk deviations under a risk-weighted assessment; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.55 — The conformance score ... A numeric score may eventually be useful, but only after the evidence matrix exists. Score=WeightedEvidence. Never Score=NumberOfImplementedClasses.
rows.statement: States a numeric conformance score is only meaningful after the evidence matrix exists, and must be Score=WeightedEvidence, never a raw class count.

rows.anchor: 108.56 — Experiment 20 ... System has 100 classes named 'Knowledge.' Expected: this does not establish semantic conformance. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 20: 100 classes literally named 'Knowledge' do not establish semantic conformance; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.57 — Implementation archaeology ... Step A find architectural claim, Step B find implementation candidates, Step C find tests, Step D find runtime evidence, Step E find governance ownership, Step F classify.
rows.statement: Defines a six-step implementation-archaeology methodology: find claim, find implementation candidates, find tests, find runtime evidence, find governance ownership, classify.

rows.anchor: 108.58 — Evidence collection discipline ... We should not search only for files named knowledge/architecture/governance, because architecture may be encoded indirectly in database schemas, migrations, APIs, services, policies, tests, CI, hooks, configuration, scripts.
rows.statement: Warns against filename-only evidence search, since architecture may be encoded indirectly in schemas, migrations, APIs, services, policies, tests, CI, hooks, configuration, or scripts.

rows.anchor: 108.59 — Experiment 21 ... Architecture capability 'Agent action logging.' Implementation may exist as session-changes-logger rather than AgentAuditService. Expected: semantic search rather than filename search. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 21: an 'agent action logging' capability implemented as session-changes-logger (not AgentAuditService) requires semantic rather than filename search; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 108.60 — This is why evidence reconstruction matters ... The architecture must be reconstructed from Artifacts+Behavior+Relationships. Not from class names alone.
rows.statement: States architecture must be reconstructed from Artifacts+Behavior+Relationships, not from class names alone.

rows.anchor: 108.61 — Current conformance matrix baseline ... D={Knowledge,Governance,Agents,Runtime,Assurance,Traceability}. Each domain contains concrete capabilities.
rows.statement: Defines the baseline conformance domain set D={Knowledge,Governance,Agents,Runtime,Assurance,Traceability}.

rows.anchor: 108.62 — Master matrix ... capabilities across Knowledge/Governance/Agents/Runtime/Assurance/Traceability domains, columns Intended/Implementation/Verification/Runtime/Governance, all cells '?'. The question marks are intentional.
rows.statement: Presents the master capability matrix across all six domains with all Implementation/Verification/Runtime/Governance cells deliberately left as '?'.

rows.anchor: 108.63 — The next phase begins here ... Until Step 108 we have mostly answered: What must KnowledgeOS be? Now we can ask: What is KnowledgeOS actually? This is a methodological transition from ArchitectureConstruction to ArchitectureVerification.
rows.statement: States the methodological transition from ArchitectureConstruction (what must KnowledgeOS be) to ArchitectureVerification (what is KnowledgeOS actually).

rows.anchor: 108.64 — Step 108 verdict: STEP 108 — CONFORMANCE MODEL: PASS. The conformance framework is now sufficiently defined to perform empirical reconstruction. The implementation status of individual capabilities remains TBD until evidence is mapped.
rows.statement: Records Step 108 verdict PASS, scoped to the conformance framework's sufficiency for empirical reconstruction; individual capability status remains TBD.

rows.anchor: 108.65 — The next step: Step 109 — Evidence-Based Repository Reconstruction. This is where we should stop inventing additional conceptual layers and begin the actual archaeological examination of KnowledgeOS/EKS. Architecture Claim→Artifact→Code→Test→Runtime Evidence. Output: KnowledgeOS Actual Comp
rows.statement: Previews Step 109: the transition from conceptual layering to actual archaeological examination of KnowledgeOS/EKS, following Architecture Claim→Artifact→Code→Test→Runtime Evidence, starting with system boundaries and major components, producing a ten-category KnowledgeOS Actual Component Inventory.

lexical.anchor: We now move from defining the architecture to measuring conformance. ConformanceMatrix=Requirement×Architecture×Implementation×Verification×Runtime×Governance.

formal.anchor: We now move from defining the architecture to measuring conformance. ConformanceMatrix=Requirement×Architecture×Implementation×Verification×Runtime×Governance.

operational.anchor: 108.7 — Experiment 1 ... Architecture document states 'Agents use KnowledgeOS.' No code or configuration demonstrates this. Expected: Specified=True but Implemented=Unknown. Result: PASS

sources.note: Step 230 (phase_measure_theory): derives a candidate minimal mathematical/DDD kernel for KnowledgeOS, reducing the initial 6-tuple (K,C,T,A,E,L) to a 5-tuple (K,C,T,E,A) with Lineage L=History(T), and proposes the seven candidate architectural principles (Semantic Integrity, Boundary Preservation, Epistemic Integrity, Governed Action, Temporal Lineage, Assurance) as DERIVED functions of the kernel rather than independent primitives. Also formalizes the O->E->Q->I->K epistemic progression, context as a 5-tuple, the phi_AB context-mapping-induced semantic-collapse equivalence relation, candidate DDD aggregates (KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy), a four-plane architecture (Semantic/Epistemic/Transformation/Governance + crossing Lineage), and a four-level stack (Mathematical/Domain/Implementation/Philosophical).

rows.anchor: O\rightarrow E\rightarrow Q\rightarrow I\rightarrow K and K\rightarrow D\rightarrow A.
rows.statement: First correction: a single set K cannot mean 'knowledge' generically -- distinguishes O (Observation), E (Evidence), Q (Claim), I (Inference), K (Accepted Knowledge), D (Decision), A (Action) as different domain objects, giving epistemic progression O->E->Q->I->K and operational progression K->D->A.

rows.anchor: Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C. ... Artifact\neq EpistemicRole. Meaning is contextual.
rows.statement: Artifact versus epistemic role: for artifact X, Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C, so Artifact != EpistemicRole -- the same artifact can be evidence in one context and historical knowledge after acceptance in another; 'meaning is contextual' connects DDD directly to the mathematical model.

rows.anchor: C=(S_C,V_C,R_C,P_C,A_C)
rows.statement: Context is formalized beyond a bounded-context name as a 5-tuple C=(S_C semantic vocabulary, V_C validity rules, R_C material distinctions, P_C policies, A_C authority model) -- a DDD bounded context is thus a semantic and governance environment.

rows.anchor: \llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_1}\neq\llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_2}. Same representation \not\Rightarrow same meaning.
rows.statement: Bounded context as semantic space: an object x has meaning through a context-relative denotation [[x]]_C, and the same representation can have different meanings under different contexts ([[x]]_C1 != [[x]]_C2) -- 'same representation does not imply same meaning' is proposed as a mathematical foundation of DDD bounded contexts.

rows.anchor: x_1\sim_\phi x_2\iff\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2). ... [x]_\phi.
rows.statement: Context mapping phi_AB: S_A -> S_B between bounded contexts is not assumed bijective (often partial/many-to-one/one-to-many/conditional/lossy); it induces an equivalence relation x1 ~phi x2 iff phi(x1)=phi(x2) with equivalence classes [x]_phi, giving a rigorous formal handle on information/semantic collapse.

rows.anchor: SemanticViolation\iff MaterialDistinction\land UncontrolledCollapse.
rows.statement: Semantic loss is formalized precisely: a collapse phi_AB(x1)=phi_AB(x2) where x1 is not~_A x2 is a candidate semantic-loss event, but is an error (SemanticViolation) only if the collapsed distinction belongs to R_A or R_B (i.e. is material) -- SemanticViolation iff MaterialDistinction and UncontrolledCollapse, much stronger than simply 'preserve semantics'.

rows.anchor: M_A(x_1,x_2)\land\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2)\Rightarrow DeclaredLoss
rows.statement: Context-specific materiality predicate M_C(x1,x2) ('the distinction between x1 and x2 is material in context C') yields the architectural invariant candidate: M_A(x1,x2) and phi(x1)=phi(x2) implies DeclaredLoss for a transformation crossing from A to B.

rows.anchor: T=(K_A,C_A,A_t,P_t,E_t,\tau)\rightarrow(K_B,C_B).
rows.statement: Transformation T is progressively enriched from a bare (K_A,C_A)->(K_B,C_B) mapping to a full domain operation T=(K_A,C_A,Actor_t,Policy_t,Evidence_t,tau)->(K_B,C_B), with the DDD distinction Command (expresses intent) -> Transformation (domain operation/process) -> Event (records what happened).

rows.anchor: L(K_t)=\{(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,\tau_i,C_i)\}. ... KnowledgeOS lineage = typed provenance graph.
rows.statement: Lineage is formalized as a typed provenance graph G_L=(V_L,E_L) (nodes=knowledge states/artifacts, edges=transformations carrying metadata (T,A,E,C,tau)), generally a DAG allowing branching (K1->{K2^A,K2^B}) and merging -- substantially stronger than an ordinary version chain.

rows.anchor: Auth(a,r,c,p) mean actor a is authorized under role r, context c, and policy p. ... Identity\neq Authority.
rows.statement: Authority is formalized as a relation Auth(a,r,c,p) (actor, role, context, policy) rather than A=User; an action is legitimate only if Auth(a,r,c,p)=True, giving Identity != Authority (authenticated but not authorized is possible).

rows.anchor: E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance). ... E_q\xrightarrow{\mathcal I}Q.
rows.statement: Evidence is formalized as a 6-tuple E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance) rather than a boolean Evidence=True, supporting a claim Q via an inferential procedure E_q -I-> Q.

rows.anchor: \hat F_n\neq F. Observation\neq PopulationTruth.
rows.statement: Statistical interpretation of evidence: the empirical distribution hat F_n(x) estimates but is not identical to the underlying distribution F, giving Observation != PopulationTruth; likewise a confidence interval must never be silently converted into a ProbabilityOfTruth.

rows.anchor: P(\theta\mid E)=\frac{P(E\mid\theta)P(\theta)}{P(E)}. ... Bayesian machinery is one possible formalism for representing uncertainty where the domain permits probabilistic interpretation.
rows.statement: Bayesian evidence via Bayes' rule is offered as one possible uncertainty formalism, not a mandatory commitment -- must not be introduced merely because 'KnowledgeOS is probabilistic'.

rows.anchor: Assurance=DeterministicAssurance\cup StatisticalEvidence\cup HumanJudgement.
rows.statement: Two assurance modes are distinguished and must not be conflated: Deterministic (I(x)=True/False, e.g. SchemaValid(x)) and Statistical (P(H|E) or an estimator with uncertainty), together with human judgment forming Assurance = DeterministicAssurance union StatisticalEvidence union HumanJudgement; the appropriate mode depends on the invariant.

rows.anchor: Hash(x)=h. ... P(X>x). ... Meaning(x,C). ... Authorized(a,p). These require different mathematical structures.
rows.statement: Architectural properties are classified by kind, each needing different mathematics: exact (Hash(x)=h), empirical (P(X>x)), interpretive (Meaning(x,C)), normative (Authorized(a,p)) -- resolving the previous risk of treating every architectural property as probabilistically quantifiable.

rows.anchor: Set/Logic + Probability/Statistics + Semantics + Graph Theory.
rows.statement: KnowledgeOS is proposed to span four mathematical domains: Logic (handles invariants), Statistics (uncertainty and empirical evidence), Semantics (meaning and context), Graph theory (lineage and transformation history) -- a more defensible architecture than reducing everything to one equation.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord. Each aggregate protects its own invariants.
rows.statement: Candidate DDD aggregate boundaries (avoiding one enormous transactional aggregate): KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord, each with its own invariant -- e.g. KnowledgeItem 'cannot change materially without a recorded transition'; Transformation 'cannot be considered governed without an applicable authority/policy decision'; EvidenceRecord 'cannot silently change after being used to support a claim' (a source change must produce a new evidence state); Decision = f(Evidence,Authority,Context,Policy), not authoritative merely by existing; Policy determines AllowedTransformations/RequiredEvidence/RequiredAuthority/RequiredValidation, giving Policy->GovernedTransformation.

rows.anchor: ObservationRecorded, EvidenceRegistered, ClaimProposed, KnowledgeAccepted, TransformationRequested, TransformationExecuted, ValidationCompleted, DecisionApproved, KnowledgeSuperseded.
rows.statement: Nine candidate domain events forming the temporal history, supporting an event-sourced interpretation K_t = Fold(E_1,...,E_t), i.e. CurrentState = f(EventHistory) -- explicitly noted as an implementation choice, not a mandatory architecture requirement.

rows.anchor: \mathcal K=(State,Context,Transformation,Evidence,Authority) with Lineage being generated by the sequence of transformations: L=History(T).
rows.statement: The kernel is reduced from the original 6-tuple (K,C,T,A,E,L) to a 5-tuple (K,C,T,E,A) by recognizing Lineage L is not independent but generated by the transformation history: L = History(T) -- an important reduction toward the minimal kernel.

rows.anchor: SI=f(K,C,T) ... BP=f(C,T) ... EI=f(K,E) ... GA=f(A,T) ... TL=f(T_{1:n}) ... DA=f(E,T,Policy). ... the seven principles may not be seven fundamental architectural primitives. They may be derived properties.
rows.statement: Candidate dependency equations deriving the 6 (of the earlier 7-8) named architectural principles as functions of the minimal kernel: SemanticIntegrity=f(K,C,T), BoundaryPreservation=f(C,T), EpistemicIntegrity=f(K,E), GovernedAction=f(A,T), TemporalLineage=f(T_{1:n}), Assurance/DeterministicAssurance=f(E,T,Policy) -- proposing that these principles may be derived properties rather than independent primitives, precisely the compression the historical audit sought.

rows.anchor: \forall x,y: M_{C_A}(x,y)\land T(x)=T(y)\Rightarrow Loss(x,y) \text{ must be declared and governed.}
rows.statement: The deepest candidate invariant, the strongest mathematical expression of semantic integrity under transformation so far: for T:(K_A,C_A)->(K_B,C_B), for all x,y, M_{C_A}(x,y) (material distinction) and T(x)=T(y) (collapsed by the transformation) implies Loss(x,y) must be declared and governed.

rows.anchor: X_i=SemanticError(T_i). ... It measures the empirical behavior of transformations. It does not define semantics itself.
rows.statement: Statistical extension: repeated transformation executions T_1..T_n yield an empirical sample of a semantic-error variable X_i=SemanticError(T_i), from which hat F_X(x) and E[X] can be estimated -- distribution theory legitimately measures empirical transformation behavior but does not define semantics itself.

rows.anchor: \hat p=\frac1n\sum X_i estimates the observed violation rate p=P(MaterialViolation). ... we cannot conclude p=0. We can only say \hat p=0.
rows.statement: Transformation reliability: an indicator variable X_i=1 for material violation gives an observed-violation-rate estimator hat p = (1/n)sum X_i for the population quantity p=P(MaterialViolation); explicitly warns that hat p=0 over n=100 trials does not license concluding p=0 -- testing provides evidence, not automatic proof of universal correctness.

rows.anchor: Validator\Rightarrow Property proved for checked input, whereas StatisticalTesting\Rightarrow Evidence about population behavior. ... FormalAssurance+EmpiricalAssurance.
rows.statement: Two-layer assurance architecture: Layer 1 formal/deterministic (Invariant->Validator, proving a property for checked input) and Layer 2 empirical/statistical (Experiment->Sample->Distribution->Estimate->Uncertainty, giving evidence about population behavior) -- these are fundamentally different epistemic claims, combined as FormalAssurance + EmpiricalAssurance.

rows.anchor: K | Knowledge domain state ... L | Domain event/provenance graph. Mathematical abstraction \leftrightarrow Domain abstraction but they are not identical.
rows.statement: DDD interpretation table mapping each kernel element to a domain concept: K->Knowledge domain state, C->Bounded Context, T->Domain transformation/service, E->Evidence aggregate/value object, A->Authority/policy, L->Domain event/provenance graph -- mathematical abstraction corresponds to but is not identical to domain abstraction.

rows.anchor:
BoundedContext
eq Microservice. Aggregate
eq DatabaseTable. DomainEvent
eq MessageBrokerMessage.
rows.statement: Very important architectural rule set preventing technical implementation from corrupting the domain model: BoundedContext != Microservice, Aggregate != DatabaseTable, DomainEvent != MessageBrokerMessage; candidate bounded contexts (Knowledge, Evidence, Transformation, Governance, Verification) should not automatically become five microservices, since a bounded context is a semantic boundary, not a deployment unit.

rows.anchor: Semantic plane ... Epistemic plane ... Transformation plane ... Governance plane. And crossing all four: Lineage.
rows.statement: The architecture is expressed as four interacting planes -- Semantic (Context+Meaning), Epistemic (Evidence+Claims+Knowledge), Transformation (K_A->K_B), Governance (Authority+Policy+Decision) -- with Lineage crossing all four, diagrammed as Governance sitting above a central Transformation node connecting Semantic and Epistemic planes, feeding down into Lineage.

rows.anchor: L_1=Mathematical Structure ... L_2=Domain Architecture ... L_3=Software Implementation ... L_4=Philosophical Interpretation. This prevents category confusion.
rows.statement: A four-level architectural stack prevents category confusion: L1 Mathematical Structure (e.g. T:K_A->K_B), L2 Domain Architecture (e.g. KnowledgeTransformation), L3 Software Implementation (ApplicationService/Workflow/Agent), L4 Philosophical Interpretation (reflection through philosophy) -- with the Gita explicitly placed only at L4, safely separate from the mathematical kernel, since Gita is not a mathematical axiom and not a DDD bounded context.

rows.anchor: Chapter 1\rightarrow EncounteredConflict ... Chapter 4\rightarrow Knowledge-Action-Transmission. ... Observation\rightarrow Interpretation\rightarrow Knowledge\rightarrow Decision\rightarrow Action. There is therefore a possible structural correspondence.
rows.statement: A candidate Gita chapter correspondence at the interpretive (L4) layer: Ch1->EncounteredConflict, Ch2->Discernment, Ch3->ResponsibleAction, Ch4->Knowledge-Action-Transmission, structurally resembling the engineering kernel's Observation->Interpretation->Knowledge->Decision->Action -- explicitly labeled a possible structural correspondence, not identity.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS may be modeled as a governed transformation system over contextually typed knowledge, with the minimal candidate kernel (K,C,T,E,A). ... this is still a candidate reconstruction.
rows.statement: Step 230 verdict: KnowledgeOS may be modeled as a governed transformation system over contextually typed knowledge, with minimal candidate kernel (K,C,T,E,A) and the other named principles appearing derived rather than primitive -- explicitly still a candidate reconstruction requiring historical validation against Steps 1-182, and leaving 'what is K?' as the next major unresolved problem.

rows.anchor: 𝒦 = (K,C,T,E,A) is UNDER-SPECIFIED and NOT MINIMAL AS CLAIMED. It is not closed ... not independent ... minimality is asserted, never demonstrated.
rows.statement: Headline verdict: Step 230's candidate kernel (K,C,T,E,A) is UNDER-SPECIFIED and NOT MINIMAL AS CLAIMED -- not closed (its own definitions require Policy and tau, neither a kernel component), not independent (4 of 5 components appear inside the fifth, T), and minimality is asserted but never demonstrated; the corpus's own hedge ('still a candidate reconstruction') is credited as accurate.

rows.anchor: §230 opening 6-tuple ... §230.31/230.50 5-tuple ... with Lineage being generated by the sequence of transformations. L = History(T). ... one kernel, correctly reduced. Credited.
rows.statement: Q1 verdict: the 6-tuple (K,C,T,A,E,L) and 5-tuple (K,C,T,E,A) forms are NOT two different kernels but one legitimately, transparently reduced kernel via L=History(T) -- credited as a sound compression.

rows.anchor: History(T) is empty at t=0, and K_0's evidence still has an external source. ... it is not derivable from any transformation.
rows.statement: Q2/Q3 executed counterexample: L=History(T) holds only for internal lineage; at the initial state t=0, History(T) is empty, yet K_0's founding evidence (a document/measurement/external system) is genuine provenance not derivable from any transformation -- the corpus conflates internal derivation history with external provenance (kept apart in earlier steps 073 and 022), so lineage is NOT necessarily History(T), and CAN exist independently of transformation (Q4, verified via this base-case witness).

experiment.hypothesis: L=History(T) fully captures KnowledgeOS lineage
experiment.setup: examine the base case t=0 where no transformations have yet occurred
experiment.assumptions: T's signature per SS230.10 carries A,E,C,tau metadata
experiment.inputs: SS230.10, SS230.12, SS230.13 definitions
experiment.method: logical/executed counterexample construction
experiment.result: History(T)=empty set at t=0 while K_0 has external provenance
experiment.interpretation: L=History(T) valid for internal lineage only, not external provenance
experiment.limitations: corpus-internal analysis, not software-executed against real KnowledgeOS data
experiment.conclusion: reduction from 6-tuple to 5-tuple loses external provenance unless folded elsewhere, which the corpus does not do

rows.anchor: symbols referenced by the kernel's own definitions: ['A','C','E','K','Policy','T','tau'] NOT kernel components: ['Policy','tau'] => CLOSED? NO
rows.statement: THE DECISIVE RESULT (executed test, rated the single strongest finding of the audit): the kernel (K,C,T,E,A) is NOT CLOSED -- SS230.10's definition of T requires Policy (P_t) and tau (time), and SS230.32's derivation of Assurance is f(E,T,Policy), but Policy and tau are not kernel components; the kernel cannot define its own transformation component as written, and the corpus never notices this internal inconsistency.

rows.anchor: T's signature (§230.10) contains: ['A','C','E','K','Policy','tau'] => 4 of the other 4 kernel components appear INSIDE T. ... Both readings cannot hold. The corpus asserts both.
rows.statement: Independence-failure executed test: every one of the kernel's other 4 components (K,C,A,E) appears inside T's own signature, making the components mutually definable with the direction of primitiveness undetermined -- either T is primitive and K,C,A,E are projections of it (not independent), or K,C,A,E are primitive and T is derived from them (not itself primitive); the corpus asserts both readings simultaneously by listing all five as kernel components while defining one in terms of the other four, with no independence argument given anywhere in Step 230.

rows.anchor: remove T: breaks [SemanticIntegrity, BoundaryPreservation, GovernedAction, TemporalLineage, Assurance, Lineage] <- NOT recoverable. ... the minimal kernel may be (T) alone, with the other four as projections.
rows.statement: Executed removal test on SS230.32's six derived properties: removing T breaks 6 of 7 derived properties and is NOT recoverable, while removing K, C, E, or A each breaks fewer properties and each IS recoverable as a projection of T's own signature -- under a 'T is primitive' reading the minimal kernel may collapse to (T) alone; A's removal breaks only GovernedAction, the weakest claim to primitiveness on the corpus's own table. Verdict: minimality is not demonstrated and the executed test gives positive reason to doubt it -- (K,C,T,E,A) is very likely redundant, not minimal, and no formal minimality proof exists anywhere (SS230.32's six f(...) derivations never supply an actual function).

rows.anchor: Model F (§230.51): K = (Graph, Types, Propositions, Evidence, Probability, Time) Evidence appears INSIDE K and ALSO as kernel component E -> DUPLICATED
rows.statement: Q5 executed test: under Model F (Step 230/231's own proposed hybrid answer to 'what is K?'), Evidence appears both inside K and as the separate sibling kernel component E -- Evidence is double-bound/duplicated with no stated distinction (e.g. evidence-as-content vs evidence-as-warrant); Time similarly sits inside K while tau (required by T) is not itself a kernel component -- asymmetric treatment with no stated reason. Verdict: CONTRADICTED.

rows.anchor: A appears (i) as a kernel component, (ii) inside T's signature as A_t -- time-indexed, and (iii) inside lineage edges as metadata. ... step-179 boxed a 7-ary Authority, and step-182 boxed a 5-ary Authority with no actor argument. Step 230's A is neither and cites neither.
rows.statement: Q6: whether Authority A is primitive or contextual is undetermined by the corpus -- it appears as a kernel component, as time-indexed A_t inside T's signature (suggesting it is a function of context and time, i.e. contextual not primitive), and as lineage-edge metadata; this collides uncited with step-179's 7-ary Authority and step-182's 5-ary actor-less Authority, neither of which Step 230's A matches or cites.

rows.anchor: §230.5 treats C as a semantic space ... §230.13 carries C as edge metadata. §230.10 has C_A and C_B as arguments and results of T. A space, a metadatum, and a function argument are three different types. No typing is given.
rows.statement: Q7: Context C is treated inconsistently as three different types with no stated typing relation -- a mathematical semantic space (SS230.5), edge metadata (SS230.13), and a function argument/result of T (SS230.10). Verdict: UNDER-SPECIFIED.

rows.anchor: We have K but have not yet defined what a knowledge state actually is. ... This honesty is exemplary and is credited. It is also devastating for the kernel.
rows.statement: Q8: the corpus itself explicitly admits (SS230.49) that K, the first kernel component, remains undefined ('is it a set? a graph? a probability distribution?...this is the next major problem') -- credited as exemplary honesty, but devastating for the kernel since 4 of the 6 SS230.32 derivations depend on K. Verdict: OPEN by the corpus's own admission.

rows.anchor: KERNEL_5 (005) ... K_OS=(A,T,P,E,I,S,X,R) (070) ... 16-term freeze (201-A) ... Step 230 cites none of them. Under LATER\neq SUPERSEDING, all seven kernels remain live and unreconciled.
rows.statement: Q9: whether the historical corpus supports kernel (K,C,T,E,A) is not established -- Step 230 itself defers this question, and independent cross-check finds 6 prior competing kernel proposals (KERNEL_5 at step 005, K_OS=(A,T,P,E,I,S,X,R) 8-tuple at step 070 SS70.1, K_L 7-tuple at step 070 SS70.21, amended K_OS+Identity at step 073 SS73.63, an 8-primitive family, and the 16-term freeze at 201-A) none of which Step 230 cites -- under LATER!=SUPERSEDING, all 7 kernels remain live and unreconciled, and the newest is the only one whose components are mutually definable (not independent).

rows.anchor: SI=f(K,C,T) ... Every one is an unnamed f. No function is supplied, so no property is actually derived. ... VERDICT: ARCHITECTURAL HYPOTHESIS, not derivation.
rows.statement: Q10: SS230.32's six derivations (SemanticIntegrity=f(K,C,T), BoundaryPreservation=f(C,T), EpistemicIntegrity=f(K,E), GovernedAction=f(A,T), TemporalLineage=f(T_1:n), Assurance=f(E,T,Policy)) each use an unnamed, unsupplied function f -- no property is actually derived, and Assurance's formula references Policy, a symbol outside the kernel (compounding the closure failure). Verdict: ARCHITECTURAL HYPOTHESIS, not derivation; 'this is precisely the compression we were looking for' is rated AUTHOR ASSERTION.

rows.anchor: §230.30's reduction L=History(T) ... §230.13's KnowledgeOS lineage=typed provenance graph ... §230.11's Command\rightarrow Transformation\rightarrow Event ... §230.49's admission that K is undefined -- the most valuable sentence in the file.
rows.statement: What survives from Step 230 per this audit: the L=History(T) reduction (for internal lineage), the typed-provenance-graph lineage structure, the Command->Transformation->Event DDD triad, Observation!=PopulationTruth, the Assurance=Deterministic union Statistical union HumanJudgement split, the three DDD guard distinctions (BoundedContext!=Microservice etc.), the Gita-is-not-an-axiom discipline, and (rated the most valuable sentence in the file) the admission that K is undefined. What does NOT survive: minimality, closure, component independence, the six f(...) derivations, and L=History(T) as a total (rather than internal-only) account of lineage.

rows.anchor: 1. Add Policy and tau to the kernel ... Smallest closing set: (K,C,T,E,A,P,τ). 2. State the direction of primitiveness. ... 5. Supply one f.
rows.statement: Six verifier-recommended (not applied) repairs: (1) add Policy and tau to the kernel or remove them from T's/Assurance's definitions -- smallest closing set (K,C,T,E,A,P,tau); (2) explicitly state the direction of primitiveness (T primitive with K,C,E,A as projections, or vice versa) rather than asserting both; (3) distinguish external provenance from internal lineage and state which the kernel carries; (4) resolve Evidence's double binding (remove it from Model F's K, or distinguish evidence-as-content from evidence-as-warrant); (5) supply at least one actual function f to convert an assertion into a derivation; (6) reconcile against the six prior kernels or record them as UNRECONCILED ALTERNATIVES -- item 1 rated the minimum required for the kernel to be well-formed at all.

rows.anchor: The corpus contains TWO separate kernel lineages, each internally coherent and genuinely evolving, which COMPETE with one another and are never reconciled. It is not one evolving theory. EQUIVALENT: 0 pairs, CONSERVATIVE EXTENSION: 7 pairs, COMPETING: 27 pairs, INCOMPARABLE: 2 pairs.
rows.statement: Executed pairwise comparison (by role, not name) of all nine candidate KnowledgeOS kernels answers the Reconciliation Gate's central question: the corpus contains TWO separate, internally-coherent, genuinely-evolving kernel lineages that COMPETE with each other and are never reconciled -- NOT one evolving theory. Of 36 kernel pairs: 0 equivalent, 7 conservative extension, 27 competing, 2 incomparable.

rows.anchor: K0/7-frame, K_OS(8), K_L(7), amended(8), 201-A freeze(16), 230 v0(6), 230 v1(5), 232 v2(6), 232 inner K(5). Steps 234, 235 and 236 introduce no new kernel.
rows.statement: Nine candidate kernels are catalogued with exact components and origin: K0/7-frame (pre-070), K_OS 8-tuple (070 SS70.1), K_L 7-tuple (070 SS70.21), amended 8-tuple (073 SS73.63), 201-A freeze 16-term, Step 230 v0 6-tuple (opening), Step 230 v1 5-tuple (SS230.31), Step 232 v2 6-tuple (SS232.41), Step 232 inner mathfrak K 5-tuple (SS232.1) -- Steps 234-236 introduce no new kernel, reusing 232's mathfrak K.

rows.anchor: Lineage A -- the artifact lineage: K0/7-frame subset 070 K_OS ... 201-A freeze. Lineage B -- the state-transformation lineage: 230 v1 subset 230 v0 subset 232 v2. The two lineages share only transformation and policy.
rows.statement: Two genuinely-evolving but mutually competing kernel lineages are identified: Lineage A (artifact lineage: K0->K_OS->K_L->amended->201-A freeze; core vocabulary artifact/type/event/invariant/provenance/transformation/policy) and Lineage B (state-transformation lineage: 230v1->230v0->232v2; core vocabulary state/context/transformation/evidence/authority/policy) -- sharing only transformation and policy; Lineage B never adopts artifact/type/event/invariant/provenance, Lineage A never adopts context/evidence/authority until the 201-A freeze, which then drops them again by omission.

rows.anchor: 232 v2 vs 232 inner K: COMPETING -- overlap {policy} only. ... Step 232 carries two incommensurable five/six-component structures -- its outer kernel and its own state tuple -- sharing exactly one role.
rows.statement: A third structure is found competing WITHIN one file: Step 232's outer kernel v2 {state,context,transformation,evidence,authority,policy} and its own inner state tuple mathfrak K {graph,status,temporal validity,lineage,policy} share exactly one role (policy) and are never mapped to each other in the file.

rows.anchor: BEFORE ... not closed ... REPAIR ... §232.41 adds P ... AFTER -- the nine tests: 1. Closure YES -- repaired. 2. Well-typedness NO. ... 5. Composability NO -- and Step 232 proves it itself. ... 9. Historical continuity NO.
rows.statement: Formal before/repair/after test of the 230->232 closure repair against the Reconciliation Gate's 9 required properties: only closure is repaired (Policy added, time re-handled as a sequence index); well-typedness, totality, determinism, composability (Step 232 itself proves T1,T2 in T_G but T2 o T1 not in T_G), computability, minimality, independence, and historical continuity ALL remain unresolved -- the repair is REAL but PARTIAL, fixing exactly one of nine properties, vindicating the earlier warning that 'a repair that makes a definition larger is not automatically a successful repair'.

rows.anchor: I*={Provenance} -- the only invariant in all nine historical phases (PHASE-LEDGER). Provenance appears in only 5 of 9 kernels, and in neither 230 v1 nor 232 v2. ... The one concept present in every phase of the 182-step history is demoted to a derived quantity by the latest kernels.
rows.statement: The decisive convergence finding: three independent methods (executed regex over 182 sources finding I*={Provenance}; executed role-comparison finding Provenance in only 5/9 kernels, absent from BOTH current kernels 230v1 and 232v2; and the formal counterexample showing L=History(T) fails to derive external provenance at t=0) converge on the sharpest structural finding of the reconciliation gate: the history's only universal invariant is absent from the kernel claiming to reconstruct that history, and the argument for its absence (L=History(T)) does not itself hold.

rows.anchor: transformation 8/9 <- the only near-universal primitive. policy 6/9. ... transformation is the only role appearing in 8 of 9 kernels. If any single primitive is historically warranted, it is that one.
rows.statement: Executed role-coverage count across all nine kernels: transformation appears in 8/9 (the only near-universal primitive), policy 6/9, {event,provenance,artifact,invariant,state,type} 5/9 each, {context,evidence,authority} 4/9, {status,identity,lineage} 2/9, {graph,temporalvalidity,observation,decision,assessment,action} 1/9 -- transformation being the one role historically warranted as a primitive is consistent with the corpus's own headline 'KnowledgeOS approx Governed Knowledge State Transformation System'.

rows.anchor: A -- ESTABLISHED: Nine candidate kernels exist; 27 of 36 pairs compete ... B -- PROVEN UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS ... C -- PLAUSIBLE/PROPOSED: That the two lineages could be unified via artifact->state and invariant->policy. No document proposes this; it is my conjecture. D -- REFUTED/UNDER-SPECIFIE
rows.statement: Final 4-class verdict per the gate's own mandated schema: (A) ESTABLISHED -- 9 kernels exist with 27/36 competing pairs, two disjoint never-reconciled lineages, Step 232's two incommensurable structures, the partial closure repair, transformation as the sole near-universal primitive, Provenance as I* yet absent from both current kernels; (B) PROVEN UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS -- L=History(T) holds for internal lineage only; (C) PLAUSIBLE/PROPOSED -- the two lineages COULD be unified via artifact->state and invariant->policy mappings, explicitly labeled the verifier's own unestablished conjecture, proposed by no corpus document; (D) REFUTED/UNDER-SPECIFIED -- 070's minimality (REFUTED via TV-F-043), 230/232's minimality (UNPROVEN), mathbb K's well-typedness (UNDER-SPECIFIED), kernel independence (REFUTED for both 230 and 232), and 'one evolving theory' itself (REFUTED -- two competing lineages).

rows.anchor: I have not chosen a kernel. All nine remain live. ... I have not repaired K's typing, ⊨'s semantics, or the independence failure. Nothing here is empirically validated. Corpus record: 494 files, 238 steps, zero empirical acts.
rows.statement: Explicit discipline statement of what must NOT be concluded from this reconciliation: no kernel has been chosen (all nine remain live), the two lineages have not been merged (the unification conjecture is explicitly the verifier's own, not established), Step 236 has not been treated as corroboration, and nothing here is empirically validated -- corpus record at this point: 494 files, 238 steps, zero empirical acts.

aliases: Semantics, Ontology, Bounded Contexts, Meaning Alignment and Semantic Interoperability

sources.note: S0914's Step 25V: the fully worked bounded-context-relative semantics/ontology model (SemanticRelation taxonomy, Anti-Corruption Layer, SemanticMapping contract, Zero_semantic); the next foundational layer after S0911's (Step 25S) entity-identity-resolution work, sharing its merge/split pattern at the meaning level.

rows.anchor: SameText\neq SameMeaning ... one of the most important principles for KnowledgeOS
rows.statement: States SameText ≠ SameMeaning, worked with an identical 'Approved' string across two contexts with differing meaning — 'one of the most important principles for KnowledgeOS.'

rows.anchor: Syntax: What was written? Identity: What entity does it refer to? Semantics: What does the statement mean? ... Syntax\neq Identity\neq Semantics
rows.statement: Defines three distinct layers (Syntax, Identity, Semantics) — Syntax ≠ Identity ≠ Semantics, worked with an 'Approved Nexus' example.

rows.anchor: SameMeaning(P_A,P_B\mid C_A,C_B) ... \{Equivalent,Compatible,Related,Different,Unknown\} ... Unknown must be a first-class result
rows.statement: Defines SameMeaning(PA,PB|CA,CB) with a five-value result set, requiring Unknown to be a first-class result.

rows.anchor: Meaning belongs to a BoundedContext ... Architecture Context Approved = board accepted ... Change Management ... Security ... These are related concepts. They are not necessarily identical
rows.statement: States 'Meaning belongs to a BoundedContext,' worked with three differing 'Approved' definitions across Architecture/Change Management/Security contexts.

rows.anchor: Approved=true and reuse it everywhere. That is dangerous ... Approved_{Architecture}, Approved_{Change}, Approved_{Security} remain distinct concepts. They may be mapped explicitly
rows.statement: Rejects a naive universal 'Approved=true' ontology entry, requiring distinct per-context concepts with explicit mappings.

rows.anchor: Bounded context defines Vocabulary+Meaning+Rules+Invariants ... Meaning(term,C) is context-dependent ... Meaning(Approval,C_1)\neq Meaning(Approval,C_2)
rows.statement: Formally defines a bounded context's semantic content as Vocabulary+Meaning+Rules+Invariants, giving context-dependent Meaning(term,C).

rows.anchor: Term\rightarrow Concept ... ArchitectureDecision, ArchitectureReview, ArchitectureApproval, ArchitectureException ... the language must correspond to DomainModel
rows.statement: Requires Ubiquitous Language (Term->Concept) to correspond to the DomainModel, not merely serve as a dictionary, worked with four Architecture BC terms.

rows.anchor: Ontology as Concepts+Relations+Constraints+Semantics ... Ontology\neq DomainModel
rows.statement: Defines Ontology as Concepts+Relations+Constraints+Semantics, distinct from the DomainModel (Behavior+Invariants+BusinessRules) — Ontology ≠ DomainModel, both supported without one replacing the other.

rows.anchor: SemanticRelation\in\{Equivalent,Subsumes,Specializes,Overlaps,Related,MapsTo,Incompatible,Unknown\} ... much richer semantic interoperability
rows.statement: Defines an eight-value SemanticRelation taxonomy, giving much richer semantic interoperability than a bare same/different check.

rows.anchor: Customer_A\equiv Client_B only if the domain mapping explicitly establishes it ... We should not assume this merely because humans often use the words similarly
rows.statement: Requires Equivalent relations to be explicitly established by domain mapping, never assumed from casual similar word usage (Customer/Client example).

rows.anchor: ProductionSystem\subset System ... ProductionSystem\sqsubseteq System ... matters for inheritance of knowledge
rows.statement: Defines subsumption ProductionSystem ⊑ System, mattering for knowledge inheritance.

rows.anchor: Repository\rightarrow requiresBackup ... Nexus repository may inherit requiresBackup ... Repository\rightarrow supportsFeatureX does not necessarily imply every specialized repository supports X ... Subsumption does not imply unrestricted property inheritance
rows.statement: States a specialized concept may inherit some but not all parent properties, giving the explicit invariant that subsumption does not imply unrestricted property inheritance.

rows.anchor: C_A\cap C_B\neq\emptyset without C_A=C_B ... Architecture Change / Software Change ... semantic mapping can be Overlap
rows.statement: Defines partial overlap between two concepts as a distinct semantic relation, worked with an Architecture-Change/Software-Change example.

rows.anchor: technically reviewed versus legally authorized [Approved] ... Treating them as equivalent could cause serious governance failure ... SemanticIncompatibility must be representable explicitly
rows.statement: Worked incompatible-meaning example under a shared term ('Approved' meaning technically-reviewed vs legally-authorized), warning conflation risks serious governance failure — SemanticIncompatibility must be explicit.

rows.anchor: ContextA\leftrightarrow ContextB ... ArchitectureApproval_A\rightarrow ArchitectureGatePassed_B. But this mapping should be explicit
rows.statement: Requires DDD-style explicit context mapping between concepts across bounded contexts, worked with an ArchitectureApproval->ArchitectureGatePassed example.

rows.anchor: Translate(C_A)=C_B does not necessarily mean C_A\equiv C_B ... transformation; aggregation; decomposition; enrichment; loss of information ... Translation\neq Equivalence
rows.statement: States Translation ≠ Equivalence: a translation mapping does not imply equivalence, since translation may involve transformation, aggregation, decomposition, enrichment, or information loss.

rows.anchor: Legacy System->Anti-Corruption Layer->KnowledgeOS Domain Model ... precisely what KnowledgeOS needs when integrating Jira; GitLab; CMDB; architecture repositories; monitoring systems; documents; external APIs
rows.statement: Applies the DDD Anti-Corruption Layer pattern to protect KnowledgeOS from directly importing foreign semantics when integrating Jira, GitLab, CMDB, architecture repositories, monitoring systems, documents, and external APIs.

rows.anchor: status=Done ... Done=Approved. That may be completely wrong ... ExternalStatus\neq DomainState unless an explicit mapping establishes it
rows.statement: Worked danger example: naively mapping Jira's status=Done to domain 'Approved' can be completely wrong — ExternalStatus ≠ DomainState absent explicit mapping.

rows.anchor: SemanticMapping=(SourceContext,SourceConcept,TargetContext,TargetConcept,Transformation,Conditions,Loss,Validity) ... extremely valuable
rows.statement: Defines an eight-field SemanticMapping contract, worked with a Jira/Status=Done -> ChangeManagement/ImplementationCompleted example explicitly noting non-equivalence to ArchitectureApproved.

rows.anchor: C_A contains five pieces of information but C_B contains only three ... InformationLoss ... otherwise the receiving system may assume equivalence when there is only partial correspondence
rows.statement: Requires explicit InformationLoss representation when a translation target holds less information than its source.

rows.anchor: Ticket 4811 Status=Done enriched with Deployment completed + Tests passed ... EnrichedConcept\leftarrow OriginalConcept+AdditionalEvidence
rows.statement: Worked semantic-enrichment example: an external record enriched with additional evidence into a richer domain concept, required to preserve provenance to the original concept plus additional evidence.

rows.anchor: T:C_A\rightarrow C_B may be 1:1, 1:n, n:1, or n:n ... matters when integrating enterprise systems
rows.statement: Defines a four-way semantic transformation cardinality taxonomy (1:1, 1:n, n:1, n:n).

rows.anchor: Status=Approved [external] while KnowledgeOS requires TechnicalApproval, SecurityApproval, ArchitectureApproval, BusinessApproval ... Approved_{External}\rightarrow Unknown\{Technical,Security,Architecture,Business\} ... precisely where Zero becomes useful
rows.statement: Worked one-to-many mapping example: an external 'Approved' cannot map to any specific required domain approval type without more information, yielding an Unknown-set result feeding Zero.

rows.anchor: M=\{m_1,\ldots,m_n\} ... interpretation should not prematurely choose one ... SemanticAmbiguity ... Lord may decide whether clarification is worthwhile
rows.statement: Requires retaining SemanticAmbiguity when a term has multiple candidate meanings rather than prematurely choosing one, with Lord deciding whether clarification is worthwhile.

rows.anchor: P(M=m_1)=0.92 ... does not mean Meaning=m_1 ... the domain may require deterministic mapping
rows.statement: Warns a semantic-confidence probability does not establish which meaning is correct where the domain requires deterministic mapping.

rows.anchor: tested against examples; counterexamples; domain invariants; expert validation; historical records ... Properties(A) remain valid after transformation
rows.statement: Requires semantic mappings to be validated against examples, counterexamples, domain invariants, expert validation, and historical records, testing property preservation across transformation.

rows.anchor: Approved(Change) implies AuthorizedForImplementation(Change) ... if the external Approved does not imply authorization, the mapping violates the target invariant ... SemanticMapping must preserve relevant invariants
rows.statement: Worked invariant-violation example (an external 'Approved' mapped to a domain concept that implies authorization it doesn't actually carry), giving the invariant that SemanticMapping must preserve relevant target invariants.

rows.anchor: A Context Map should not merely say A maps to B. It should say under these conditions, A may be interpreted as B without violating the target domain's invariants ... much stronger
rows.statement: Strengthens the DDD Context Map principle from a bare mapping statement to a conditional, invariant-preserving interpretation statement.

rows.anchor: G_C=(C,M) ... Jira->Change Management->Architecture Governance ... each arrow has an explicit contract
rows.statement: Defines a semantic interoperability graph G_C=(C,M) of bounded contexts and mappings, worked with a Jira->Change Management->Architecture Governance chain, each edge carrying an explicit contract.

rows.anchor: UniversalConcept and discard the originating context ... Concept=(Context,ConceptID,MeaningVersion) should remain explicit
rows.statement: Warns against flattening the semantic graph into a UniversalConcept, requiring the explicit tuple Concept=(Context,ConceptID,MeaningVersion) instead.

rows.anchor: Approval_A and Approval_B ... (Context_A,Approval) and (Context_B,Approval) ... prevents accidental collision
rows.statement: Worked example preventing accidental term collision across contexts by keeping (Context,Concept) tuples distinct.

rows.anchor: Approval_{v1} means technical approval ... Approval_{v2} means technical+security approval ... historical assertions must retain the version under which their meaning was established ... SemanticVersion becomes necessary
rows.statement: Defines semantic versioning: meanings evolve (e.g. 'technical approval' expanding to 'technical+security approval'), requiring historical assertions to retain their originating SemanticVersion.

rows.anchor: Application Owner may become Service Owner ... Meaning_{2025}\approx Meaning_{2026} ... KnowledgeOS must distinguish Renaming from SemanticChange
rows.statement: Distinguishes mere Renaming from genuine SemanticChange, worked with an Application-Owner/Service-Owner terminology-change example.

rows.anchor: Meaning_t against Meaning_{t+1} ... Equivalent, Modified, Split, or Merged ... resembles our identity merge/split operations from 25S
rows.statement: Defines semantic-drift detection comparing consecutive meaning versions into four outcomes (Equivalent/Modified/Split/Merged), explicitly resembling the identity merge/split operations from Step 25S.

rows.anchor: C_A\rightarrow C and C_B\rightarrow C ... historical meanings should remain preserved ... ConceptMerge is a semantic migration event
rows.statement: Defines ConceptMerge as a semantic migration event preserving historical meanings when two contexts' concepts converge.

rows.anchor: C\rightarrow\{C_1,C_2\} ... Approval becomes TechnicalApproval, ArchitectureApproval ... old records cannot automatically be assigned to either ... SemanticZero
rows.statement: Defines ConceptSplit ('Approval' splitting into TechnicalApproval and ArchitectureApproval), where old records cannot be automatically reassigned, producing SemanticZero — 'an important result.'

rows.anchor: Zero_{semantic}=MeaningInsufficientlyDetermined ... ambiguous terminology; incompatible context; missing mapping; outdated semantic version; semantic split; uncertain translation ... expands the Zero concept significantly
rows.statement: Formally defines Zero_semantic=MeaningInsufficientlyDetermined, covering six sub-cases, significantly expanding the general Zero concept.

lineage_claims.quote: Zero_semantic = MeaningInsufficientlyDetermined.

rows.anchor: LLM\rightarrow CandidateMapping\rightarrow SemanticValidator\rightarrow DomainApproval ... LLM should not silently establish JiraDone\equiv ArchitectureApproved
rows.statement: Establishes the LLM-proposes/SemanticValidator-decides pattern for candidate semantic mappings, explicitly forbidding an LLM from silently establishing a cross-context equivalence.

rows.anchor: ExplicitMapping over SimilarityInference ... Jira.status=Done -> ChangeManagement.ImplementationCompleted is explicit ... probably Approved is probabilistic. They must remain different
rows.statement: Prefers ExplicitMapping over SimilarityInference for high-value mappings, keeping deterministic and probabilistic mapping results visibly distinct.

rows.anchor: SourceContext, SourceConcept, MappingVersion, TargetConcept, Transformation ... TargetKnowledge\leftarrow SemanticMapping\leftarrow SourceKnowledge ... makes cross-context reasoning auditable
rows.statement: Requires every translated assertion to retain a five-field semantic provenance trail, making cross-context reasoning auditable.

rows.anchor: Same entity? YES. Same time? YES. Same proposition? NO ... SemanticConflict ... Both can be true simultaneously
rows.statement: Defines SemanticConflict as distinct from factual conflict: apparent disagreement can stem from differing propositional meaning even with matching entity/time, both sides simultaneously true.

rows.anchor: Equivalent(C_A,C_B) only if relevant properties are preserved ... complete equivalence is often impossible to prove ... many mappings should be Compatible rather than Equivalent
rows.statement: Formally defines Equivalent(CA,CB) via universal preservation of relevant properties, noting complete equivalence is often unprovable in practice, so many mappings should be Compatible rather than Equivalent.

rows.anchor: ArchitectureContext may treat ArchitectureDecision as an explicit aggregate. Another context may not have that concept at all ... exactly why bounded contexts exist
rows.statement: Argues bounded contexts exist precisely because different contexts make different ontological commitments — one context's aggregate concept need not exist in another.

rows.anchor: Entity, Event, Assertion, Evidence, Context, Time, Provenance, IdentityRelation, SemanticMapping ... but not every business concept ... KnowledgeOS should share epistemic semantics, not necessarily business semantics
rows.statement: Defines a lightweight shared semantic kernel (nine listed concepts), explicitly not extending to every business concept — 'KnowledgeOS should share epistemic semantics, not necessarily business semantics.'

rows.anchor: ontology lookup; concept matching; schema validation; rule validation; mapping execution; graph traversal; subsumption reasoning; constraint checking ... natural-language interpretation; ontology alignment; ambiguous concept matching ... SemanticCandidate\neq SemanticTruth
rows.statement: Distinguishes deterministic semantic operations (computationally feasible) from harder LLM-assisted tasks (NL interpretation, ontology alignment, ambiguous concept matching), with the invariant SemanticCandidate ≠ SemanticTruth.

rows.anchor: Test A same word different contexts -> SameText=True, SameMeaning=Unknown/Different. Test B explicit context mapping -> Translation=Valid under conditions. Test C semantic loss -> InformationLoss=True. Test D ambiguous external status -> SemanticAmbiguity. Test E invariant violation -> MappingReject
rows.statement: Runs seven falsification tests (A-G, all PASS) against the semantic-interoperability model: same word across contexts yields SameText=True but SameMeaning=Unknown/Different; an explicit context mapping yields conditionally Valid translation; a source-richer-than-target mapping yields InformationLoss=True; an ambiguous external status yields SemanticAmbiguity; a mapping violating a target invariant yields MappingRejected; a semantic version change leaves historical assertions' MeaningVersion preserved; and an undeterminable concept split yields SemanticZero.

rows.statement: Synthesizes the four-step 25S-25V progression, noting the dependency chain Identity->Semantics->Evidence->Inference->Decision and warning that errors in identity or semantics propagate through inference into decisions.

rows.anchor: How do we guarantee that a conclusion is valid for the correct temporal state, semantic version, identity version, model version and rule version simultaneously? ... Evaluate(KnowledgeSnapshot,t_{query},ContextVersion) ... Step 25W
