rationale_evidence.statement: States the deterministic-inference soundness requirement (Γ⊢_ρ P⇒P valid under ρ) is required, while completeness (Γ⊨P⇒Γ⊢_ρP) is deliberately not — soundness is generally more important than completeness for deterministic governance, since incompleteness may be intentional given computational cost or open-world/undecidable semantics.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Closed-world reasoning can exist locally ... The authoritative CMDB contains the complete list of registered systems. Then System\notin CMDB may legitimately imply NotRegistered(System). But this is only valid because the domain policy explicitly establishes completeness. ClosedWorld is a policy ass
rationale_evidence.statement: Allows local closed-world reasoning (e.g. absence from an authoritative CMDB implying non-registration) only when a domain policy explicitly establishes completeness — ClosedWorld is a policy assumption, never a universal law.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Dependency closure ... Deps(A_3)=\{A_1,A_2\}. If A_2 is retracted, KnowledgeOS must find Desc(A_2) and reassess those conclusions. Thus Step 10 directly feeds the revision mechanism of Step 9.
rationale_evidence.statement: Connects derivation dependency (Deps/Desc) directly to Step 9's revision mechanism: retracting a premise triggers reassessment of its descendants.

sources.note: Full mechanical TheoryState reconstruction of corpus steps 026-268 (265 files): finds 8/9 major objects born in one 08-28 morning, the 025-series apparatus vanishes almost entirely despite an immediate declaration of continuity, and withdraws the corpus own five-re-foundings record in favor of one general mechanism (apparatus lost across declared, not announced, discontinuities).

rows.anchor: §2 Corpus census — and a defect in my own first pass ... My first census reported 224 missing. A greedy regex ... Re-run with a first-match search: 3 missing, agreeing with the corpus's own four independent records.
rows.statement: Census of the 026-268 interval: 240 distinct step numbers, 265 files, 3 genuinely missing (217, 229, 268), 21 duplicated step numbers. Reports catching its own regex defect: a greedy pattern matched the LAST 'step-' token in a filename embedding a different step number in its title, falsely reporting step 224 as missing; corrected with a first-match search to agree with the corpus's own four independent records of exactly 3 missing steps. Notes this is the second regex defect caught this week in this programme (after a missing word-boundary in the Sat birth census), both caught before entering an artifact.

rows.anchor: §4–5 Object births ... Eight of nine objects are born in ONE MORNING — 10:14 to 12:26 on 2026-08-28, steps 026–099.
rows.statement: Mechanically derives birth times (both Unicode and LaTeX spellings, ordered by mtime not step number) for nine major objects: Zero (08-28 10:14, s026), K_t (10:15, s028), Omega (10:22, s031, Omega:W->O SS31.18), tau (10:22, s031), EC (10:23, s032), Delta_t (10:40, s047), Gamma (11:36, s053), Req (12:26, s099), and Determination (13:44, s155a, but flagged as not a true birth). Finds eight of nine objects born within a single morning window (10:14-12:26, steps 026-099).

rows.anchor: ⛔ Determination is not born at 155a ... Our previous architecture identified Determination. I would now make its semantics explicit. ⇒ RECONSTRUCTION ONLY / retrospective import ... Compare Det_r ... Strong structural similarity, zero citation ⇒ IDENTITY UNWITNESSED.
rows.statement: Corrects Determination's apparent 155a birth: the source itself says 'our previous architecture identified Determination; I would now make its semantics explicit', classifying this as RECONSTRUCTION ONLY / retrospective import, not a true concept birth -- the corpus-wide earliest occurrence is actually in reviews/ (2026-08-19 00:57), a governance lane, nine days earlier. Records 155a's formalization Determination=f(Claim,Evidence,Method,Context) with f unnamed and no codomain, plus Evidence!=Determination and Verification subset-of Determination. Compares this to Det_r:VxEC->S_sat (born 09-06): 155a carries the 'how' as an explicit Method argument while Det_r carries it as a function-name index plus EC -- strong structural similarity but zero citation between them, classified IDENTITY UNWITNESSED.

rows.anchor: The silences are the structure ... The interval is not gradual evolution. It is: everything introduced in one morning, then 100–157 files of near-total silence, then a return in the 183–267 band. ... The terminal staircase ... they die one per step, at the very end
rows.statement: Measures each object's longest silence gap in files: Gamma 157 files (s053->s197), Omega 155 files (s031->s186-pre), EC 135 (s117->s238), Delta_t 117 (s047->s155a), tau 112 (s074->s188), Zero 74 (s094->recovery doc). Concludes the interval's shape is NOT gradual evolution but a sharp pattern: everything introduced in one morning, then a 100-157 file near-total silence, then a return in the 183-267 band. Also finds a 'terminal staircase' where nine objects die one per step in sequence near the end of the interval (Req s234, Delta_t s240, EC s251, Determination s252, tau s263, Zero s264, K_t s265, Omega s266, Gamma s267).

rows.anchor: §16 Q1 · What happened to the 025-series apparatus? ... The 025 apparatus enters the interval EXACTLY ONCE — at step 251, two days later, as a HISTORICAL TABLE ROW. Never as a live formulation.
rows.statement: Censuses eight 025-series objects (Derive(H,Omega,EC), R_G, Gamma_G, EC_G, ContractSpecific, EpistemicContract, Sat/Satisfied/Sat_c, EvalReq/EvalRequirement) across all 265 interval files and finds zero occurrences of every named component except a bare 'Satisfied' word (2 hits) and Update(K_t,E_t,Omega,EC) appearing exactly once, at step_251, inside a historical genealogy table; '025' is cited by name exactly once in 265 files (also step_251), with an apparent second citation at step-152 identified and discarded as a false positive (a constitution clause number 'C-025'). Concludes the entire 025 apparatus enters the interval exactly once, two days later, as a historical table row, never as a live formulation.

rows.anchor: And yet continuity was declared, 41 seconds later ... step-025z ... 2026-08-28 10:13:25 ... step-026 ... 41 seconds later ... 'We continue from 25Z.' ... Continuity is DECLARED by name, 41 seconds later — and the apparatus is not CARRIED. Declaration ≠ transmission.
rows.statement: Finds the last 025-series document (step-025z) was written 2026-08-28 10:13:25, and step-026 was written just 41 seconds later, with step-026's third line explicitly stating 'We continue from 25Z.' Concludes continuity is declared by name almost immediately, yet none of the 025 apparatus is actually carried forward -- establishing the general principle that declaration does not equal transmission. Notes in passing a step-number homonym found incidentally: a different, unrelated step-026 document exists dated 2026-08-27 16:29:19 (a work-programme document), one day earlier, same step number, unrelated content.

rows.anchor: §12–13 · The re-founding hypothesis — tested on all six candidates ... NOT ONE DECLARES A RESTART. Every discontinuity in this corpus is MEASURED, never DECLARED.
rows.statement: Tests all six previously-labeled re-founding candidates against their own opening words: 026 ('we continue from 25Z') = CONTINUITY DECLARED; 031 ('step 31 is the first deliberate attempt to turn that architecture into a formal system') = CONTINUITY, a MODE CHANGE not a restart; 183-pre ('substantially aligned... but some later formulations should NOT be promoted') = SELECTIVE REJECTION of a named subset; 186-pre ('construct the mathematics around the distinctions we have already established') = CONTINUITY; 230 ('determine whether the apparently large architecture can be generated from a small kernel') = REDUCTION of the existing architecture; 262 ('we can now continue, but there is an important correction to the previous Step 261 conclusion') = CORRECTION; and the 09-06 rewrite (via G-25) = SELECTIVE INHERITANCE. Concludes not one of the six candidates declares a restart -- every discontinuity in this corpus is measured (by an outside investigator finding lost apparatus) rather than declared (by the author announcing a break).

rows.anchor: ⛔ WITHDRAWAL — the 'five re-foundings' record ... G-25 already removed the sixth. This reconstruction removes the concept. ... apparatus is lost across declared continuities. Authors say they continue, and mean it; the objects do not travel with the declaration.
rows.statement: Formally withdraws the corpus's own '07-THEORYSTATE-CHRONICLE.md' record of five re-foundings (031, 183-pre, 230, 262, 273), revising each label: 031's 'INDEPENDENT_REFOUNDING (drops the 025 apparatus)' is corrected -- 031 itself says it continues Steps 1-30; it is actually 026 that drops the apparatus while declaring continuity, the opposite framing; 183-pre's 'EXPLICIT_REPLACEMENT (pruning)' is downgraded to SELECTIVE_REJECTION since it affirms alignment and rejects only a named subset; 230's 'UNWITNESSED' becomes REDUCTION since it explicitly presupposes the existing architecture; 262's 'EXPLICIT_REPLACEMENT' becomes CORRECTION since it names its predecessor and corrects one specific conclusion; 273 unchanged. Concludes (with G-25 having already removed the sixth candidate) this reconstruction removes the whole 're-founding' CONCEPT itself, replacing five separate events with one general mechanism: in this corpus, apparatus is lost across declared continuities -- authors say they continue and mean it, but the objects do not travel with the declaration.

rows.anchor: §8 · Mathematical audit — Update, the interval's most overloaded operation ... Ten distinct signatures for one operation name, none related to any other. Arity 2–4, each in 1–3 files, zero cross-references. ⇒ IDENTITY UNWITNESSED at scale.
rows.statement: Finds ten distinct Update(...) signatures in the interval (arities 2-4: Update(K_t,E_t,Omega,EC), Update(K,E), Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), Update(K_t,V_{t+1},Delta_t), Update(K_t,O_{t+1}), Update(K_t,E_t), Update(K_t,E_new), Update(K,y), Update(K_t,V,G), Update(K_t,Outcome_I)), each occurring in only 1-3 files with zero cross-references between them, classified IDENTITY UNWITNESSED at scale. Independently corroborated by the master gap register's G-16 finding of '45 distinct RHS strings, 11 named transition functions, arities 1-6, no settled signature.'

rows.anchor: The codomain defect is inherited across three eras ... Status ... Determination = f(Claim,Evidence,Method,Context) ... none ... EvalReq(K,r,EC,Γ) ... none ... Three objects, three eras, three lanes — the same defect, never noticed by any of them.
rows.statement: Identifies a single recurring defect across three unrelated objects, eras and lanes: Status (025e, 08-27) is named but never defined; Determination=f(Claim,Evidence,Method,Context) (155a, 08-28) has no codomain at all; EvalReq(K,r,EC,Gamma) (theory-part-06, 09-06) has no codomain (V is only type-constrained, never stated). Concludes this identical defect recurs across three separate objects, eras and lanes, never noticed by any of them independently -- generalizing the earlier per-object findings into a single corpus-wide pattern.

rows.anchor: §16 · The ten questions Q1–Q10 (full table)
rows.statement: Answers ten structured research questions about the interval: Q1 the 025 apparatus did not cross (0 in 265 files, cited once as a table row 41 seconds after continuity was declared); Q2 Omega/tau/K_t/Zero/EC/Delta_t/Gamma/Req are all born inside the interval (inherited from nothing) while Determination is genuinely inherited from a governance lane; Q3 the whole evaluation/satisfaction family was independently re-derived, clearest case Determination's 155a formalization vs Det_r; Q4 no definition inside the interval completes an earlier one -- all distributed-completeness successes cross OUT of the interval; Q5 apparent gaps (Omega:W->O, EvalReq's codomain-name, S_sat) were all resolved from OUTSIDE the interval; Q6 genuine type changes found in Update (10 signatures), Omega (5 senses), Sat (4 codomains); Q7 homonyms/identity-unwitnessed cases include Omega x5, Update x10, Gamma, Determination (governance vs mathematical), and step-026 itself (two documents, one number, a day apart); Q8 K-formulation origins traced (K_t s028; K_v1 7-tuple at 031; K_v2 6-tuple only in an s155-156 recovery doc quoting 'the earlier model'; K_v3 (A,R) from outside the interval); Q9 per-object silence/activity counts (Sat and EvalReq: ZERO occurrences in the entire interval); Q10 three carry-forward lessons: declared continuity != transmitted apparatus, the terminal staircase pattern, and the inherited codomain defect across three eras.

rows.anchor: §18 · Terminal classification (Ω class E, Sat/EvalReq class C, Determination class E, Update class E, K_t class B, the interval itself class A structural)
rows.statement: Issues terminal classifications: Omega = class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, five senses, 0 of 10 pairs same, per G-22); Sat/EvalReq = class C (COMPETING COMPLETE DEFINITIONS, four codomains, two indexing strategies, per G-25, though entirely absent from this interval); Determination = class E (IDENTITY UNRESOLVED across governance birth, mathematical formalization, and Det_r, no citation between any pair); Update/transition = class E (10 signatures, no stated relation); K_t = class B (complete through multiple sources, but those sources are outside the interval); the interval itself = class A, COMPLETE HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION (structural) -- births, silences, returns and deaths now fully mapped mechanically for 9 objects over 265 files.

rows.anchor: §14 · Negative history ... Not found: Sat, Sat_c, EvalReq, EvalRequirement, R_G, Γ_G, EC_G, Derive(H,Ω,EC), ContractSpecific, EpistemicContract. ⇒ Recorded DEFINED ELSEWHERE ... not GENUINE CORPUS GAP. Det_r's body remains FIREWALL-LIMITED
rows.statement: Reports a negative-history search across all 265 files (both spellings, word-bounded, first-match step extraction) confirming zero occurrences of ten named objects (Sat, Sat_c, EvalReq, EvalRequirement, R_G, Gamma_G, EC_G, Derive(H,Omega,EC), ContractSpecific, EpistemicContract). Correctly classifies these as DEFINED ELSEWHERE (they exist before the interval at 023/025 and after it at 09-02/09-06) rather than GENUINE CORPUS GAP, per the programme's own discipline against declaring absence-within-a-bounded-window a true gap. Det_r's body remains classified FIREWALL-LIMITED (97% of occurrences excluded). Confirms firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no definition selected, all versions preserved.

rows.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
rows.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Concludes a gap was opened for an object the corpus had already defined three days earlier, then closed by 'recovering' it -- the corpus does not record this as a loss, it records it as a discovery. Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

rows.anchor: §1–4 · The 025→026 boundary, object by object — and my G-12 headline qualified ... The concepts did not stop. They de-formalised. ... sufficiency 73% ... satisfaction 45% ... contract 40% ... The NOTATION was lost. The CONCEPTS ran on through 45–73% of the interval.
rows.statement: Qualifies the prior G-12 finding that the 025 apparatus 'vanishes' at step 026: while all formal 025 SYMBOLS score exactly 0 across 265 files (confirmed true), a census of the underlying 025-era CONCEPTS in prose form finds sufficiency at 73% (193/265 files), satisfaction at 45% (120/265), contract at 40% (107/265), gap at 20%, acceptance criterion at 2%, while the specific phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0. Concludes the NOTATION was lost but the CONCEPTS ran on informally through 45-73% of the interval -- the earlier headline ('the apparatus vanishes') is true only of formal notation, not of underlying concepts.

rows.anchor: And precisely which form survived ... Of 241 satisf* occurrences sampled: 83 in technical context, 158 prose. ... What survived is satisfaction as a PREDICATE. What was lost is satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.
rows.statement: Samples 241 'satisf*' occurrences (83 technical, 158 prose) and verifies at ten specific steps (s070,079,081,086,091,092,095,097,098,101) that the surviving technical usage is uniformly an unformalised predicate ('the rule is satisfied', 'invariants remain satisfied') rather than the 025-series typed function Satisfied(K,r,EC) with three typed arguments and a result space S(9->10->11). Concludes precisely what survived was satisfaction AS A PREDICATE; what was lost was satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.

rows.anchor: An interpretation, marked as such ... consistent with — and would explain — the four divergent Sat codomains found in G-25 ... nothing carried a result space through the interval, so each later lane supplied its own. ⛔ Recorded as [PROPOSED], not as a cause.
rows.statement: Proposes, explicitly marked as an unproven interpretation (not a corpus-stated cause), that the loss of a shared result space during the interval would explain why G-25 later found four mutually non-citing Sat codomains (S 9-11, V_Sat 3, S_sat 4, S_sat variant): each later lane, lacking an inherited result space, supplied its own. Notes this hypothesis is recorded as [PROPOSED] rather than established, citing a cautionary precedent -- a previously withdrawn batch-003 claim ('the semantics-bearing argument always disappears') that failed for exactly the same overreach.

rows.anchor: §6 · Distributed completeness — the corrected classification ... EvalReq is the only 025-era object whose concept as well as its notation leaves the interval. That singles it out, and it is the one object G-25 found still untyped at 09-06.
rows.statement: Provides a corrected four-row classification: '025 apparatus vanishes at 026' is corrected from PARTIALLY-EVIDENCED to DE-FORMALISED (symbols 0, concepts 45-73%); 'Sat is absent from 026-268' stands for the FUNCTION but is FALSE for the underlying CONCEPT (0 vs 120 files); 'EvalReq is absent' stands fully, both notation and concept (even the phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0/265); 'Omega-B has no type' is REFUTED (excluded by design, per S14). Concludes EvalReq is uniquely the only 025-era object whose CONCEPT, not merely its notation, actually leaves the interval -- and it is the same object G-25 separately found still untyped as late as 09-06.

rows.anchor: §8, §12 · Identity and DDD — EC is the interval's worst case ... Three ECs, three arities, three bounded contexts, zero cross-references ... Verdict: HOMONYM ×3, IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair.
rows.statement: Identifies EC as a triple homonym with zero cross-references between any pair: EC=EpistemicClaim (s032, 11-tuple, 'the atomic unit of KnowledgeOS'); EC=engineering change (s117, 8-tuple, 'a test object' in a traceability experiment); EC=EpistemicContract (025-series, (R_G,Gamma_G) shape, 0 occurrences in steps 026-154). Classifies this as HOMONYM x3 with IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair, noting it is the same shape of finding as Determination (governance vs mathematical vs Det_r) and Gamma (four senses), already recorded elsewhere in this programme.

rows.anchor: §7 · Mathematical typing across the interval (PROVEN: Ω-2, K_v0, K_v1, EC-claim, Γ_A, EC-engchange; UNKNOWN: Zero never defined, Δ_t only α_t defined, Ω_t unresolved, Update 10 signatures) ... No promotion of TYPE-CONSTRAINED or INFERRED to PROVEN.
rows.statement: Audits mathematical typing status across the interval: PROVEN objects include Omega-2 (W->O), K_v0 (9-tuple, s028), K_v1 (7-tuple, s031), EC-claim (11-tuple, s032), Gamma_A (4-tuple, s053), EC-engchange (8-tuple, s117); UNKNOWN status objects include Zero (never defined anywhere in 265 files), Delta_t (one occurrence, whose 'where' clause defines only a sub-component alpha_t, not Delta_t itself), Omega_t as an argument of delta_K (signature declared unresolved by its own cited sources), and Update (10 unrelated signatures). Notes no TYPE-CONSTRAINED or INFERRED-status object was promoted to PROVEN in this pass.

rows.anchor: §11 · Senior-statistician audit ('satisfaction continues' 120 files/many independent lineages; '025 symbols absent' 0 hits × 265 files/1 measurement; Ω-B 'philosophical anchor' 33 files/1 lineage)
rows.statement: Applies the programme's senior-statistician discipline (distinguishing occurrence counts from independent evidential lineages) to its own three headline claims: 'satisfaction continues' (120 files) is genuinely MANY independent lineages spread across s070-s101+ and multiple sub-lanes; '025 symbols are absent' (0 hits x 265 files) is only ONE measurement, not 265 confirmations; Omega-B's 'philosophical anchor' framing (33 files) is only ONE lineage, a single continuous Gita/Lord-Lens thread from 08-26 onward.

rows.anchor: §15 · Classification of what this pass touched (Ω-B upgraded B; satisfaction-concept B / satisfaction-function C; EvalReq D genuine corpus gap for the interval, exhausted search; EC E; Zero/Δ_t E)
rows.statement: Issues final classifications for this pass: Omega-B is upgraded from D to class B (COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES -- defined semantically at birth, its absent type being a declared exclusion, not a gap); the satisfaction CONCEPT is class B (continues as a predicate across the interval) while the satisfaction FUNCTION remains class C (competing definitions, per G-25); EvalReq is class D (GENUINE CORPUS GAP for the interval specifically, on an now-exhausted search -- both notation and concept score 0 in all 265 files); EC is class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, three homonyms); Zero and Delta_t are class E (used throughout but never defined within the interval).

rows.anchor: §10 · Negative-history discipline ... Coverage qualifier preserved: ≈1.5% of the readable corpus is read semantically. No corpus-wide negative claim is made from this slice — the EvalReq finding is scoped to the interval, and Ω-B's is scoped to its own 33-file history.
rows.statement: States the negative-history search scope precisely (265 files of 026-268 plus the whole non-firewalled corpus for Omega-B's type across its 33-file history and for the 025 concepts) and preserves an explicit coverage qualifier: only approximately 1.5% (32 of 2,099 files) of the readable corpus has been read semantically by this whole gap-discovery programme so far. Explicitly refuses to generalize any finding beyond its search scope -- the EvalReq absence is scoped to this interval only, and Omega-B's exclusion-by-design finding is scoped to its own 33-file history only. Confirms firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no definition selected or merged.

rows.anchor: First, the admission. I classified EvalReq as D — GENUINE CORPUS GAP on ONE PHRASE SEARCH ('requirement evaluation' = 0/265). §15 forbids exactly that, and it is the fourth time this pass has caught the same error in my own work.
rows.statement: Opens with a self-admission: the EvalReq='D-GENUINE CORPUS GAP' classification (from S2918/G-12-semantic) rested on a single phrase search ('requirement evaluation', 0/265), which the programme's own methodology explicitly forbids as sufficient grounds for a gap claim -- noted as the fourth time in this investigation pass that the same single-search error has been caught in the investigator's own prior work.

rows.anchor: §1, §8 · The widened search — my single phrase was hiding two live objects ... requirement + satisf* 15 ... Eval( / Evaluate( as a function 9 ... Notation absent — concept present. The zero was real for eight variants and wrong for two.
rows.statement: Runs eleven search variants for requirement-evaluation across the 265-file 026-268 interval: nine variants correctly score 0 (EvalReq/EvalRequirement, the phrase 'requirement evaluation', 'evaluate/evaluating a requirement', requirement+evaluat* co-occurrence, requirement status/check*/met/fulfil*, contract-specific evaluation), but two variants that the prior single-phrase search missed score positive: 'requirement + satisf*' (15 hits) and 'Eval(/Evaluate(' as a function (9 hits). Concludes the notation was genuinely absent for eight variants but the concept was present via two variants the earlier search missed.

rows.anchor: §2, §9 · The genuine birth point is neither EvalReq nor EvalRequirement ... DV-23 ... Eval(P,K) ∈ {T,F,U} with the §25 connective tables (step-018) ... The evaluation family is born at STEP-018 — before the 026–268 interval AND before the 025-series.
rows.statement: Finds (via verification/DEFINITION-VERIFICATION-REGISTER.md's DV-23 entry, citing step-018) that the true birth point of the entire evaluation family is Eval(P,K) in {T,F,U} with connective tables at step-018 -- earlier than both the 026-268 interval and the entire 025-series. Discloses step-018 itself falls in the 001-022 band, an acknowledged backfill debt for this reconstruction lane, so its content here is taken secondhand from the verification lane's citing register, not yet read at primary source.

rows.anchor: §3, §7 · The chronology — and it splits into TWO families (8-event table, step-018 through theory-part-06) ... The corpus typed, verified and carried PROPOSITION-evaluation for ten days — and never once gave REQUIREMENT-evaluation a result space.
rows.statement: Traces eight chronological evaluation events (step-018 Eval(P,K); 025d's Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) via a colliding oplus operator; 025e's EvalRequirement(K,r,C)->Status named-never-defined; a four-document {T,F,U} carry-through 08-29/08-30; s240's independently exhaustively checked strong-Kleene verification with commutativity/associativity/monotonicity proven; s241's necessary-not-sufficient dependency hypothesis sigma=Eval(...); Sat_c's V_Sat={top,bot,U}; theory-part-06's uncodomained EvalReq(K,r,EC,Gamma)) and splits them into two families: PROPOSITION-evaluation (Eval(P,K), Eval(P,E,K,C,pi,...)) with a verified, continuous {T,F,U} codomain and algebraic laws, versus REQUIREMENT-evaluation (Evaluate, EvalRequirement, EvalReq, Sat_c) with an oplus-structured/undefined-Status/none/V_Sat set of incompatible, non-algebraically-verified codomains and no independent computation except Sat_c's later implementation. Concludes the corpus typed, verified and carried proposition-evaluation continuously for ten days while never once giving requirement-evaluation a result space.

rows.anchor: §5 · Identity — EvalRequirement ≟ EvalReq, and both ≟ Eval ... Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) × EvalRequirement(K,r,C) SAME CONCEPT — REFINED ... Eval(P,K) × the requirement family RELATED OBJECT — DIFFERENT SUBJECT ... Eval(P,K)'s {T,F,U} × Sat_c's V_Sat={⊤,⊥,U} SAME OBJECT — STRONG CONTINUITY
rows.statement: Runs four identity tests: EvalRequirement x EvalReq remains IDENTITY UNWITNESSED (unchanged from G-25); Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) x EvalRequirement(K,r,C) is SAME CONCEPT-REFINED (written two minutes apart, 025d 18:31:42 to 025e 18:33:20, same subject, the contract argument retained as EC_G->C); Eval(P,K) versus the whole requirement-evaluation family is RELATED-DIFFERENT-SUBJECT (P is a proposition, r is a requirement -- evaluating a claim is not evaluating a requirement, and no document identifies them); Eval(P,K)'s {T,F,U} and Sat_c's V_Sat={top,bot,U} are SAME OBJECT-STRONG CONTINUITY (same three values, same 'undetermined' third value, an unbroken chain 08-29->08-30->09-02, though with no citation between the endpoints -- continuity is measured, not declared).

rows.anchor: §4 · Distributed completion — what this changes for G-25 ... V_Sat = {⊤,⊥,U} is NOT invented at 09-02. It descends from Eval(P,K) ∈ {T,F,U}, born step-018, Kleene-verified at s240. ⇒ Classification for the three-valued space: B — COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES
rows.statement: Revises G-25's finding of four unreconciled Sat codomains: shows V_Sat={top,bot,U} is NOT an independent 09-02 invention but descends directly from Eval(P,K) in {T,F,U}, born step-018 and algebraically Kleene-verified at s240 -- reclassifying the three-valued space as B (COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES: step-018 supplies connective tables, s240 supplies algebraic verification, Sat_c supplies requirement-class indexing and a body). Notes the 4-valued S_sat and the 9->11 S remain unreconciled with it -- G-25's incomparability result for those two stands untouched.

rows.anchor: §6 · Mathematical typing ... Eval(P,K) → {T,F,U} PROVEN ... that space is strong Kleene, comm./assoc./monotone PROVEN ... V_Sat ≡ {T,F,U} TYPE-CONSTRAINED — no document states the identity ... any codomain for EvalRequirement/EvalReq UNKNOWN, at every point in 10 days
rows.statement: Typing audit: Eval(P,K)->{T,F,U} is PROVEN with connective tables stated; the space being strong Kleene with commutativity/associativity/monotonicity is PROVEN via s240's independent exhaustive check; V_Sat being identical to {T,F,U} is only TYPE-CONSTRAINED (same three values and semantics, but no document ever states the identity explicitly); EvalReq->V remains TYPE-CONSTRAINED (unchanged from G-25); Status=V remains INFERRED and withdrawn; any codomain at all for EvalRequirement/EvalReq is UNKNOWN at every single point across the ten-day history. No TYPE-CONSTRAINED claim was promoted to PROVEN in this pass.

rows.anchor: §7 · The Req → EvalReq → Sat → Determination chain ... The chain is not established end-to-end. Two of six edges are UNWITNESSED/POSSIBLE, and the corpus never draws it as one pipeline.
rows.statement: Tests a six-edge candidate pipeline Req->EvalReq->Sat->Determination for direct evidential support: Req->Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) is DIRECT (025d SS25D.37, r in R_G); Evaluate->EvalRequirement is DIRECT (2-minute gap, same subject); EvalRequirement->EvalReq is UNWITNESSED (10 days, zero citation); EvalReq->Sat is DIRECT (theory-part-06 SS6.18 explicitly composes them); Sat->Determination is only POSSIBLE (Det_r is INSIDE Sat's definition, not downstream of it, and Determination's own birth is in a governance lane, 08-19); Eval(P,K)->Sat_c is only POSSIBLE (the codomain plausibly descends but with no citation). Concludes the full chain is not established end-to-end -- two of six edges are unwitnessed or merely possible, and the corpus never draws the whole thing as one pipeline anywhere.

rows.anchor: §12 · Provenance ... {T,F,U} is the evaluation codomain: ≥3 independent lineages ... requirement-evaluation is never typed: 1 measurement over 265 files + 4 named formulations — not 4 confirmations
rows.statement: Applies senior-statistician lineage-counting discipline: the claim '{T,F,U} is the evaluation codomain' rests on at least 3 genuinely independent lineages (step-018 origin, the verification lane's four 08-29/08-30 documents, and s240's independent computation); the claim 'requirement-evaluation is never typed' is only ONE measurement across 265 files plus four named formulations, explicitly not four independent confirmations.

rows.anchor: §16 · Terminal classification ... proposition-evaluation A — COMPLETE HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION ... the three-valued space B ... requirement-evaluation E — OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED (was: D) ... NOT D: the concept is present and named four times; what is missing is not the concept but a codomain it never had.
rows.statement: Issues final terminal classifications: proposition-evaluation Eval(P,K) = class A (COMPLETE HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION -- birth, evolution, algebraic verification and terminal descendant V_Sat all located); the three-valued space = class B (COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES); requirement-evaluation = class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, corrected from the earlier D -- four formulations, three shared subjects, zero cross-citations, and no result space at any point). Explicitly states requirement-evaluation is NOT class D: the concept is present and named four separate times; what is actually missing is not the concept itself but a codomain it never once received.

rows.anchor: §17 · Gap impact ... EvalReq D WITHDRAWN → E. ... G-25 RE-SCOPED — V_Sat now has an ancestry ... Three codomains unreconciled, not four ... NEW G-27 ... Requirement-evaluation has been named four times in ten days and given a result space zero times — while its sibling proposition-evaluation was typed at birth and algebraically verified. The asymmetry is the finding
rows.statement: Records gap-register impact: EvalReq's D (GENUINE CORPUS GAP) classification is WITHDRAWN and replaced with E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED); G-25 is RE-SCOPED since V_Sat now has a traced ancestry, reducing the unreconciled codomain count from four to three; G-01 is RE-SCOPED since the three-valued space is shown to be the OLDEST member of the evaluation family, not a late narrowing; Det_r remains unchanged, FIREWALL-LIMITED; a NEW gap G-27 is opened naming the asymmetry itself as the finding -- requirement-evaluation has been named four times across ten days and given a result space zero times, while its sibling proposition-evaluation was typed at birth and algebraically verified.

rows.anchor: §15 · Negative-history ... Result: NOTATION ABSENT · CONCEPT CONTINUES · DEFINED IN MULTIPLE STAGES — not GENUINE CORPUS GAP. step-018 is NOT YET READ (backfill debt)
rows.statement: Confirms the exhaustive negative-history search (265 interval files x 11 variant patterns, both spellings, plus the whole non-firewalled corpus for {T,F,U} and Evaluate(...) argument shapes) yields the correct classification NOTATION ABSENT / CONCEPT CONTINUES / DEFINED IN MULTIPLE STAGES, not GENUINE CORPUS GAP. Explicitly flags step-018 itself as NOT YET READ at primary source (a backfill debt), with its content here relying entirely on the verification lane's citing register. Confirms firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no codomain supplied, no family merged.

lexical.anchor: §2 Corpus census — and a defect in my own first pass ... My first census reported 224 missing. A greedy regex ... Re-run with a first-match search: 3 missing, agreeing with the corpus's own four independent records.

formal.anchor: §6 · Mathematical typing ... Eval(P,K) → {T,F,U} PROVEN ... that space is strong Kleene, comm./assoc./monotone PROVEN ... V_Sat ≡ {T,F,U} TYPE-CONSTRAINED — no document states the identity ... any codomain for EvalRequirement/EvalReq UNKNOWN, at every point in 10 days

governance.anchor: §18 · Terminal classification (Ω class E, Sat/EvalReq class C, Determination class E, Update class E, K_t class B, the interval itself class A structural)

rationale_evidence.anchor: The silences are the structure ... The interval is not gradual evolution. It is: everything introduced in one morning, then 100–157 files of near-total silence, then a return in the 183–267 band. ... The terminal staircase ... they die one per step, at the very end
rationale_evidence.statement: Measures each object's longest silence gap in files: Gamma 157 files (s053->s197), Omega 155 files (s031->s186-pre), EC 135 (s117->s238), Delta_t 117 (s047->s155a), tau 112 (s074->s188), Zero 74 (s094->recovery doc). Concludes the interval's shape is NOT gradual evolution but a sharp pattern: everything introduced in one morning, then a 100-157 file near-total silence, then a return in the 183-267 band. Also finds a 'terminal staircase' where nine objects die one per step in sequence near the end of the interval (Req s234, Delta_t s240, EC s251, Determination s252, tau s263, Zero s264, K_t s265, Omega s266, Gamma s267).

rationale_evidence.anchor: And yet continuity was declared, 41 seconds later ... step-025z ... 2026-08-28 10:13:25 ... step-026 ... 41 seconds later ... 'We continue from 25Z.' ... Continuity is DECLARED by name, 41 seconds later — and the apparatus is not CARRIED. Declaration ≠ transmission.
rationale_evidence.statement: Finds the last 025-series document (step-025z) was written 2026-08-28 10:13:25, and step-026 was written just 41 seconds later, with step-026's third line explicitly stating 'We continue from 25Z.' Concludes continuity is declared by name almost immediately, yet none of the 025 apparatus is actually carried forward -- establishing the general principle that declaration does not equal transmission. Notes in passing a step-number homonym found incidentally: a different, unrelated step-026 document exists dated 2026-08-27 16:29:19 (a work-programme document), one day earlier, same step number, unrelated content.

rationale_evidence.anchor: §12–13 · The re-founding hypothesis — tested on all six candidates ... NOT ONE DECLARES A RESTART. Every discontinuity in this corpus is MEASURED, never DECLARED.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests all six previously-labeled re-founding candidates against their own opening words: 026 ('we continue from 25Z') = CONTINUITY DECLARED; 031 ('step 31 is the first deliberate attempt to turn that architecture into a formal system') = CONTINUITY, a MODE CHANGE not a restart; 183-pre ('substantially aligned... but some later formulations should NOT be promoted') = SELECTIVE REJECTION of a named subset; 186-pre ('construct the mathematics around the distinctions we have already established') = CONTINUITY; 230 ('determine whether the apparently large architecture can be generated from a small kernel') = REDUCTION of the existing architecture; 262 ('we can now continue, but there is an important correction to the previous Step 261 conclusion') = CORRECTION; and the 09-06 rewrite (via G-25) = SELECTIVE INHERITANCE. Concludes not one of the six candidates declares a restart -- every discontinuity in this corpus is measured (by an outside investigator finding lost apparatus) rather than declared (by the author announcing a break).

rationale_evidence.anchor: §16 · The ten questions Q1–Q10 (full table)
rationale_evidence.statement: Answers ten structured research questions about the interval: Q1 the 025 apparatus did not cross (0 in 265 files, cited once as a table row 41 seconds after continuity was declared); Q2 Omega/tau/K_t/Zero/EC/Delta_t/Gamma/Req are all born inside the interval (inherited from nothing) while Determination is genuinely inherited from a governance lane; Q3 the whole evaluation/satisfaction family was independently re-derived, clearest case Determination's 155a formalization vs Det_r; Q4 no definition inside the interval completes an earlier one -- all distributed-completeness successes cross OUT of the interval; Q5 apparent gaps (Omega:W->O, EvalReq's codomain-name, S_sat) were all resolved from OUTSIDE the interval; Q6 genuine type changes found in Update (10 signatures), Omega (5 senses), Sat (4 codomains); Q7 homonyms/identity-unwitnessed cases include Omega x5, Update x10, Gamma, Determination (governance vs mathematical), and step-026 itself (two documents, one number, a day apart); Q8 K-formulation origins traced (K_t s028; K_v1 7-tuple at 031; K_v2 6-tuple only in an s155-156 recovery doc quoting 'the earlier model'; K_v3 (A,R) from outside the interval); Q9 per-object silence/activity counts (Sat and EvalReq: ZERO occurrences in the entire interval); Q10 three carry-forward lessons: declared continuity != transmitted apparatus, the terminal staircase pattern, and the inherited codomain defect across three eras.

rationale_evidence.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
rationale_evidence.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Concludes a gap was opened for an object the corpus had already defined three days earlier, then closed by 'recovering' it -- the corpus does not record this as a loss, it records it as a discovery. Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

rationale_evidence.anchor: And precisely which form survived ... Of 241 satisf* occurrences sampled: 83 in technical context, 158 prose. ... What survived is satisfaction as a PREDICATE. What was lost is satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.
rationale_evidence.statement: Samples 241 'satisf*' occurrences (83 technical, 158 prose) and verifies at ten specific steps (s070,079,081,086,091,092,095,097,098,101) that the surviving technical usage is uniformly an unformalised predicate ('the rule is satisfied', 'invariants remain satisfied') rather than the 025-series typed function Satisfied(K,r,EC) with three typed arguments and a result space S(9->10->11). Concludes precisely what survived was satisfaction AS A PREDICATE; what was lost was satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.

rationale_evidence.anchor: §7 · The Req → EvalReq → Sat → Determination chain ... The chain is not established end-to-end. Two of six edges are UNWITNESSED/POSSIBLE, and the corpus never draws it as one pipeline.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests a six-edge candidate pipeline Req->EvalReq->Sat->Determination for direct evidential support: Req->Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) is DIRECT (025d SS25D.37, r in R_G); Evaluate->EvalRequirement is DIRECT (2-minute gap, same subject); EvalRequirement->EvalReq is UNWITNESSED (10 days, zero citation); EvalReq->Sat is DIRECT (theory-part-06 SS6.18 explicitly composes them); Sat->Determination is only POSSIBLE (Det_r is INSIDE Sat's definition, not downstream of it, and Determination's own birth is in a governance lane, 08-19); Eval(P,K)->Sat_c is only POSSIBLE (the codomain plausibly descends but with no citation). Concludes the full chain is not established end-to-end -- two of six edges are unwitnessed or merely possible, and the corpus never draws the whole thing as one pipeline anywhere.

sources.note: Candidate research object: a transition event at which an inquiry's applicable closure conditions become satisfied, sitting between epistemic interaction and the successor state K_{t+1}; explicitly not yet established as required.

rows.anchor: [PROP] A successful epistemic inquiry may contain a transition event at which its applicable closure conditions become satisfied. Candidate: ClosureEvent(Q,t) ... But we have not established that KnowledgeOS requires such an event. That needs an experiment.
rows.statement: Proposes the candidate object ClosureEvent(Q,t), sitting between the epistemic-interaction process and the resulting successor state (K_t -> Inquiry -> EpistemicInteraction -> ClosureEvent -> K_{t+1}), explicitly not yet established as required by KnowledgeOS and flagged as needing a dedicated experiment.

rows.anchor: Case A: No one investigated. Case B: Evidence insufficient. Case C: Evidence contradictory. Case D: Theory cannot evaluate the requirement. Case E: Inquiry genuinely closed. All of these could superficially collapse into some generic 'not known yet.' But they are structurally different.
rows.statement: Connects to Experiment G's finding that EVal={T,F,U} is insufficient: five structurally distinct cases (no investigation, insufficient evidence, contradictory evidence, theory cannot evaluate, genuinely closed) could all superficially collapse into a generic 'not known yet' but must be kept distinct, yielding Closure != Evaluation Value and ClosureStatus != EpistemicTruth.

rows.anchor: This metaphor must not currently be used to establish: A new KnowledgeOS primitive called Orgasm / A kernel operator / Orgasm = Reconciliation / A new truth value / Zero = closure (refuted) / Closure = knowledge (not established) / Knowledge = truth (already separated) / Proposal/Challenge as DDD aggregates (too early) / Two agents as a required architecture (not supported).
rows.statement: Explicit scope-limiting ruling on what the sexual-metaphor document does NOT establish: no new primitive 'Orgasm', no kernel operator, no Orgasm=Reconciliation equation, no new truth value, Zero=closure is refuted as oversimplification, Closure=Knowledge is unestablished, Knowledge=Truth remains separated, Proposal/Challenge as DDD aggregates is premature, and a required two-agent architecture is unsupported.

rows.anchor: I would therefore NOT immediately create 'Epistemic Orgasm.' I would preserve it as a source metaphor/hypothesis, but create the research abstraction: Epistemic Closure Event ... Then test: Proposal->Challenge->Evidence->Assessment->Reconciliation->ClosureEvent->SuccessorState ... Can Closure Event be distinguished from reconciliation, determination, knowledge attribution, truth, and Zero closure?
rows.statement: Governance decision: retain 'epistemic orgasm' only as a source metaphor, formalize the research abstraction Epistemic Closure Event, and pose the critical experiment as whether Closure Event can be distinguished from reconciliation, determination, knowledge attribution, truth, and Zero closure -- if yes the metaphor generated a real theoretical distinction, if no it is merely a colorful redescription.

rows.anchor: I would now insert this after the Zero Boundary work, not before it ... New candidate branch: After Boundary semantics become sufficiently stable: Epistemic Interaction / Closure Event experiment. Then ask whether it actually adds explanatory power.
rows.statement: Revises the research TODO sequence to Zero->Boundary->Inquiry->Interaction->Evaluation->Reconciliation->Closure?->Successor State, inserting the Epistemic Interaction/Closure Event experiment after Zero Boundary work stabilizes rather than before, with Closure deliberately left unresolved pending that experiment.

rows.anchor: Suppose K_t is determined. We declare Orgasm_t. Then new evidence arrives E_{t+1} and invalidates the determination. ... The metaphor survives if Orgasm_t is understood as closure at time t. It fails if orgasm means permanently complete knowledge. Therefore: EpistemicOrgasm_t must be temporal and revisable.
rows.statement: Falsification test: if a determination is declared closed (Orgasm_t) and later evidence invalidates it (K_{t+1}!=K_t), the ClosureEvent metaphor survives only if understood as closure-at-time-t (temporal and revisable), and fails if it means permanently complete knowledge.

rows.anchor: An epistemic system may contain a distinct closure event in which a proposal/challenge process has reached a sufficiently reconciled and inquiry-adequate condition, producing a new epistemic state, without identifying that event with Zero, Truth, Determination, or Knowledge. ... The formal candidate name should be: EpistemicClosureEvent.
rows.statement: States the formal research question: can a distinct EpistemicClosureEvent (formal name, replacing the metaphorical 'Orgasm' label) be identified where a proposal/challenge process reaches sufficient reconciliation and inquiry-adequacy, producing a new epistemic state, without collapsing into Zero, Truth, Determination, or Knowledge?

rows.anchor: Model A - Closure as state: Closed_t(K). Model B - Closure as transition event: ClosureEvent_t: K_t -> K_(t+1). ... If closure can later be revised, determine whether ClosureEvent_t is historical and irreversible as an event, while K_(t+1) remains revisable.
rows.statement: Requires testing two competing formal models of closure -- Model A, closure as a state predicate Closed_t(K); Model B, closure as a transition event ClosureEvent_t: K_t -> K_{t+1} -- and, if closure can later be revised, whether the event itself remains historical/irreversible while the resulting state K_{t+1} remains revisable (HistoricalClosure != CurrentClosure; StateRevision != EventDeletion).

rows.anchor: A question can be closed for inquiry Q while another inquiry Q' exposes additional gaps. ... Closure(Q,t) = true, ZeroLens(K_t,Q') ≠ empty. If this is possible, record it as evidence that closure is inquiry-relative and does not imply global completeness.
rows.statement: Critical Zero-separation test: whether Closure(Q,t)=true can coexist with ZeroLens(K_t,Q')!=empty for a different inquiry Q', which if possible would establish that closure is inquiry-relative and does not imply global completeness.

rows.anchor: Test: ClosureEvent ≠ KnowledgeAttribution and Determination ≠ KnowledgeAttribution. Construct false-but-well-supported proposals. If closure occurs without truth, this must NOT automatically produce knowledge. Record: [EXP] Closure can be epistemically successful without being factive knowledge.
rows.statement: Requires testing ClosureEvent!=KnowledgeAttribution and Determination!=KnowledgeAttribution via constructed false-but-well-supported proposals; if closure occurs without truth this must not automatically produce knowledge, recordable only if witnessed as [EXP] closure can be epistemically successful without being factive knowledge.

rows.anchor: Does an epistemic system contain a distinct closure event ... without identifying that event with Zero, Truth, Determination or Knowledge? Answer: yes for the distinctions, no for the primitiveness. All five conditions separate; the event itself is derivable as a predicate but carries one thing no predicate does.
rows.statement: Headline answer to the KR-CLOSURE research question: yes for the distinctions (Balanced/Reconciled/Determined/Known/Closed all separate), no for primitiveness (the closure event is derivable as a predicate); the event nonetheless carries something no predicate carries -- historical irreversibility.

rows.anchor: {Balanced, Reconciled, Determined, Known, Closed} ... 10 of 10 distinguishable. Two directed cells initially had no witness; both were investigated rather than reported as implications.
rows.statement: The pairwise distinction matrix over {Balanced, Reconciled, Determined, Known, Closed} yields 10 of 10 pairs distinguishable by constructed witness; two directed cells (Balanced-and-not-Reconciled, Known-and-not-Determined) initially lacked a witness and were investigated rather than defaulted to an implication.

experiment.hypothesis: Balanced, Reconciled, Determined, Known, Closed are five formally distinct epistemic conditions
experiment.setup: Construct witness states for each of the 10 unordered pairs in both directions where possible
experiment.inputs: named witness states w_bal_only, w_rec_not_bal, w_det_not_rec, w_det_not_known, w_known_not_closed, w_closed_not_det
experiment.method: For each pair attempt to construct a state where one condition holds and the other does not
experiment.result: 10/10 pairs distinguishable; two initially-missing directed witnesses were resolved (one a catalogue gap, one policy-relative)
experiment.interpretation: the five conditions are genuinely formally distinct, not merely differently named
experiment.conclusion: [EXP]

rows.anchor: Balanced ∧ ¬Reconciled -- a catalogue gap, not an implication. Negative-control case 2 (support .8 + contradict .8) is the witness: balanced, not reconciled. Repaired.
rows.statement: The missing Balanced-and-not-Reconciled witness was a catalogue gap rather than a genuine implication: negative-control case 2 (support 0.8 + contradict 0.8) supplies it (balanced, not reconciled) once identified.

rows.anchor: Known ∧ ¬Determined -- constructible, but forbidden by the attribution policy. ... [EXP] Known ⇒ Determined is policy-relative, not conceptual. It is a property of Γ's attribution policy, and it disappears when the policy is relaxed.
rows.statement: [EXP]: Known=>Determined is policy-relative, not conceptual -- a Known-without-Determined state is constructible but forbidden under the 'justified-unique' attribution policy while reachable under 'justified-any' (confirmed by the -C policy sweep), so the apparent implication is a property of Gamma's attribution policy, not a conceptual necessity.

rows.anchor: A -- Closed_t(K) as a state: true at t, false after new evidence at t+1. B -- ClosureEvent_t: K_t -> K_{t+1}: occurred at t, still occurred after t+1. Closure-as-state is refuted by temporal revision; closure-as-event is not. ... This does not make the event permanent truth ... a system can close on a falsehood.
rows.statement: [EXP]: closure-as-state (Closed_t(K)) is refuted by temporal revision (true at t, false after new evidence at t+1), while closure-as-event (ClosureEvent_t: K_t->K_{t+1}) survives (occurred at t, still occurred after t+1) -- the event is a historical fact remaining true of the past even though K_{t+1} remains revisable; this does not make the event permanent truth, since a system can close on a falsehood (the B1 factivity counterexample still stands).

experiment.hypothesis: Closure can be modeled either as a state predicate or as a transition event
experiment.setup: Compare Model A Closed_t(K) vs Model B ClosureEvent_t:K_t->K_{t+1} under temporal revision (new evidence arriving at t+1)
experiment.inputs: a closed state at t and new contradicting evidence at t+1
experiment.method: Evaluate both models' truth value at t and after t+1
experiment.result: Model A flips to false after revision; Model B remains true (the event occurred)
experiment.interpretation: closure must be modeled as an event, not a state, to preserve historical record under revision
experiment.limitations: does not establish the event as permanently true/factive
experiment.conclusion: [EXP]

rows.anchor: ClosureEvent ... DERIVABLE AS A PREDICATE -- Determined ∧ Adequate. But §4 shows it carries a historical record that neither conjunct carries. So: derivable as a predicate, not as an event [PROP]. ... The predicate adds nothing; the event adds irreversibility. Whether irreversibility is kernel structure or an audit-log concern is [OPEN] -- and it is a DDD question, not a mathematical one.
rows.statement: [PROP]/[OPEN]: ClosureEvent is derivable as a predicate (Determined AND Adequate) but that predicate carries no historical record, while the event does -- so ClosureEvent is derivable as a predicate but not as an event; whether the irreversibility the event carries is kernel structure or merely an audit-log concern is left [OPEN] as a DDD boundary question (History vs Kernel), not a mathematical one.

rows.anchor: Decide whether event-irreversibility is kernel structure or an audit concern. It is the only thing ClosureEvent contributes that its defining conjunction does not, and the question is a DDD boundary question -- History vs Kernel -- not a mathematical one. It is also cheap: it needs no new simulation, only a context-map decision.
rows.statement: Recommended next step: decide, as a DDD context-map decision (History vs Kernel boundary) rather than a new simulation, whether ClosureEvent's irreversibility belongs to kernel structure or is merely an audit-log concern -- the only contribution ClosureEvent makes beyond its defining conjunction (Determined AND Adequate).

rows.anchor: I currently lean strongly toward: ClosureEvent ∈ History, not Kernel, because the experiment found ClosureEvent as predicate is derivable from Determined ∧ Adequate, while the additional property is 'this closure occurred at t.' That sounds fundamentally historical.
rows.statement: Preliminary position: ClosureEvent likely belongs to History, not Kernel, since the derivable predicate (Determined AND Adequate) is fully kernel-explicable while the additional property ('this closure occurred at t') is fundamentally historical -- Closed(K_t,Q) as a current epistemic predicate vs ClosureEvent(t,Q,K_t,K_{t+1}) as a historical transition record.

rows.anchor: Current State ≠ Historical Transition and therefore: K_t ≠ History_{≤t}. History records what happened to the epistemic state, not necessarily what the current epistemic state is. ... irreversibility may belong to event identity, not epistemic computation.
rows.statement: Proposes a general principle: Current State != Historical Transition, hence K_t != History_{<=t} -- history records what happened to the epistemic state, not what the current state is; the kernel operates on state/transition semantics while history preserves the fact that a transition occurred, so irreversibility may belong to event identity rather than epistemic computation.

rows.anchor: A -- Pure audit: ClosureEvent ∈ Audit/History. The kernel does not need to know that closure happened. B -- Domain history: ClosureEvent ∈ DomainHistory. ... C -- Kernel structure: ClosureEvent ∈ 𝒦. ... I think C is currently unlikely, but we should not assume A versus B.
rows.statement: Refines the History-vs-Kernel question into three possibilities for where ClosureEvent belongs: (A) pure audit/infrastructure history the kernel need not know about, (B) domain history -- a genuine domain event because later domain behavior may depend on it, (C) kernel structure itself; judges C currently unlikely but declines to assume between A and B.

rows.anchor: if a later epistemic operation needs to distinguish 'This proposition has never been closed' from 'This proposition was closed and subsequently reopened/revised,' then the historical event has domain meaning, even though it still need not be kernel power. That would favor: ClosureEvent ∈ Domain History rather than merely an infrastructure audit log.
rows.statement: Argues for Domain History over pure audit: if any later epistemic operation must distinguish 'never closed' from 'closed and subsequently reopened/revised', the historical closure event carries domain meaning even though it need not be kernel power.

rows.anchor: operations run (Determine, Revise, Reject, OpenHypothesisSpace): 0 produce differing output. static: kernel transitions that READ E.history: 0. kernel transitions that WRITE E.history: 2 -- Revise, Supersede. [NEG] Hypothesis C is REFUTED. The kernel neither reads history nor behaves differently because of it. History in this implementation is write-only from the kernel's side.
rows.statement: [NEG]: Hypothesis C (ClosureEvent in Kernel) is refuted -- running Determine/Revise/Reject/OpenHypothesisSpace against both H_closed and H_never produces zero differing outputs; a static scan finds zero kernel transitions read E.history while two (Revise, Supersede) write it, establishing history as write-only from the kernel's side in this implementation.

experiment.hypothesis: ClosureEvent's irreversibility requires kernel-level event semantics (Hypothesis C)
experiment.setup: Two epistemic states with identical current content and different histories (H_closed containing a ClosureEvent, H_never not)
experiment.assumptions: the kernel operation set is Determine, Revise, Reject, OpenHypothesisSpace
experiment.inputs: H_closed and H_never states
experiment.method: Run each kernel operation against both states and compare outputs; statically scan kernel transitions for reads/writes of E.history
experiment.result: 0 operations produce differing output; 0 kernel transitions read E.history; 2 (Revise, Supersede) write it
experiment.interpretation: the kernel is architecturally indifferent to closure history; history is write-only from the kernel's perspective
experiment.limitations: confined to the current theory's operation set and implementation
experiment.conclusion: [NEG] Hypothesis C refuted

rows.anchor: C -- REFUTED -- 0 reads, 0 behavioural differences. B -- AVAILABLE BUT UNEXERCISED -- no consumer in theory or corpus; a design option [OPEN]. A -- ESTABLISHED for the current theory -- a write-only preservation duty [EXP]. ... ClosureEvent ∈ History, not Kernel holds. But the reason is not that closure is 'fundamentally historical' -- it is that nothing consumes it.
rows.statement: Final verdict: Hypothesis C is REFUTED (0 reads, 0 behavioral differences); Hypothesis B is AVAILABLE BUT UNEXERCISED (no consumer exists; a design option, [OPEN]); Hypothesis A is ESTABLISHED for the current theory as a write-only preservation duty, [EXP]. Confirms S2441's preliminary direction (ClosureEvent in History, not Kernel) but sharpens the reason: not that closure is 'fundamentally historical' but that nothing currently consumes it -- introducing a consumer would make B true without making ClosureEvent kernel power.

rows.anchor: 'Reconciliation = the orgasm.' But KR-CLOSURE showed: Reconciliation ≠ ClosureEvent. ... Reconciliation was experimentally found to be derivable from typed argument relations, whereas the historical event carries something extra. ... Orgasm ≈ EpistemicClosureEvent only as an analogy, not an identity.
rows.statement: Corrects the source document's 'Reconciliation=Orgasm' using the KR-CLOSURE experimental result (S2440): Reconciliation!=ClosureEvent because Reconciliation is derivable from typed argument relations while ClosureEvent-as-event carries the extra historical/irreversibility property; Orgasm should be treated as an analogy for EpistemicClosureEvent, not an identity, and Reconciliation is at most a possible precursor/condition of closure.

rows.anchor: 'Knowledge = offspring' and even 'Truth = offspring.' Both should be rejected ... because we have already demonstrated that closure can occur on a falsehood. ... ClosureEvent ⇏ Truth and ClosureEvent ⇏ Knowledge. The better interpretation is: Offspring ≈ NewEpistemicState rather than: Offspring = Knowledge.
rows.statement: Rejects the source document's Knowledge=offspring and Truth=offspring using the standing factivity counterexample (closure can occur on a falsehood, preserved by the KR-CLOSURE experiment): ClosureEvent does not imply Truth and does not imply Knowledge; the offspring is better interpreted as the NewEpistemicState (interaction->transformation->new state), not automatically knowledge or truth.

rows.anchor: Offspring ≈ New Epistemic State. ... The 'offspring' is the new configuration produced by the inquiry process. It may contain: knowledge, hypotheses, uncertainty, unresolved questions, rejected propositions, conflicts, revised beliefs. Therefore: New State ≠ Knowledge and New State ≠ Truth.
rows.statement: Reaffirms Offspring~NewEpistemicState (not automatically Knowledge or Truth), enumerating what the new state may actually contain: knowledge, hypotheses, uncertainty, unresolved questions, rejected propositions, conflicts, or revised beliefs.

rows.anchor: The document's phrase 'proposer of truth' is also too strong. The active principle can propose a candidate for truth; it cannot bring truth into existence.
rows.statement: Rejects the source document's 'proposer of truth' phrasing: the active/Linga principle can propose a candidate for truth but cannot bring truth into existence -- reinforcing Offspring!=Truth.

rows.anchor: Do not immediately turn those conceptual distinctions into domain objects. Instead ask: What richer structure contains the distinction between proposal, challenge, evidence, reconciliation and closure? ... The document explicitly moves Yoni toward a metaphor for a structured candidate space rather than a KnowledgeOS object.
rows.statement: Reinterprets the Proposal/Challenge/Evidence/Reconciliation/Closure metaphor through the projection framework: rather than turning these directly into domain objects, ask what richer structure contains the distinction and which projections preserve or destroy it, keeping the sexual/Yoni metaphor as an external lens over a structured candidate space.

rows.anchor: Do not add ClosureEvent because the metaphor suggests it. Determine whether the richer transition structure contains a distinction that existing projections cannot represent. That is a much stronger test.
rows.statement: Applies the projection framework to ClosureEvent: rather than adding it because the metaphor suggests it, determine whether the richer transition structure contains a distinction existing projections cannot represent -- a stronger admission test than metaphorical plausibility.

rows.anchor: > **What are the exact semantics of state transition?**
rows.statement: TODO Group E (δ, state transition): what are the exact semantics of δ? Sub-todos E1-E4: define the signature δ(K,o,Γ)→K', define transition causes (observation/determination/decision/action/revision/retraction/supersession), define transition composition, define closure semantics (ClosureEvent≠ClosureState).

rows.anchor: > Lifecycle should investigate **relations/events**, not automatically create a state machine. ClosureEvent ≠ ClosureState.
rows.statement: Restates (from the prior Epistemic Closure Event track) that lifecycle/retirement should be modeled via relations/events rather than assumed to require a state machine, reaffirming ClosureEvent≠ClosureState.

rows.anchor: So lifecycle should investigate **relations/events**, not automatically create a state machine.
rows.statement: Restates ClosureEvent≠ClosureState as grounds for requiring lifecycle/retirement to be modeled as relations/events rather than assumed to be a state machine.

lexical.anchor: [PROP] A successful epistemic inquiry may contain a transition event at which its applicable closure conditions become satisfied. Candidate: ClosureEvent(Q,t) ... But we have not established that KnowledgeOS requires such an event. That needs an experiment.

operational.anchor: Model A - Closure as state: Closed_t(K). Model B - Closure as transition event: ClosureEvent_t: K_t -> K_(t+1). ... If closure can later be revised, determine whether ClosureEvent_t is historical and irreversible as an event, while K_(t+1) remains revisable.

governance.anchor: This metaphor must not currently be used to establish: A new KnowledgeOS primitive called Orgasm / A kernel operator / Orgasm = Reconciliation / A new truth value / Zero = closure (refuted) / Closure = knowledge (not established) / Knowledge = truth (already separated) / Proposal/Challenge as DDD aggregates (too early) / Two agents as a required architecture (not supported).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Case A: No one investigated. Case B: Evidence insufficient. Case C: Evidence contradictory. Case D: Theory cannot evaluate the requirement. Case E: Inquiry genuinely closed. All of these could superficially collapse into some generic 'not known yet.' But they are structurally different.
rationale_evidence.statement: Connects to Experiment G's finding that EVal={T,F,U} is insufficient: five structurally distinct cases (no investigation, insufficient evidence, contradictory evidence, theory cannot evaluate, genuinely closed) could all superficially collapse into a generic 'not known yet' but must be kept distinct, yielding Closure != Evaluation Value and ClosureStatus != EpistemicTruth.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Suppose K_t is determined. We declare Orgasm_t. Then new evidence arrives E_{t+1} and invalidates the determination. ... The metaphor survives if Orgasm_t is understood as closure at time t. It fails if orgasm means permanently complete knowledge. Therefore: EpistemicOrgasm_t must be temporal and revisable.
rationale_evidence.statement: Falsification test: if a determination is declared closed (Orgasm_t) and later evidence invalidates it (K_{t+1}!=K_t), the ClosureEvent metaphor survives only if understood as closure-at-time-t (temporal and revisable), and fails if it means permanently complete knowledge.

rationale_evidence.anchor: I currently lean strongly toward: ClosureEvent ∈ History, not Kernel, because the experiment found ClosureEvent as predicate is derivable from Determined ∧ Adequate, while the additional property is 'this closure occurred at t.' That sounds fundamentally historical.
rationale_evidence.statement: Preliminary position: ClosureEvent likely belongs to History, not Kernel, since the derivable predicate (Determined AND Adequate) is fully kernel-explicable while the additional property ('this closure occurred at t') is fundamentally historical -- Closed(K_t,Q) as a current epistemic predicate vs ClosureEvent(t,Q,K_t,K_{t+1}) as a historical transition record.

rationale_evidence.anchor: if a later epistemic operation needs to distinguish 'This proposition has never been closed' from 'This proposition was closed and subsequently reopened/revised,' then the historical event has domain meaning, even though it still need not be kernel power. That would favor: ClosureEvent ∈ Domain History rather than merely an infrastructure audit log.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues for Domain History over pure audit: if any later epistemic operation must distinguish 'never closed' from 'closed and subsequently reopened/revised', the historical closure event carries domain meaning even though it need not be kernel power.
