sources.note: A fully self-contained formal sub-theory of the Knowledge Gap, developed the same day as and explicitly building on this batch's v1.0 Definitions/Axioms/Theorems document (reusing its DEF-21/DEF-22/THM-4 Gap/Zero apparatus but developing it into its own DEF-G1/DEF-G2/THM-G1..G6 numbering): rejects Delta=I-K as mathematically too strong, defines the Gap as the set of unsatisfied epistemic requirements Delta_t={r in R_t : Sat(K_t,r)=0} with no arithmetic/vector-space assumption; derives Zero as the bottom element of the gap lattice (P(R_t),subseteq); introduces a ten-class gap taxonomy (Coverage/Value/Uncertainty/Evidence-Warrant/Contradiction/Model/Observability/Temporal-Staleness/Identity-Referential/Representation gaps); a positive-deficit/negative-conflict/epistemic-insufficiency three-way reduction; a three-level Semantic->Typed->Numerical gap hierarchy with a derived weighted gap functional G(K_t,EC_t) and the Zero-equivalence theorem G=0 iff Delta_t=empty (THM-G3); a partial order K_{t+1} >=_EC K_t iff Delta_{t+1} subseteq Delta_t with a proven gap-reduction theorem (THM-G2); a contract-invariance theorem (THM-G4, gap comparison requires contract compatibility, preventing 'moving the goalposts'); the gap-increase-does-not-imply-knowledge-decrease result (an investigation can enlarge the known gap while improving epistemic honesty); a gap-composition/algebra structure (P(R),Sat,Type,union,subseteq); reformalized Lord/Sarathi roles as Gap->Proposal->Decision; a Gap Control theorem (THM-G5); a two-measure Progress vector (Adequacy, GapObservability, Warrant, UncertaintyReduction, ModelAdequacy); a Gap Decomposition theorem (THM-G6, non-exclusive overlapping gap classes); and a closing ten-item explicitly OPEN list. Possibly the same milestone object as knowledgeos-theory-v1-0-definitions-axioms-theorems (a companion/extension chapter of the same v1.0 specification), possibly a distinct standalone artifact -- not resolved within this batch.

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Gap should not initially be defined as I_t-K_t, because K_t and I_t are generally heterogeneous semantic objects and may not live in a vector space. Instead, the fundamental Gap is a **set of unsatisfied epistemic requirements**.
rows.statement: States the file's central correction: the Gap must not be initially defined as I_t-K_t (K_t and I_t are heterogeneous semantic objects that may not live in a vector space); the fundamental Gap is instead a set of unsatisfied epistemic requirements, with numerical gap measures derived from that set only once additional structure (weights, costs, probabilities, metrics, utilities) is explicitly supplied.

rows.anchor: I=[1,1,1,1], K_t=[1,0.8,0.4,0]. Then: I-K_t=[0,0.2,0.6,1]. ... what do the values mean? The 0.2 might mean: insufficient evidence, probability of correctness, measurement uncertainty, incomplete coverage, stale information, disagreement between sources. ... Numerical difference != Epistemic Gap in general.
rows.statement: Gives a worked numerical counterexample (I=[1,1,1,1], K_t=[1,0.8,0.4,0], I-K_t=[0,0.2,0.6,1]) showing the resulting numbers are semantically ambiguous (0.2 could mean insufficient evidence, probability of correctness, measurement uncertainty, incomplete coverage, staleness, or source disagreement), establishing Numerical difference != Epistemic Gap in general -- valid only once the semantics and scale of every coordinate is established.

rows.anchor: $$r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity)$$ ... $$I_t=\mathcal R_t$$ semantically. ... The Ideal State is therefore **the set of epistemically relevant requirements**. ... knowledge sufficient for the declared purpose.
rows.statement: Defines a formal Epistemic Requirement r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity) and re-derives the Ideal State semantically as I_t = R_t, the set of epistemically relevant requirements (knowledge sufficient for the declared purpose), rather than a mysterious perfect object.

rows.anchor: [DEF-G1] Epistemic Gap: $$\Delta_t=\{r\in\mathcal R_t: Sat(K_t,r)=0\}.$$ ... It does not require: subtraction, Euclidean geometry, probability, vectors, finite dimensionality. That makes it much more general.
rows.statement: [DEF-G1] States the fundamental Gap Definition: Delta_t = {r in R_t : Sat(K_t,r)=0}, the set of currently unsatisfied epistemic requirements, requiring no subtraction, Euclidean geometry, probability, vectors, or finite dimensionality -- making it substantially more general than any arithmetic-difference formulation.

rows.anchor: [DEF-G2] Zero_t iff Delta_t=empty. ... [THM-G1] ... Proof: By definition, Delta_t=empty iff there exists no requirement unsatisfied. Therefore every requirement is satisfied ... which is exactly K_t|=EC_t.
rows.statement: [DEF-G2]/[THM-G1] Formalizes Zero_t iff Delta_t=empty iff (for all r in R_t, Sat(K_t,r)=1) iff K_t models EC_t, with an explicit proof by direct definitional unfolding -- much stronger than saying Zero is 'distance zero.'

rows.anchor: G1 Coverage Gap ... purest form of missing knowledge. G2 Value Gap: Dimension(r) exists AND Value_Kt(r)=bottom. Unknown Value != Unknown Dimension. G3 Uncertainty Gap: P(p|E,C,M) below required threshold. G4 Evidence/Warrant Gap: Having an answer != Having justified knowledge.
rows.statement: Defines the first four of ten gap classes: G1 Coverage Gap (required knowledge item not established at all, the purest missing-knowledge case); G2 Value Gap (dimension known but value unknown, formalized as Dimension(r) exists AND Value_Kt(r)=bottom, giving Unknown Value != Unknown Dimension); G3 Uncertainty Gap (a claim exists but its probability falls below the contract's required threshold); G4 Evidence/Warrant Gap (a claim exists but its evidence is absent or below the required strength threshold, giving Having an answer != Having justified knowledge).

rows.anchor: G5 Contradiction Gap: Conflict(p,not p)=1 ... The KnowledgeOS state should not silently select one. G6 Model Gap: observations sufficient for correlation, insufficient for causal determination. G7 Observability Gap: Observable(r,K_t)=0 ... must not automatically become Value(r)=False.
rows.statement: Defines gap classes G5-G7: G5 Contradiction Gap (two admissible sources produce p and not-p; KnowledgeOS must represent Conflict(p,not-p) rather than silently selecting one, worked with a Nexus-version-disagreement example); G6 Model Gap (facts known but the required interpretive model, e.g. causal vs correlational, is inadequate, drawn from the causal/statistical experiments); G7 Observability Gap (Observable(r,K_t)=0 because the required observation is currently unavailable, e.g. no network access to check a firewall rule -- must not automatically collapse into Value(r)=False).

rows.anchor: G8 Temporal/Staleness Gap: Age(p)>TTL_EC ... Superseded != False. G9 Identity/Referential Gap: the required claim cannot be reliably attached to the required domain identity. Identity != State. G10 Representation Gap: Expressible_r(p)=0 ... different representation algebras can produce different apparent primitive counts.
rows.statement: Defines gap classes G8-G10: G8 Temporal/Staleness Gap (Age(p) exceeds the contract's TTL, giving Superseded != False); G9 Identity/Referential Gap (a true proposition that cannot be reliably attached to the required domain identity is unusable for the inquiry, giving Identity != State); G10 Representation Gap (Expressible_r(p)=0, the current representation cannot express a required semantic distinction -- connected explicitly to the kernel experiments' finding that different representation algebras produce different apparent primitive counts).

rows.anchor: $$\Delta_t=(G_{cov},G_{val},G_{unc},G_{warrant},G_{con},G_{model},G_{obs},G_{stale},G_{id},G_{repr})$$ ... **not a numerical vector yet**. It is a **typed semantic gap vector**.
rows.statement: Assembles the complete typed Gap vector Delta_t=(G_cov,G_val,G_unc,G_warrant,G_con,G_model,G_obs,G_stale,G_id,G_repr), explicitly a typed semantic gap vector, not yet a numerical one, worked through a comparative example table showing this preserves epistemic meaning that a bare I-K difference would flatten.

rows.anchor: K_t != Delta_t. And: K_t != I_t. Therefore: K_t != I_t-K_t. ... The derivation correctly warned against collapsing Knowledge and Knowledge Gap.
rows.statement: States the crucial theoretical correction Gap is not Knowledge: K_t != Delta_t and K_t != I_t, therefore K_t != I_t - K_t (guarding against collapsing the Knowledge state, Ideal state, and Gap into interchangeable objects).

rows.anchor: $$K_{t+1}\succeq_{EC}K_t \iff \Delta(K_{t+1},EC)\subseteq\Delta(K_t,EC)$$ ... [THM-G2] If Delta_{t+1} subset-eq Delta_t, then K_{t+1} >=_EC K_t. If Delta_{t+1} subset Delta_t, then K_{t+1} >_EC K_t. This finally gives us a mathematically defensible notion of **knowledge improvement** without requiring a numerical metric.
rows.statement: Defines a partial order of knowledge adequacy K_{t+1} >=_EC K_t iff Delta_{t+1} subset-or-equal Delta_t (subject to preservation of previously valid requirements), with [THM-G2] the Gap-reduction theorem giving strict improvement K_{t+1} >_EC K_t when the inclusion is strict -- a mathematically defensible notion of knowledge improvement requiring no numerical metric.

rows.anchor: Suppose K_t={p,q,r} but q is later discovered unsupported. Then K_{t+1}={p,r}. The cardinality decreased ... Yet epistemic quality may improve. ... |K_{t+1}|<|K_t| not=> K_{t+1} prec K_t.
rows.statement: Gives a worked example (K_t={p,q,r} shrinking to K_{t+1}={p,r} after q is found unsupported) showing knowledge can improve while cardinality decreases, giving |K_{t+1}|<|K_t| does not imply K_{t+1} is epistemically worse -- the reason knowledge quantity and knowledge quality must remain separate.

rows.anchor: Negative Gap ... Ideal State requires p. But current knowledge contains not-p. The issue is not simply "missing p." It is: Contradictory State. ... Delta^+ = missing required knowledge and Delta^- = currently held knowledge violating requirements. Delta_t=(Delta_t^+,Delta_t^-).
rows.statement: Introduces Negative Gap: when the Ideal State requires p but current knowledge contains not-p, the issue is a Contradictory State, not simple absence; formalizes a directional split Delta_t=(Delta_t^+, Delta_t^-) where Delta^+ is missing required knowledge and Delta^- is currently-held knowledge violating requirements -- more informative than an undirected absolute distance.

rows.anchor: Positive deficit: Missing ... Negative conflict: Contradictory ... Epistemic insufficiency: Insufficient ... Gap = Deficit union Conflict union Insufficiency.
rows.statement: Consolidates the ten gap classes into three fundamental gap directions -- Positive deficit (Missing: required but absent), Negative conflict (Contradictory: present but incompatible with requirements), and Epistemic insufficiency (Insufficient: present but below required evidence/uncertainty/model standard) -- giving Gap = Deficit union Conflict union Insufficiency as the top-level decomposition of which the detailed taxonomy is a refinement.

rows.anchor: $$G_{coverage}=1-Coverage_t$$ ... g_r^unc=max(0,tau_r-p_r) ... g_r^evidence=max(0,tau_e-e_r) ... g_r^time=max(0,age_r-L_r) ... g_r^model=1-Sat(M_t,A_r) ... g_r^obs=1-O_r. But this is **not** the probability that the requirement is false.
rows.statement: Derives six named numerical gap measures (each a DERIVED view, not the Gap's definition) once explicit scales exist: coverage gap 1-Coverage_t; uncertainty gap max(0,tau_r-p_r); evidence gap max(0,tau_e-e_r); temporal gap max(0,age_r-L_r); model gap 1-Sat(M_t,A_r); observability gap 1-O_r (explicitly NOT the probability the requirement is false, but uncertainty about observability itself).

rows.anchor: $$G(K_t,EC_t)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_t}w_r d_r(K_t,EC_t).$$ ... [THM-G3] Zero equivalence ... Proof: If G=0 and every term is non-negative, then every term must be zero ... Therefore: G=0 iff Zero.
rows.statement: Derives the master weighted Gap functional G(K_t,EC_t)=sum over required r of w_r*d_r(K_t,EC_t) (d_r>=0, d_r=0 iff satisfied), and proves [THM-G3] the Zero-equivalence theorem G(K_t,EC_t)=0 iff Delta_t=empty, with an explicit non-negative-sum proof -- the rigorous bridge from semantic Gap to statistical/numerical Gap that was previously missing.

rows.anchor: Level 1 -- Semantic: Delta_t. Level 2 -- Structured: Delta_t^typed. Level 3 -- Numerical: G_t. Thus: Semantic Gap -> Typed Gap -> Numerical Gap. Not the reverse.
rows.statement: States the three-level Gap hierarchy discipline: Semantic Gap (Delta_t, what is missing/contradictory/uncertain/stale) -> Typed Gap (how each requirement is deficient) -> Numerical Gap (G_t, magnitude under an explicit loss/weighting model) -- and explicitly never the reverse order.

rows.anchor: $$\mathfrak G=(\mathcal R,Sat,Type,\oplus,\preceq)$$ ... $$\Delta_1\oplus\Delta_2=\Delta_1\cup\Delta_2.$$ ... [THM-G4] ... If EC_t=EC_{t+1}, then Gap reduction is directly comparable. If EC_t != EC_{t+1}, then a direct comparison requires an explicit mapping M: Req(EC_t)->Req(EC_{t+1}). Without such mapping: Delta_t not~ Delta_{t+1} in general. This protects KnowledgeOS against "moving the goalposts."
rows.statement: Defines a formal Gap algebra G=(R,Sat,Type,+,<=) with gap composition Delta1 (+) Delta2 = union (with identity-based normalization needed under requirement overlap), and proves [THM-G4] the Contract Invariance theorem: gap comparison across time is only valid when EC_t=EC_{t+1}, or else requires an explicit mapping M:Req(EC_t)->Req(EC_{t+1}) between requirement sets -- protecting KnowledgeOS against artificially achieving Zero by silently changing requirements ('moving the goalposts').

rows.anchor: Ideal State is therefore not arbitrary. ... Prov(I_t)=(Knower,Goal,Inquiry,Context,Contract,Time,Authority). ... its origin is auditable.
rows.statement: Gives the Ideal State its own provenance object Prov(I_t)=(Knower,Goal,Inquiry,Context,Contract,Time,Authority), making the Ideal State's origin auditable rather than an arbitrary given, following the earlier conclusion that the Knower owns the epistemic frame and Ideal State.

rows.anchor: $$\Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)$$ not simply: Gap(K_t). The same knowledge state can have Zero for one purpose and LargeGap for another. ... For "What operating system does Nexus use?" the gap may be empty. For "Is Nexus ready for migration?" the gap may be large. Gap is purpose relative.
rows.statement: States the Gap is fundamentally relational (Gap(K_t,EC_t), never Gap(K_t) alone), worked through a concrete Nexus example where the same knowledge (OS=RHEL9.8, 8vCPU, Nexus OSS 3.69.0) has Delta=empty for 'what OS does Nexus use?' but a large gap for 'is Nexus ready for migration?' -- Gap is purpose-relative.

rows.anchor: A new observation can make the Gap **larger** without making KnowledgeOS worse. ... backup system is not actually verified ... The Gap increased. But epistemically, KnowledgeOS may have improved because an unknown problem became visible. GapIncrease not=> KnowledgeDecrease. The system has changed from Unknown to Known Gap. That is epistemic progress.
rows.statement: States a profound consequence, worked with a backup-verification example: a new observation can enlarge the Gap (from Delta=empty because a requirement was not even represented, to Delta={backup verification} once it becomes known to be unmet) without making the system epistemically worse -- giving GapIncrease does not imply KnowledgeDecrease, since going from Unknown to Known-Gap is itself epistemic progress.

rows.anchor: $$A_t=Adequacy(K_t,EC_t)$$ ... $$O_\Delta(t)=Observable(\Delta_t).$$ ... A_{t+1}<A_t while O_Delta(t+1)>O_Delta(t). The knowledge state can therefore become **more truthful about its own deficiency**. ... $$Progress_t=(Adequacy,GapObservability,Warrant,UncertaintyReduction,ModelAdequacy).$$
rows.statement: Recommends two decoupled measures -- State adequacy A_t=Adequacy(K_t,EC_t) and Gap observability O_Delta(t)=Observable(Delta_t) -- since an investigation can simultaneously decrease adequacy while increasing gap observability (the system becoming more truthful about its own deficiency); proposes a five-component Progress vector (Adequacy, GapObservability, Warrant, UncertaintyReduction, ModelAdequacy), with a scalar score derivable only if the epistemic contract itself supplies a utility function.

rows.anchor: [THM-G6] Gap decomposition theorem: every unsatisfied requirement belongs to at least one declared failure class: Delta_t = union of Delta^cov,val,unc,warrant,con,model,obs,stale,id,repr. ... we should not falsely claim that these categories are naturally mutually exclusive. ... an obsolete claim may also have insufficient evidence.
rows.statement: States [THM-G6] the Gap Decomposition theorem: every unsatisfied requirement falls into at least one of the ten declared failure classes (Delta_t = union of all ten typed subsets), explicitly warning the classes are NOT naturally mutually exclusive (an obsolete claim may also have insufficient evidence), so the semantic model must allow multiple simultaneous gap tags per requirement.

rows.anchor: $$\Delta_1\preceq\Delta_2\iff\Delta_1\subseteq\Delta_2.$$ Then: (G_t,subseteq) is a partially ordered set. ... Delta_1 vee Delta_2 = union, Delta_1 wedge Delta_2 = intersection. Thus the Gap structure naturally admits a lattice interpretation. ... Zero = bottom_G. ... Delta_max=R. ... (P(R),subseteq) is the simplest mathematical carrier of the semantic Gap.
rows.statement: Shows the set of typed gap states forms a lattice (G_t,subseteq) under set-theoretic ordering, with join = union and meet = intersection, giving Zero the precise mathematical status of the BOTTOM ELEMENT of the gap lattice (Zero = bottom_G, far stronger than 'distance equals zero'), and a maximum gap Delta_max=R (all requirements unsatisfied); concludes the power set (P(R), subseteq) is the simplest rigorous mathematical carrier for the semantic Gap -- crucially achievable WITHOUT first solving the complete mathematical structure of K_t itself, judged an important breakthrough since it unblocks Gap theory from the still-open K_t-type question.

rows.anchor: $$EC_t\rightarrow \mathcal R_t\rightarrow Sat(K_t,r)\rightarrow \Delta_t$$ gives us a rigorous Gap semantics even while the complete mathematical structure of K_t remains open.
rows.statement: States the revised KnowledgeOS mathematical backbone chain EC_t -> R_t -> Sat(K_t,r) -> Delta_t as achieving rigorous Gap semantics independent of resolving K_t's mathematical type, resolving what had previously blocked progress (K_t=? and D(K_t,I_t)=?).

rows.anchor: Still open: 1. The exact universal mathematical type of K_t. 2. The universal semantics of Sat(K_t,r). 3. The canonical atomic knowledge unit. 4. The universal statistical meaning of uncertainty. 5. Whether all gap classes above are complete. 6. Whether the gap lattice is the final mathematical structure. 7. How semantic equivalence of different representations preserves Sat. 8. How causal/model adequacy should be formally represented. 9. How to construct optimal interventions for reducing Delta_t. 10. Whether a canonical scalar gap function exists.
rows.statement: Closes with an explicit ten-item open-questions list that the Gap theory does NOT resolve: the universal mathematical type of K_t; the universal semantics of Sat(K_t,r) (identified as the single narrowest and most important next problem); the canonical atomic knowledge unit; the universal statistical meaning of uncertainty; completeness of the ten gap classes; whether the gap lattice is the final mathematical structure; how semantic equivalence of representations preserves Sat; formal representation of causal/model adequacy; construction of optimal gap-reducing interventions; and whether a canonical scalar gap function exists -- explicitly instructing these remain [OPEN], not be prematurely turned into axioms.

rows.anchor: $$Adeq(K,Q,C,EC)\iff \forall r\in Req(Q,C,EC),\ Sat(K,r).$$ This is a genuine derivation from the definitions. ... $$\Delta(K,Q,C,EC)=\{r\in Req(Q,C,EC):\neg Sat(K,r)\}.$$ ... Zero(K,Q,C,EC) iff Delta(K,Q,C,EC)=empty. ... Zero is not a number. It is a **predicate over an empty requirement residual**.
rows.statement: Derives Adeq(K,Q,C,EC) iff for all r in Req(Q,C,EC), Sat(K,r) -- a genuine derivation from existing definitions rather than a new assumption -- and correspondingly Delta(K,Q,C,EC)={r in Req: not Sat(K,r)} with Zero iff Delta=empty, stronger than the prior K models EC formulation since it identifies exactly what the discrepancy is; states Zero is not a number but a predicate over an empty requirement residual (independently converging with the companion Gap-theory document's identical formalization).

rows.anchor: Gap is therefore not distance. ... Delta_t is first a **residual requirement structure**. Only afterwards may a regime define: d(Delta_t) or: Severity(Delta_t). Thus: Gap -> Requirement Residual -> optional Measurement. This eliminates the temptation to invent a universal Knowledge Distance.
rows.statement: States Gap -> Requirement Residual -> optional Measurement as the correct hierarchy, eliminating the temptation to invent a universal Knowledge Distance -- independently convergent with the companion Gap-theory document's semantic-before-numerical discipline.

aliases: Step 5: What Is the Mathematical Object Being Aggregated

sources.note: S0860's Step 5: separates Evidence/Support/Belief/Probability/Truth, defines the Evidence Contribution Domain Q with c_rho:ExPxC->Q left calculus-agnostic, recommends KERNEL (evidence semantics/provenance/relations) vs pluggable POLICY (Bayesian/DS/argumentation/possibility) calculi, distinguishes Assessment/Acceptance/Truth, argues probability requires a model, and introduces Information Gain/EvidenceValue vs EvidenceStrength as a new axis feeding Step 6 and Lord/Sarathi's evidence-acquisition selection.

rows.anchor:
Until now we have deliberately used the generic word "support." We now need to determine what that actually means. ... Evidence 
eq Support 
eq Belief 
eq Probability 
eq Truth
rows.statement: States that Evidence, Support, Belief, Probability, and Truth are different mathematical/domain concepts that must not be conflated under the generic word 'support'.

rows.anchor: Start with the simplest object: a proposition ... An evidence object e does not itself need to be a proposition. ... These are artifacts or observations from which propositions may be extracted or supported. Evidence\ object\rightarrow Proposition is already an important transformation.
rows.statement: Distinguishes propositions (P1: Nexus version=3.69, etc.) from evidence objects (API response, PDF, database row, screenshot, LLM output, ADR, etc.), which are artifacts/observations from which propositions are extracted, not propositions themselves; Evidence object → Proposition is itself a nontrivial transformation.

rows.anchor: Evidence contribution ... c_\rho(e,P,C) ... the evidential contribution of e toward proposition P under context C and policy \rho. But we deliberately do not say c(e,P)\in[0,1] yet. That would prematurely impose a numerical interpretation.
rows.statement: Defines the primitive c_ρ(e,P,C) — evidential contribution of e toward P under context C and policy ρ — deliberately withholding any commitment that its range is [0,1].

rows.anchor: Why a scalar is dangerous ... c(e,P)=0.8 ... 80% probability ... strong evidential support; source reliability; confidence of an LLM; likelihood ratio; degree of belief; degree of plausibility; quality of the source. These are completely different things. 0.8 has no epistemic meaning until its seman
rows.statement: Warns that an unlabeled scalar contribution value (e.g. 0.8) is dangerously ambiguous — it could mean probability, evidential support strength, source reliability, LLM confidence, likelihood ratio, degree of belief, plausibility, or source quality — and has no fixed epistemic meaning until its semantics are specified.

rows.anchor: The semantic domains ... Reliability R(e) ... Relevance Rel(e,P,C) ... Evidential support Supp(e,P,C) ... Probability Pr(P\mid E,C) ... Belief Bel(P) ... Plausibility Pl(P) ... Information IG(E;P) ... How much did the evidence reduce uncertainty? Not: Is the proposition true?
rows.statement: Enumerates seven distinct semantic domains that evidential contribution might mean: Reliability R(e), Relevance Rel(e,P,C), Evidential support Supp(e,P,C), Probability Pr(P|E,C), Belief Bel(P) (Dempster-Shafer sense, distinct from probability), Plausibility Pl(P), and Information IG(E;P) (uncertainty reduction, not truth).

rows.anchor: Therefore we need an Evidence Contribution Domain ... \mathcal Q ... c_\rho: \mathcal E\times\mathcal P\times\mathcal C \rightarrow \mathcal Q ... Q does not have to be [0,1]. It might be an ordered scale; a vector; a belief function; a likelihood ratio; an argument structure; a set of possible stat
rows.statement: Defines an Evidence Contribution Domain Q with c_ρ:E×P×C→Q, explicitly allowing Q to be an ordered scale, vector, belief function, likelihood ratio, argument structure, set of possible states, or probability distribution rather than fixed to [0,1].

rows.anchor: My recommendation: the kernel should not choose one ... I would not put Bayesian probability or Dempster–Shafer belief into the KnowledgeOS kernel. KnowledgeOS Kernel = Evidence Semantics + Provenance + Relations ... Assessment Calculus = Pluggable Policy
rows.statement: Recommends the kernel not commit to any specific probabilistic/belief framework: KnowledgeOS Kernel = Evidence Semantics + Provenance + Relations, while Assessment Calculus (Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, Argumentation, Possibility, deterministic-rule, domain-specific) remains Pluggable Policy.

rows.anchor: The most fundamental representation is therefore relational ... Rel(E,P) rather than Score(E,P). ... E1 → supports, E2 → supports, E3 → derived-from E1, E4 → contradicts, E5 → stale-supports. This relational structure is the epistemic foundation.
rows.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should first construct a relational structure Rel(E,P) (supports/derived-from/contradicts/stale-supports edges) rather than a Score(E,P) scalar, calling the relational structure the epistemic foundation.

rows.anchor: Then assessment can be performed ... Assessment_\rho(P\mid E) ... Assessment_{Bayes}(P\mid E)=Pr(P\mid E) ... Assessment_{DS}(P\mid E)=(Bel(P),Pl(P)) ... Assessment_{Argument}(P\mid E)=Arguments^+(P),Arguments^-(P) ... These are not necessarily convertible into one universal number.
rows.statement: Shows three concrete policy-specific instantiations of Assessment_ρ(P|E): Bayesian (Pr(P|E)), Dempster-Shafer ((Bel(P),Pl(P))), and Argumentation (Arguments+/-(P)), noting these are not necessarily convertible into one universal number.

rows.anchor: This resolves an earlier problem ... Should KnowledgeOS use one evidence algebra? The answer is becoming clearer: No. The kernel should define what evidence means and how evidence relates. The reasoning policy determines how that evidence is mathematically assessed. This is a very strong DDD boundar
rows.statement: Answers the recurring 'one evidence algebra?' question definitively No, drawing the DDD boundary: the kernel defines what evidence means and how it relates; the reasoning policy determines how it is mathematically assessed.

rows.anchor: But we still need a common interface ... AssessmentResult ... AR=(P,Support,Opposition,Uncertainty,Basis,Context,Policy) ... Bayesian Support=Pr(P\mid E) ... Dempster-Shafer Support=Bel(P) ... Argumentation Support=accepted supporting arguments ... The domain object retains the semantics of the chos
rows.statement: Proposes a common AssessmentResult interface AR=(P,Support,Opposition,Uncertainty,Basis,Context,Policy) whose Support field's internal representation differs by calculus (Bayesian probability, DS belief, argumentation's accepted arguments) while retaining that calculus's own semantics.

rows.anchor: Important: "support" itself may need qualification ... EvidentialSupport from Acceptance ... Pr(P\mid E)=0.95 ... 0.95\Rightarrow Accepted ... Another may require 0.99\Rightarrow Accepted. Assessment\neq Acceptance. Acceptance is a policy decision.
rows.statement: Distinguishes EvidentialSupport from Acceptance: different policies may set different acceptance thresholds on the same support value (e.g. 0.95 vs 0.99), so Assessment ≠ Acceptance — acceptance is a policy decision.

rows.anchor: And acceptance is not truth ... Accepted(P) does not mean Truth(P). Accepted(P) = currently accepted under policy \rho. This is precisely the distinction our Knowledge State needs.
rows.statement: States Accepted(P) ≠ Truth(P); Accepted(P) means only 'currently accepted under policy ρ', a distinction needed by the Knowledge State.

rows.anchor: The statistical interpretation ... Pr(P\mid E) = Pr(E\mid P)Pr(P)/Pr(E) ... we need prior; likelihood; evidence model; dependency assumptions; sampling assumptions; model adequacy. KnowledgeOS cannot simply infer these from the existence of a document. Probability requires a model.
rows.statement: Notes Bayesian Pr(P|E) requires priors, likelihoods, an evidence model, dependency and sampling assumptions, and model adequacy that cannot be inferred merely from a document's existence — 'Probability requires a model.'

rows.anchor: Example: two documents ... A naive system might say 2 confirmations. But our model asks Dependency(A,B)=? If A\rightarrow B then IndependentEvidenceCount=1. If A\perp B then they may provide two contributions. If Dependency(A,B)=Unknown then we do not pretend to know.
rows.statement: Worked example: two documents both stating 'Nexus 3.69' naively look like two confirmations, but the correct count depends on Dependency(A,B) — 1 if dependent, 2 if independently acquired, and an honest 'we do not pretend to know' if Dependency is Unknown.

rows.anchor: The evidence contribution should therefore be factored ... c_\rho(e,P,C)=g_\rho(Rel,Qual,Relia,Valid,Context,Dependency,Polarity) ... g_\rho is policy-specific. The kernel stores the dimensions. The policy determines how they combine.
rows.statement: Factors evidence contribution as c_ρ(e,P,C)=g_ρ(Relevance,Quality,Reliability,Validity,Context,Dependency,Polarity), where the kernel stores the seven dimensions and the policy-specific function g_ρ determines how they combine.

rows.anchor: This gives us a very clean mathematical decomposition ... Evidence semantics ... Evidence relation ... Proposition relation ... Assessment ... Conclusion ... Knowledge State ... E\rightarrow Relations\rightarrow Assessment\rightarrow Conclusion\rightarrow KnowledgeState
rows.statement: Assembles the full pipeline E→Relations→Assessment→Conclusion→KnowledgeState across six named mappings (Evidence semantics, Evidence relation, Proposition relation, Assessment, Conclusion, Knowledge State update).

rows.anchor: DDD interpretation ... Evidence ... EvidenceRelation ... PropositionAssessment ... Conclusion ... KnowledgeState ... Decision ... These should not be one aggregate.
rows.statement: Names six DDD concepts (Evidence, EvidenceRelation, PropositionAssessment, Conclusion, KnowledgeState, Decision) that must remain separate aggregates rather than merged into one.

rows.statement: Re-examines candidate calculi against the semantic-domain requirement: weighted arithmetic's 0.8 still lacks universal semantics; saturating aggregation (1-∏(1-s_i)) does not itself resolve dependency without the Evidence Graph; Bayesian and Dempster-Shafer each carry their own assumptions; argumentation uniquely preserves why an assertion is supported/attacked.

rows.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS needs two complementary calculus families — quantitative (Bayesian/Statistical/Possibility) for numerically meaningful uncertainty, and qualitative/argumentative (for ADRs, architectural principles, competing interpretations) — proposing the principle 'Not every epistemic problem should become a probability problem.'

rows.statement: Consolidates the formal model: Evidence Universe E, Proposition Universe P, Context Universe C, Evidence Relations R_E, and Assessment_ρ:(E,R_E,P,C)→A_ρ where A_ρ is the policy-defined assessment space.

rows.statement: Proposes a nine-item KERNEL vocabulary (Evidence, Proposition, Provenance, Lineage, Dependency, Context, TemporalValidity, Polarity, AssessmentBasis) versus a six-item POLICY vocabulary (Aggregation, Inference, Thresholds, ProbabilityModels, BeliefModels, DecisionRules) as an architecturally clean separation.

A weak piece of evidence can sometimes have enormous information value if it resolves a previously critical uncertainty. EvidenceValue\neq EvidenceStrength. This will be
rows.statement: Introduces InformationGain as distinct from EvidenceStrength, illustrated by a probability shift from 0.5 to 0.99: a weak piece of evidence can have enormous information value if it resolves a critical uncertainty — EvidenceValue ≠ EvidenceStrength, foreshadowing Lord/Sarathi's evidence-acquisition selection.

rows.anchor: Step 5 verdict ... Theoretical status: substantially resolved ... The fundamental object is not a scalar score. Evidence Contribution is a policy-interpreted semantic relation. rows.statement: Declares Step 5 'substantially resolved': the fundamental object is not a scalar score; Evidence Contribution is a policy-interpreted semantic relation; Assessment is a structured object; probability/belief/likelihood/information-gain/argument-strength are different mathematical constructs.

rationale_evidence.statement: Warns that an unlabeled scalar contribution value (e.g. 0.8) is dangerously ambiguous — it could mean probability, evidential support strength, source reliability, LLM confidence, likelihood ratio, degree of belief, plausibility, or source quality — and has no fixed epistemic meaning until its semantics are specified.

sources.note: Step 278 exists in three successive layers. Layer 1 defines the Policy-Authority integration model: Verdict as a tagged union including a structured Conditional(RequiredConditions,SatisfiedConditions,MissingConditions,ResolutionStrategy in {WAIT,REQUEST,ESCALATE,REASSESS,BLOCK}) distinct from Unknown; recommends Constitutional Authority as the non-circular root (Constitution -> Authority -> Policy -> Authorization -> Operation); defines policy versioning/immutability/temporal validity as half-open intervals, deny-over-permit Authorization=Combine(PolicyVerdict,AuthorityVerdict) precedence table, and the ontology correction 'governance Policy not-in K, but knowledge ABOUT policy in K'; introduces four independent closure dimensions Formal/Computational/Empirical/Governance (FC/CC/EC/GC) that may be set independently (e.g. FC=1,CC=0,EC=0,GC=1); specifies F1-F13 falsification tests. Layer 2 is Layer 1 plus an appended supervisory review that CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTS it while flagging twelve underspecified areas (policy-evaluation algorithm, Combine's condition-merging, statistical-model integration, policy-version identity, eventual-consistency mechanism, non-executable falsification tests, unenforced DDD invariants, imprecise closure terminology, underspecified Step 279 deliverables, measurement-evidence integration, unoperationalized rule independence, missing calibration model). Layer 3 ('FINAL') answers all twelve, replacing the closure vocabulary with five explicit states (OPEN/FORMALLY SPECIFIED/COMPUTATIONALLY PARAMETRIC/EMPIRICALLY CLOSED/GOVERNANCE CLOSED), adding a policy-content-addressed identity model (PID=Hash(...)), three independence classes (structural/logical/statistical, explicitly distinct), a measurement/calibration model with scale-typing (nominal/ordinal/interval/ratio), five new falsification tests F9-F13, and a mandatory rule 'overlap without a resolution rule => INVALID', concluding Policy/Authority in C1 (formally specified), pending Step 279 (executable implementation) and Step 280 (end-to-end empirical closure test); no theory-completeness claim is made at any layer.

rows.anchor: formal closure, computational closure, empirical closure, and governance closure are four different claims. They must never be conflated. ... No overall theory closure is claimed by Step 278.
rows.statement: States the four-independent-closure-claims principle (formal/computational/empirical/governance) governing the whole of Step 278, and explicitly disclaims any overall theory-closure claim.

rows.anchor: Verdict = Permit | Deny | Conditional(c) | Unknown(u) ... Conditional(c)=(RequiredConditions,SatisfiedConditions,MissingConditions,ResolutionStrategy) ... WAIT ... REQUEST ... ESCALATE ... REASSESS ... BLOCK
rows.statement: Replaces the previously vague four-value Verdict enum with a tagged union where Conditional carries a structured (RequiredConditions, SatisfiedConditions, MissingConditions, ResolutionStrategy) record, ResolutionStrategy in {WAIT, REQUEST, ESCALATE, REASSESS, BLOCK}; explicitly distinguishes Unknown (policy result undeterminable) from Conditional (policy known, conditions unresolved).

rows.anchor: RootAuthority = ConstitutionalAuthority ... A self-rooted model is circular: Authority => Authority. An external root pushes the foundational question outside the KnowledgeOS governance model. ... A constitutional root provides an explicit meta-level
rows.statement: Recommends Constitutional Authority as the root of the authority regress (Constitution -> Authority -> Policy -> Authorization -> Operation), against three rejected alternatives (self-rooted, circular; external, pushes the question outside; organizational, unstable when organizational authority itself changes).

rows.anchor: Policy as governing mechanism NOT-IN K ... but: Knowledge about Policy IN K when represented as an epistemic assertion. This resolves the ontology error.
rows.statement: Corrects an earlier overstated claim (Policy not-in K) to distinguish the active governance policy (external, not itself epistemic content) from PROPOSITIONS about policy (e.g. 'policy version v became effective at t'), which are legitimate epistemic assertions and so CAN be in K.

rows.anchor: | Policy | Authority | Authorization | ... Conditional | Permit | Conditional | ... Unknown | * | Unknown | This establishes deny-over-permit semantics. No positive authorization may be inferred from incomplete information.
rows.statement: Defines Authorization=Combine(PolicyVerdict,AuthorityVerdict) via an explicit precedence table establishing deny-over-permit semantics (any Deny or Unknown input dominates; Conditional propagates unless overridden by Deny), so no positive authorization can ever be inferred from incomplete information.

rows.anchor: 35.1 Formal Closure ... 35.2 Computational Closure ... 35.3 Empirical Closure ... 35.4 Governance Closure ... A foundation may therefore have: FC=1, CC=0, EC=0, GC=1
rows.statement: Introduces four independently-settable closure-symbol dimensions FC/CC/EC/GC (Formal/Computational/Empirical/Governance), with the explicit example that a construct can be formally-and-governance-defined (FC=1,GC=1) while not yet executable or empirically tested (CC=0,EC=0) -- FormalClosure != CompleteClosure.

rows.anchor: F1 -- Policy-free transition ... F5 -- Missing policy ... Expected: Unknown, not Permit. ... F9 -- Overlapping policy versions ... F13 -- Statistical policy boundary
rows.statement: Specifies 13 falsification tests F1-F13 (policy-free transition, authority-free transition, policy conflict, authority conflict, missing policy -> Unknown not Permit, expired policy, revoked authority under historical replay, unauthorized policy mutation, overlapping policy versions, policy rollback creating a new version, authority delegation escalation, governance propagation race, statistical policy boundary) each with a stated expected outcome, for the executable implementation in Step 279.

rows.anchor: STEP 278 -- FORMAL POLICY/AUTHORITY SEMANTICS: CLOSED ... COMPUTATIONAL CLOSURE: PENDING STEP 279 ... EMPIRICAL CLOSURE: PENDING STEP 280 ... GOVERNANCE CLOSURE: PENDING NORMATIVE RATIFICATION ... KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY IS NOT YET DECLARED COMPLETE.
rows.statement: Layer 1's final HPA ruling: formal Policy/Authority semantics CLOSED, but computational closure pending Step 279, empirical closure pending Step 280, governance closure pending normative ratification (constitutional root, exact authority holder, emergency governance, policy-conflict defaults, propagation mode all listed as remaining N1-N5 normative decisions) -- no theory-completeness claim made.

rows.anchor: The revised Step 278 is a substantially improved document. ... However, several issues remain that must be addressed before Step 278 can be considered complete. ... Step 278 is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED with required corrections.
rows.statement: Supervisory review's overall verdict: Layer 1 correctly introduces the four closure dimensions, structured Conditional verdict, Constitutional Authority recommendation, Policy-vs-knowledge-about-policy distinction, concrete DDD contexts, and statistical/rule-independence models, but is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED pending twelve corrections.

rows.anchor: The document defines: Evaluate_pi : (K, E, C, A) -> V_pi. But it does not specify how policy rules are evaluated. ... The Combine function is underspecified ... The Statistical Measurement Model Is Not Integrated ... No Calibration Model for Probabilistic Policies
rows.statement: Identifies specific gaps in Layer 1: the policy-evaluation function's algorithm (as opposed to its signature) is unspecified; Combine's handling of Conditional-with-conditions-from-both-sides is unspecified; the statistical measurement model (P(theta>c|X)>=q) is defined but not connected to policy-rule representation or evaluation; and no calibration-verification model exists for probabilistic policy predicates (severity HIGH on the latter two).

rows.anchor: The Falsification Tests Are Not Executable ... without execution specifications, the tests are not falsifiable. ... The DDD Invariants Are Not Validated ... The Closure Matrix Is Still Too Optimistic
rows.statement: Further identified gaps: F1-F13 lack execution specifications (setup/execute/expected/pass-criteria) so are not yet actually falsifiable; the DDD invariants G-I1..G-I5 lack enforcement-location/violation-consequence specification; and the closure matrix conflates 'Formally Specified' (definition exists) with 'Formally Closed' (definition complete and consistent) -- recommends distinguishing five closure-status labels rather than the prior binary-ish set.

rows.anchor: The Policy–Authority integration model is formally specified but not yet closed. Formal Closure: CONDITIONAL -- requires corrections. ... The theory is NOT COMPLETE. ... Next: STEP 278 FINAL
rows.statement: Supervisory ruling: Step 278 is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTED, with all twelve identified issues mandatory to address before completion; directs the next artifact to be 'Step 278 Final -- Policy-Authority Integration with Corrections'.

rows.anchor: The previous Step 278 correctly identified Policy and Authority as the remaining governance dependency, but it was too strong in several places. In particular, it blurred: formal definition with computational closure; computational closure with empirical validation; governance policy with knowledge
rows.statement: Accepts the supervisory review's finding that Layer 1 blurred several distinctions (formal/computational/empirical closure; governance policy vs knowledge-about-policy; authority vs authorization; policy versioning vs knowledge-state history; DDD aggregates vs mathematical objects), and states the corrected position: Policy/Authority are now a formal governance subsystem, with computational/empirical closure deferred to Steps 279/280.

rows.anchor: C0 -- OPEN ... C1 -- FORMALLY SPECIFIED ... C2 -- COMPUTATIONALLY PARAMETRIC ... C3 -- EMPIRICALLY CLOSED ... C4 -- GOVERNANCE CLOSED ... These dimensions are ORTHOGONAL.
rows.statement: Replaces the closure vocabulary a third time with five explicit orthogonal states C0-C4 (OPEN, FORMALLY SPECIFIED, COMPUTATIONALLY PARAMETRIC, EMPIRICALLY CLOSED, GOVERNANCE CLOSED), explicitly noting a policy can be 'formally specified + computationally executable + empirically tested + governance-open' without contradiction.

rows.anchor: PID = Hash(content, rules, parameters, authority, validity) ... A change therefore creates a new policy identity rather than mutating the identity of an existing policy. ... Policy replacement is represented as: Supersedes(pi_18, pi_17) not deletion.
rows.statement: Defines content-addressed policy-version identity (PID=Hash(content,rules,parameters,authority,validity)), so any change produces a new identity rather than mutation, with replacement represented via an explicit Supersedes relation over immutable historical policies rather than deletion.

rows.anchor: Structural independence ... Inputs(r_i) intersect Inputs(r_j) = emptyset ... Logical independence ... Statistical independence ... These are different concepts. Structural independence != Logical independence != Statistical independence
rows.statement: Defines three explicitly distinct independence classes for policy rules -- structural (disjoint inputs), logical (neither entails the other), statistical (observed evaluations approximately probabilistically independent) -- correcting an earlier undifferentiated 'rule independence' concept.

rows.anchor: Nominal | Equality/classification | Ordinal | Ordering | Interval | Differences | Ratio | Ratios + arithmetic ... a policy must not perform x+y merely because x and y are represented numerically.
rows.statement: Requires every policy measurement to declare its measurement scale (nominal/ordinal/interval/ratio) and forbids performing an operation (e.g. addition) not licensed by that scale merely because values happen to be represented numerically; adds a calibration model (bias b=E[theta-hat]-theta, variance bound) for inexact measurement functions.

rows.anchor: Overlap without a resolution rule => INVALID. ... A node must never silently move backward ... unless an explicit historical replay operation is being performed. ... Operational policy propagation = monotonic while Replay = intentionally historical
rows.statement: States two mandatory invariants: overlapping policy validity intervals without an explicit resolution rule are INVALID by construction (not silently resolved); and normal operational policy-version propagation must be monotonic (never silently regress to an older version) except during an explicitly intentional historical Replay.

rows.anchor: F9 -- Unauthorized Policy Mutation ... F10 -- Historical Policy Replay ... F11 -- Overlapping Policy Conflict ... F12 -- Governance Propagation ... F13 -- Rule Independence
rows.statement: Adds five new falsification tests F9-F13 (each with an explicit hypothesis and failure condition): unauthorized policy mutation must not activate; historical replay must use the historically-applicable policy not the current one; overlapping unprioritized policies must yield CONFLICT not a silent choice; a policy change must propagate to all nodes within its stated bound; and structurally-independent rules must not acquire hidden result-dependency through implementation.

rows.anchor: Policy, Authority in C1 ... Empirical closure requires Step 280. Governance closure requires organizational ratification. ... NEXT: STEP 279 -- POLICY AND AUTHORITY EXECUTABLE IMPLEMENTATION
rows.statement: Final ruling: Policy and Authority are placed in closure state C1 (formally specified), with computational closure pending Step 279's executable implementation, empirical closure pending Step 280's end-to-end test, and governance closure pending organizational ratification of five listed normative decisions (ND-01 through ND-05) -- explicitly not a claim of KnowledgeOS theory completeness.

rows.anchor: ### PA-1 (`EXECUTED`, CRITICAL) — the commissioned K-sufficiency step was silently replaced ... Step 277 ends: "Next: STEP 278 — K-SUFFICIENCY AND TRANSFORMATION MINIMALITY TEST" The actual Step 278 is "POLICY–AUTHORITY INTEGRATION..." and it mentions K-sufficiency zero times.
rows.statement: PA-1 (EXECUTED, CRITICAL): Step 277 explicitly commissions 'STEP 278 — K-SUFFICIENCY AND TRANSFORMATION MINIMALITY TEST' as its next step, but the actual Step 278 that was written is 'POLICY-AUTHORITY INTEGRATION, TEMPORAL SEMANTICS, AND GOVERNANCE CLOSURE', mentioning K-sufficiency zero times; its header claims to supersede an earlier draft of itself, not the commissioned step, and no artifact records the substitution. Identified as the fourth instance of the same corpus-wide 'commissioned-but-not-performed' failure mode (alongside the repaired measure-theory model, Regime, and Determination).

rows.anchor: ## The one thing no decision covers ... K-sufficiency. Step 277 declares it OPEN and commissioned Step 278 to test it; Step 278 did Policy–Authority instead and mentions it zero times (PA-1). ... This needs no decision. It needs the commissioned step to actually be performed, with the criterion `Sufficient(K, 𝒪, ℐ)` rather than congruence alone.
rows.statement: Distinguishes K-sufficiency from the six named decisions: unlike D-0 through D-5, K-sufficiency is not blocked by a normative choice but by a commissioned step (Step 278's original mandate) never having been performed. Recommends actually performing the K-sufficiency test using the Sufficient(K,O,I) criterion (congruence plus invariant-expressibility) rather than congruence alone.

rows.anchor: $$PID = Hash(content,rules,parameters,authority,validity)$$ ... A policy version is immutable after activation.
rows.statement: Implements Step 278's content-addressed policy identity: PID = Hash(content, rules, parameters, authority, validity), with a policy version treated as immutable after activation.

rows.anchor: | Dimension | Meaning | | Formal closure | Definitions and signatures are complete | | Computational closure | The specified operations execute | | Empirical closure | Behaviour is validated against real KnowledgeOS | | Governance closure | Required normative decisions are ratified | The implementation phase can establish at most the first two. Therefore: $$\boxed{Step\ 279 \neq Empirical\ Closure}$$ and: $$\boxed{Step\ 279 \neq Governance\ Closure}$$
rows.statement: Restates and applies the four-dimension closure taxonomy from Step 278 (Formal/Computational/Empirical/Governance), explicitly limiting what Step 279's implementation phase can establish to at most Formal and Computational closure; Empirical closure (validation against real KnowledgeOS) is reserved for Step 280, and Governance closure (ratified normative decisions) cannot be achieved through implementation at all. Explicitly forbids declaring 'KnowledgeOS Theory Complete' at this stage.

sources.note: The formal research mandate D288 - Decision-Procedure Closure, naming four targets to formalize (semantic equality ≡, observational equality ≈, provenance-sensitive equality ≅_λ, and Qualify) with a moratorium on new Sanskrit-correspondence expansion until they resolve or are classified as irreducible G1 gaps.

rows.anchor: **The programme has moved from "discover the missing concepts" to "formalise the decision procedures for concepts that the corpus already names."**
rows.statement: States the programme's phase transition: from discovering missing concepts to formalizing decision procedures for concepts the corpus already names, motivating the D288 mandate.

rows.anchor: **D288 — Decision-Procedure Closure** with four primary targets: 1. `≡` semantic equality ... 2. `≈` observational equality ... 3. `≅_λ` provenance-sensitive equality ... 4. `Qualify`
rows.statement: Defines the next research frontier as D288 - Decision-Procedure Closure, with four primary targets and their guiding questions: (1) semantic equality ≡ — what constitutes 'same knowledge semantics', what is the semantic carrier, is provenance Π included (must respect the still-open 'Decision 3'); (2) observational equality ≈ — what is the permitted observation set, is the relation parameterised by Ω/role/access level/purpose, can it be decided or only characterised; (3) provenance-sensitive equality ≅_λ — what counts as 'relevant provenance' (especially important since it changes the D285-5 injectivity result); (4) Qualify — its input/output types, what information it needs from W, Ω, O, provenance and the existing kernel, and whether it can be defined without introducing an unratified primitive.

rows.anchor: **My recommendation: freeze this package as the current D285/D287 evidence state and make the next prompt exclusively about closing `≡`, `≈`, `≅_λ`, and `Qualify`—with no new Sanskrit expansion until those four are resolved or explicitly classified as irreducible G1 gaps.**
rows.statement: Final recommendation: freeze the current package as the D285/D287 evidence state, and scope the next research prompt exclusively to closing the four D288 targets (semantic, observational, provenance-sensitive equality, and Qualify), with an explicit moratorium on new Sanskrit-correspondence expansion until those four are resolved or explicitly classified as irreducible G1 gaps.

rows.anchor: **RESEARCH ARTIFACT — corpus reconstruction; normative promotion explicitly prohibited.** ... **no new Sanskrit expansion, no invented equality procedure, no invented `Qualify`, and no silent promotion of `Π`, `Σ`, or the candidate order into architecture.**
rows.statement: Sets the required status line for both Step 286 and 287: 'RESEARCH ARTIFACT — corpus reconstruction; normative promotion explicitly prohibited', and preserves the standing stop-gate: no new Sanskrit expansion, no invented equality procedure, no invented Qualify, and no silent promotion of Pi, Sigma, or the candidate product order into architecture; recommends Step 286 be written before Step 287 since invariants should be derived against the ontology actually reconstructed in 286, not the older 8-component model.

rows.anchor: ### Dependency on unresolved D288 decisions Step 285 establishes the semantic projection independently of the unresolved equality procedures. It does **not** establish the decision procedures required to compute or test the relations `≡`, `≈`, or `≅_λ`, nor does it resolve `Qualify`. ... 285 establishes a **relationship** labelled semantic equality; it does not establish its **decision procedure**.
rows.statement: Recommends adding an explicit dependency note connecting Step 285 to D288: Step 285 establishes the semantic-equality relationship independently of the unresolved equality decision procedures, but does not establish those decision procedures for ≡, ≈, or ≅_λ, nor resolve Qualify; Step 287's invariant research may build on Step 285, but equality-dependent invariants must be marked conditional until D288 resolves -- otherwise a future reader could wrongly conclude 'Step 285 established =_semantic as an executable predicate.'

rows.anchor: | **286 · Ontology** | reconstruct the ontology **around the established `K_t → (𝒜,ℛ)` projection**, keeping `K_core` unresolved. ... | **287 · Invariants `𝓘`** | derive and audit `𝓘(K_t)` — **over the ratified `K_t`, not over an unresolved choice.** ... | **D288** | separate closure mechanism for the equality/qualification blockers | scoped, not executed |
rows.statement: Hands explicit, binding mandates and status lines to the three downstream steps: Step 286 must reconstruct the ontology around the established K_t->(A,R) projection while keeping K_core unresolved, carrying the status line 'RESEARCH ARTIFACT — corpus reconstruction; normative promotion explicitly prohibited'; Step 287 must derive and audit the invariant universe I(K_t) over the ratified K_t (not an unresolved choice), tagging every invariant CORPUS/DERIVED/CANDIDATE/NORMATIVE/BLOCKED and testing dependence on ≡/≈/≅_λ/Qualify/Π/Sigma's component orders; D288 remains the separate closure mechanism, scoped not executed. States 286 must come first since 287's invariants should be derived against 286's ontology, and neither is blocked by D288.

rows.statement: Explicit non-closure declaration and Step-288 boundary table: items CLOSED by 287 (four relations exist non-interchangeably; 'history' is not a corpus relation; structural-subset-semantic witnessed strict; D285-5 scoped to a quotient; Sigma-order != K-order; equality independence from the Gita; value-level ≡_D has a procedure), items BOUNDED-but-OPEN (the ≈_X family with X unselected; the conditional Sigma order with 0/5 axes established; ≅_λ's relevance principle without a predicate; ≡ named without a procedure), and items DEFERRED to Step 288+ (decision procedures for ≡ and ≅_λ; the three governance questions; per-axis orders; state/operation/authority-act/event identity; implementation semantics; interaction with delta; behavioural observational equivalence; K-order). rows.anchor: Step 287 is OPEN and deliberately does NOT establish an equality contract. Step 288 is therefore a RESEARCH AND CLOSURE-PROGRAMME STEP, not permission to invent or silently ratify the missing contract.
rows.statement: Frames Step 288 as a research/closure step, not a licence to invent the missing equality contract: it must determine, with maximum precision, which parts of equality/identity can be technically closed, which require governance, and which remain technically open, and must not prematurely declare the equality blocker solved. Mandates reading REFINED-STEP-287.md plus Steps 261, 246, 258, 259, 260, 264, 265, 266, 271 first, then a corpus-wide search over an explicit term list (equality, equivalence, identity, same-as, structural/semantic/observational/provenance-sensitive equality, congruence, quotient, canonicalization, normalization, deduplication, EntityID/KAID/RecordID, operation/event/state/history identity, and the symbols =,≡,≈,≅,≡_D), plus named identity/equality artifacts (Steps 195, 025s, 038, 012, 261, 258, 025i) -- explicitly instructing the agent not to assume the existing Step-288 draft is correct but to audit it.

rows.anchor: Do NOT ask merely: "Which equality should KnowledgeOS use?" ... Identity -> state equality -> semantic equality -> observational relation -> provenance-sensitive relation -> quotient/canonicalization -> operation congruence -> delta semantics -> kernel sufficiency -> canonical kernel selection
rows.statement: Reframes the central research question from a selection question ('which equality should KnowledgeOS use') to a reconstruction question ('what exact equality/identity machinery is established, named-only, technically derivable, normatively chosen, or implementation-open'), requiring a full dependency chain to be reconstructed from Identity through state equality, semantic equality, observational relation, provenance-sensitive relation, quotient/canonicalization, operation congruence, delta semantics, kernel sufficiency, up to canonical kernel selection, with every unestablished arrow marked OPEN/QUALIFY/NORMATIVE/TECHNICALLY OPEN rather than assumed.

rows.anchor: LEVEL DISCIPLINE — MANDATORY ... A relation established at one level MUST NOT be promoted automatically to another level. ... SOURCE LEVEL -> TARGET LEVEL ... VALID / INVALID / CONDITIONAL / UNPROVEN
rows.statement: Mandates an explicit ten-level typing discipline (L-value, L-assertion, L-entity/object, L-state, L-history, L-operation, L-event, L-policy, L-observation, L-provenance, L-system/behaviour) for every equality statement, forbidding automatic promotion of a relation established at one level to another (worked examples given: value-level equality does not establish state-level equality; structural equality on Sigma does not establish structural equality on K; equality of outputs for one input does not establish equality of operations). Every proposed inference must be written as SOURCE LEVEL -> TARGET LEVEL and classified VALID / INVALID / CONDITIONAL / UNPROVEN.
invariants: a relation established at one level must never be automatically promoted to another level

rows.anchor: Investigate identity independently from equality. ... Do not infer an identity model from the existence of an ID field. ... Specifically investigate: id = H(P,e,c,t,Π) ... Do not silently promote it.
rows.statement: Requires identity to be investigated independently of equality, across eleven identity kinds (entity, assertion, state, history, event, operation, authority-act, policy, provenance, record, knowledge-artifact) and twelve questions per kind (what it identifies, stability, immutability, whether version is part of identity, scope, survival under merge/transform/retraction, semantic-vs-referential nature, collision model, canonicalization rule, decision procedure), explicitly forbidding inferring an identity model merely from the existence of an ID field, and requiring the specific construction id=H(P,e,c,t,Pi) to be classified as an established definition, a candidate construction, a hash-based implementation suggestion, or something else, without silent promotion.

rows.anchor: DECISION 3 — Pi in equiv ? ... Analyze BOTH branches ... Do NOT recommend either branch. ... Do NOT call either branch "the architecture".
rows.statement: Mandates a strictly non-recommending, dual-branch analysis of Step 254/287's open Decision 3 (is governance/authority/provenance Pi part of semantic equality), requiring both branches (Pi in equiv, Pi not in equiv) to be traced for their effects on equiv itself, on the provenance-sensitive relation, on D285-5 and D285-6, on deduplication, canonicalization, provenance, replay, contradiction handling, operations, delta, and governance, with the genuinely normative components separated from what follows mathematically once a choice is made.

rows.anchor: Actively try to falsify: 1. There is one universal equality relation. ... 13. Equality closure automatically produces an implementable kernel.
rows.statement: Specifies thirteen required negative results (falsification targets) that Step 288 must actively attempt to disprove: (1) one universal equality relation exists; (2) semantic equality is already fully specified; (3) observational equivalence is already defined at K level; (4) approx_X is the corpus's approx; (5) Sigma-order implies K-order; (6) structural equality is a congruence; (7) a hash identity is semantic identity; (8) same output on a finite sample proves equality; (9) provenance relevance is already an executable predicate; (10) Decision 3 alone closes equality; (11) the 32 projections close observational equivalence; (12) Step 288 can close kernel selection independently of Step 261; (13) equality closure automatically produces an implementable kernel -- each requiring an attempted proof, counterexample/obstruction, verdict, and evidence. (These thirteen are precisely the thirteen items later reported all-falsified in file 06-STEP-288-MATHEMATICAL-AUDITS.md.)

rows.anchor: GOVERNANCE BOUNDARY ... Do NOT make governance decisions. ... Instead produce a normative decision register. For every decision record: DECISION ID / QUESTION / FORMALLY CONSISTENT OPTIONS / TECHNICAL CONSEQUENCES / GOVERNANCE CONSEQUENCES / CURRENT STATUS / AUTHORITY
rows.statement: Explicitly forbids Step 288 from making any governance decision (choosing Pi-in/Pi-out of equiv, a final X, a final approx/cong_lambda/Deduplicate criterion, final operation/equality bindings, final EntityID/KAID/RecordID policy, final K identity semantics, K-order, or kernel state), requiring instead a normative decision register with each entry recording a decision ID, question, formally consistent options, technical and governance consequences, current status, and an assigned authority.

rows.anchor: STEP 288 CLOSURE CRITERION ... If ANY condition fails: equality remains OPEN. Do not force closure. ... The strongest acceptable result is a precisely bounded OPEN problem. The weakest unacceptable result is a premature "CLOSED" created by terminology.
rows.statement: Specifies a twelve-condition closure criterion for Step 288 (every register reconciled; every symbol has one unambiguous level; identity semantics explicit; decision procedures specified; provenance/observational semantics explicit; operation/equality bindings explicit; congruence established; quotient/canonicalization semantics established where required; implementation semantics sufficiently complete; dependency on delta/operation-registry resolved or classified; Step 261 section 261.23 no longer blocking), with equality remaining OPEN if any condition fails; states the strongest acceptable result is a precisely bounded OPEN problem and the weakest unacceptable result is a premature 'CLOSED' created by terminology alone, and explicitly forbids converting 'not established' into 'impossible', 'available' into 'established', or 'candidate' into 'canonical'.

sources.note: A self-declared non-canonical mathematical closure proposal factoring Sat into Eval (assessment) composed with Accept (boolean acceptance depending on r,Gamma,EC), with a weak non-numeric sufficiency relation, an undecided binary-vs-three-valued Sat question, and a SAT-CLOSURE-01 five-condition closure gate; ends with a concrete corpus search list rather than choosing definitions.

rows.anchor: Yes. At this point I would switch roles from historical auditor to mathematical closure reviewer. ... derive only what is forced by the already reconstructed structure. ... we should not introduce arbitrary probability thresholds, weights, confidence scores, or domain-specific acceptance rules. ... Evidence → Assessment → Acceptance → Satisfaction → Gap → Determination
rows.statement: Declares an explicit role/method shift from historical corpus-auditing to mathematical closure review, with a governing constraint to derive only what is forced by already-reconstructed structure and never introduce arbitrary probability thresholds, weights, confidence scores or domain-specific acceptance rules. Proposes a six-layer dependency chain Evidence -> Assessment -> Acceptance -> Satisfaction -> Gap -> Determination as the object to be separated and formalized.

rows.anchor: 1. First principle: do not make Sat do everything ... Eval(K_t,r) → Assessment ... Accept(Assessment,r,Γ,EC) → Sat(K_t,r) ... Sat(K_t,r) = Accept(Eval(K_t,r),r,Γ_t,EC_t) ... This is not a new empirical theory. It is the minimum factorization required to make the existing distinction between evaluation and acceptance mathematically explicit.
rows.statement: Proposes factoring Sat(K_t,r) into two stages -- Eval(K_t,r)->Assessment followed by Accept(Assessment,r,Gamma,EC)->Sat(K_t,r) -- giving Sat(K_t,r)=Accept(Eval(K_t,r),r,Gamma_t,EC_t), explicitly framed as the minimum factorization needed to make an evaluation/acceptance distinction the corpus already implies mathematically explicit, not a new empirical theory.

rows.anchor: 2. Define the epistemic assessment space ... 𝔸 = {Established, Rejected, Conflicted, Unknown} ... Eval_r : 𝕂×ℝ → 𝔸 ... or, more generally, Eval: 𝕂×ℝ×𝔼×Γ×EC → 𝔸 ... I would not yet choose between those two signatures. ... Eval must produce an assessment; Sat should not itself be responsible for discovering the assessment.
rows.statement: Defines an abstract four-valued assessment space A={Established,Rejected,Conflicted,Unknown} and proposes two candidate Eval signatures (a compressed Eval_r:KxR->A versus a fuller Eval:KxRxExGammaxEC->A), explicitly declining to choose between them as an open corpus-typing question. States the governing principle: Eval must produce an assessment; Sat should not itself be responsible for discovering it.

rows.anchor: 3. Define the evidence support relation ... Suff(E,r,Γ,EC) ... a relation, not a numerical score. ... Suff ⊆ 𝔼×ℝ×Γ×EC ... prevents the illegal inference |E|>n ⇒ Suff(E,r) or P(E)>p ⇒ Suff(E,r) because neither is supported by the current corpus.
rows.statement: Introduces a deliberately weak, non-numeric sufficiency relation Suff(E,r,Gamma,EC) subset-of ExRxGammaxEC (or equivalently a boolean-valued function), explicitly designed to block illegitimate inferences from evidence-count or probability thresholds to sufficiency (neither |E|>n nor P(E)>p implies Suff), since neither is supported by the current corpus -- keeping the acceptance standard explicit rather than smuggled in through an invented statistical threshold.

rows.anchor: 4. Separate evidence from its assessment ... Eval(K_t,r)=Established does not mean merely Evidence(r)≠∅. ... evidence existence is not evidence sufficiency. ... Evidence≠Assessment and Assessment≠Acceptance
rows.statement: Argues Eval(K_t,r)=Established must not be conflated with mere evidence existence (Evidence(r)!=empty-set), citing that evidence existence is not evidence sufficiency as already strongly supported by the historical material. Establishes two boxed mathematical boundaries: Evidence != Assessment and Assessment != Acceptance.

rows.anchor: 5. Define the acceptance function ... Accept: 𝔸×ℝ×Γ×EC → 𝔹 where 𝔹={⊤,⊥}. ... We have now defined the architecture of the missing function, not its empirical/content rule. ... unless the corpus establishes that mapping.
rows.statement: Defines the minimal acceptance function Accept:AxRxGammaxEC->B where B={top,bot}, giving Sat(K_t,r)=Accept(Eval(K_t,r),r,Gamma_t,EC_t) as 'the mathematically clean closure point.' Explicitly caveats that this only defines the ARCHITECTURE of the missing function, not its empirical content rule -- specific mappings like Accept(Established,r,Gamma,EC)=top cannot be asserted unless the corpus itself establishes them.

rows.anchor: 6. The four-valued assessment must not automatically become binary satisfaction ... Eval(K,r)=Unknown does not imply Sat(K,r)=0. ... Unknown≠False≠ProbabilityZero. ... Architecture A — binary satisfaction with indeterminacy outside Sat ... Architecture B — three-valued satisfaction Sat: K×R → {⊤,⊥,U}. ... We must not choose yet.
rows.statement: Argues Eval(K,r)=Unknown must NOT automatically imply Sat(K,r)=0, invoking the boxed invariant Unknown != False != ProbabilityZero as already protected by the historical corpus. Presents two undecided candidate architectures for the Eval-to-Sat relation: Architecture A (binary Sat:KxR->{0,1} that is merely PARTIAL/undefined when acceptance isn't determinable) versus Architecture B (three-valued Sat:KxR->{top,bot,U}, noted to already exist as a later historical candidate formulation in the corpus). Explicitly refuses to choose between them, framing this as one of the few remaining genuine open alternatives.

rows.anchor: 7. But Δ_t forces an important question ... Δ_t = {r∈R_t:Sat(K_t,r)=0} ... If Sat becomes three-valued ... Δ_t = {r∈R_t:Sat(K_t,r)=⊥}. Unknown requirements would not enter Δ_t. ... Δ^-_t ... and potentially Δ^?_t ... I would not yet promote Δ^? to theory.
rows.statement: Derives a mathematical consequence of adopting the three-valued Sat architecture: the historical Delta_t={r: Sat(K_t,r)=0} would become Delta_t={r: Sat(K_t,r)=bot}, meaning Unknown-status requirements would NOT enter Delta_t at all. Proposes (but explicitly declines to promote to theory) a resulting distinction between Delta^-_t={r: Sat=bot} and a new Delta^?_t={r: Sat=U}, framing this purely as a mathematical consequence to be tested against the corpus, not yet an accepted construct.

rows.anchor: 8. Responsibility Γ must become an explicit semantic parameter ... Who/what has authority to establish that the acceptance condition has been met? ... Γ(r) = responsibility/authority applicable to r ... without yet choosing whether Γ is a function, a relation, a set of actors, a responsibility matrix, or a governance object. ... Accept(a,r,Γ,EC) rather than merely Accept(a,r).
rows.statement: Reframes Gamma's role: not merely a structural question but a semantic one -- who/what has authority to establish that an acceptance condition has been met. Proposes a minimal role Gamma(r)=responsibility/authority applicable to r, explicitly declining to choose among five candidate representations (function, relation, set of actors, responsibility matrix, governance object). Elevates Accept to take Gamma and EC as explicit arguments (Accept(a,r,Gamma,EC)) since the same evidence may be acceptable under one responsibility regime and insufficient under another.

rows.anchor: 9. standard and acceptance condition ... r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity). ... Standard(r) ... Assessment →[Standard(r) via Γ,EC]→ Acceptance ... does not yet tell us what the standard is mathematically. It only prevents us from conflating 'a standard exists' with 'the standard has been evaluated.'
rows.statement: Distinguishes Standard(r) (the criterion a requirement's assessed state must meet) from Accept(a,r,Gamma,EC) (whether that criterion is actually met), positioning Standard(r) as supplying the criterion that Accept, mediated by Gamma and EC, evaluates against. Explicitly notes this distinction reveals only the ARCHITECTURE, not the mathematical content of the standard, and exists purely to prevent conflating 'a standard exists' with 'the standard has been evaluated.'

rows.anchor: 10. Minimal formal definition of Sat ... Sat(K,r;Γ,EC) = Accept(Eval(K,r;Γ,EC),r,Γ,EC) ... we should not silently change its arity. Instead record: Sat(K,r) ≟ Sat(K,r;Γ,EC) as a closure question
rows.statement: States the smallest currently-permissible formal Sat definition, Sat(K,r;Gamma,EC)=Accept(Eval(K,r;Gamma,EC),r,Gamma,EC), while cautioning against silently changing the historical notation's arity -- Sat(K,r) versus Sat(K,r;Gamma,EC) is recorded as an open closure question (are Gamma and EC explicit arguments, or context already contained in K/r?), explicitly identified as a real mathematical typing question to be resolved, not assumed.

rows.anchor: 11. Determination can now be derived cleanly ... Req_p(EC,Γ) ... 𝐒𝐚𝐭(K,p) = (Sat(K,r))_{r∈Req_p(EC,Γ)} ... Det_r: 𝒜^{Req_p}×EC×Γ → 𝕊_det ... Sat≠Determination because satisfying epistemic requirements is not itself the same semantic object as determining a proposition.
rows.statement: Derives a determination architecture once satisfaction and determination are separated: defines a satisfaction vector Sat(K,p)=(Sat(K,r))_{r in Req_p(EC,Gamma)} over all requirements relevant to a proposition p (exposing determination's input, not yet defining it), then a determination function Det_r: A^Req_p x EC x Gamma -> S_det with S_det={Established,Rejected,Conflicted,Unknown}. Establishes Sat != Determination, consistent with (per this document) the corpus's own separation of extraction/determination and of observation/knowledge/assessment/decision.

rows.anchor: 12. What does 'sufficient' now mean mathematically? ... Sufficient(E,r,Γ,EC) is an acceptance relation whose content must be recovered from the historical corpus. ... Case 1 — explicit criterion exists ... Case 2 — finite operational rules exist ... only if the historical correspondence is demonstrated. ... Case 3 — only qualitative language exists ... Suff is an open primitive. That is not a failure of the mathematical framework. It is the correct mathematical diagnosis.
rows.statement: Frames 'sufficient' as an acceptance relation Sufficient(E,r,Gamma,EC) whose actual content must come from the corpus, not be invented, laying out three mutually exclusive possible historical outcomes: Case 1 an explicit criterion C(E,r,Gamma,EC) exists and the problem is solved by definitional equivalence; Case 2 finite operational evaluators collectively instantiate the criterion, provable only if historical correspondence is demonstrated; Case 3 only qualitative language exists ('sufficient independent support' undefined), in which case the correct mathematical conclusion is that Suff remains an OPEN PRIMITIVE -- explicitly stated not to be a failure of the mathematical framework but the correct diagnosis.

rows.anchor: 13. Statistical closure test ... A valid evaluator must satisfy reproducibility: same admissible inputs → same assessment. No hidden human judgment. No unstated threshold. ... Computability requires determinacy of Eval and semantic closure requires determinacy of Accept.
rows.statement: Imposes a strict reproducibility/determinacy requirement on any valid Eval: identical or equivalent inputs (K,r,Gamma,EC,E) must always produce identical assessments -- no hidden human judgment, unstated threshold, undocumented source preference, implicit probability, or order-dependence permitted. Concludes computability requires determinacy of Eval, and semantic closure requires determinacy of Accept.

rows.anchor: 14. Mathematical closure condition ... The F4 satisfaction layer is closed iff all of the following exist: State, Requirement, Evidence, Evaluation, Acceptance, Satisfaction, Gap. ... K,R,E,Γ,EC → Eval → Accept → Sat → Δ. That is the mathematical backbone we were missing.
rows.statement: States a seven-part sufficient-closure condition for the F4 satisfaction layer: a sufficiently defined state space K, a closed requirement type R, evidence space E, an evaluation function Eval(K,r,E,Gamma,EC)->A, an acceptance function Accept(A,r,Gamma,EC)->B, satisfaction Sat(K,r) determined by those functions, and a gap set Delta(K,R)={r in R: Sat(K,r)=bot} (or the historical binary form). Names the resulting dependency chain K,R,E,Gamma,EC -> Eval -> Accept -> Sat -> Delta 'the mathematical backbone we were missing.'

rows.anchor: 15. Semantic equivalence becomes possible only after this ... Σ_{EC,Γ}(K) = (Sat(K,r))_{r∈R(EC,Γ)} ... K_1 ≡_sem K_2 iff Σ_{EC,Γ}(K_1)=Σ_{EC,Γ}(K_2) ... this is only a mathematically derived candidate, not something I would yet promote to F4 theory. ... ≡_sem remains downstream of Sat closure.
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate semantic-equivalence criterion once Sat is closed: define a contract-relevant semantic signature Sigma_{EC,Gamma}(K)=(Sat(K,r))_{r in R(EC,Gamma)}, with K1 equiv_sem K2 iff their signatures match. Explicitly refuses to promote this to F4 theory, noting the corpus has not closed whether semantic equivalence should be determined by satisfaction, observation, behaviour, traces, or some combination -- concluding equiv_sem remains strictly downstream of Sat closure.

rows.anchor: 16. The most important new insight ... closure dependency graph (Γ, EC → Acceptance standard → Accept ← Requirements ← r ← Eval ← Evidence → Assessment → Sat → Δ → Determination → Semantic behaviour → ≡sem) ... Sat is not the first missing object. The real missing semantic boundary is: Eval + AcceptanceCondition + Accept, with the unresolved identities of r,Γ,EC around it.
rows.statement: Presents a full closure dependency graph linking Gamma/EC through an Acceptance standard to Accept, fed by Requirements/r/Eval/Evidence/Assessment, through Sat -> Delta -> Determination -> Semantic behaviour -> equiv_sem.
